akhfash:4-6.t: He said ﴿فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ﴾ ﴿أَمْراً﴾, and He said ﴿رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾: their accusative is on the basis of "We sent it down as a command and a mercy", as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

akhfash:42-42.t: And He said ﴿إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ ٱللَّهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ﴾: he made it a badal (substitute) for the implied pronoun in ﴿يُنصَرُونَ﴾. If you wish, you make it a mubtadaʾ (subject) and imply its khabar (predicate), meaning "except one on whom Allah has mercy, for (that) will avail him".

akhfash:54-54.t: And He said ﴿وَزَوَّجْنَاهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾: He means — and Allah knows best — "We made them pairs with the ḥūr". Some Arabs say "عين حير".

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿حم﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran ﴿الْمُبِينِ﴾ which makes the lawful distinct from the unlawful.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُبَارَكَةٍ﴾ it is the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr), or the night of the middle of Shaʿbān; on it, it came down from the Mother of the Book, from the seventh heaven to the lowest heaven ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنْذِرِينَ﴾ warning by it.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿فِيهَا﴾ i.e. on the Night of Decree or the night of the middle of Shaʿbān ﴿يُفْرَقُ﴾ is set out in detail ﴿كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ﴾ firmly decided, of provisions, lifespans and other things that will occur in the year until the like of that night.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿أَمْرًا﴾ a setting out ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ﴾ the messengers: Muhammad and those before him.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ compassion for those to whom they are sent ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of their words ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of their deeds.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا﴾ with رَبُّ in the nominative it is a third khabar (predicate), and with it in the genitive [رَبِّ] it is a badal (substitute) for رَبِّكَ ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾ O people of Mecca ﴿مُوقِنِينَ﴾ that He, the Exalted, is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, then be certain that Muhammad is His Messenger.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ﴾ about the Resurrection ﴿يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ mocking you, O Muhammad. So he said: "O Allah, help me against them with seven [years] like the seven of Yūsuf." The Exalted said:

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿فَارْتَقِبْ﴾ for them ﴿يَوْمَ تَأْتِي السَّمَاءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ So the land became barren and hunger grew severe upon them, until, from its severity, they saw something like smoke between the sky and the earth.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿يَغْشَى النَّاسَ﴾ and they said: ﴿هَذَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا اكْشِفْ عَنَّا الْعَذَابَ إِنَّا مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ affirming the truth of Your Prophet. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿أَنَّى لَهُمُ الذِّكْرَى﴾ i.e. faith does not benefit them when the punishment descends ﴿وَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear in his messengership.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّوْا عَنْهُ وَقَالُوا مُعَلَّمٌ﴾ i.e. a human being teaches him the Quran ﴿مَجْنُونٌ﴾

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّا كَاشِفُوا الْعَذَابِ﴾ i.e. the hunger, from you, for a time ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ So He removed it from them ﴿إِنَّكُمْ عَائِدُونَ﴾ to your disbelief; and they did return to it. Mention:

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ الْبَطْشَةَ الْكُبْرَى﴾ it is the Day of Badr ﴿إِنَّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾ from them; and al-baṭsh is seizing with force.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا﴾ We tried ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ along with him ﴿وَجَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ﴾ he is Mūsā, upon him be peace ﴿كَرِيمٌ﴾ in the sight of Allah the Exalted.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. بِأَنْ (that) ﴿أَدُّوا إِلَيَّ﴾ what I call you to of faith, i.e. show your faith by obeying me, O ﴿عِبَادَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ﴾ trustworthy in what I have been sent with.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَأَنْ لَا تَعْلُوا﴾ be overbearing ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ by abandoning obedience to Him ﴿إِنِّي آتِيكُمْ بِسُلْطَانٍ﴾ a proof ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ clear, of my messengership. So they threatened him with stoning, and he said:

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ﴾ with stones.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا لِي﴾ believe me ﴿فَاعْتَزِلُونِ﴾ then leave off harming me. But they did not leave him alone.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنَّ﴾ i.e. بِأَنَّ (that) ﴿هَؤُلَاءِ قَوْمٌ مُجْرِمُونَ﴾ idolaters. So the Exalted said:

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿فَأَسْرِ﴾ with the hamza as a disjunctive hamza (qaṭʿ) and as a connecting one (waṣl) ﴿بِعِبَادِي﴾ the Children of Israel ﴿لَيْلًا إِنَّكُمْ مُتَّبَعُونَ﴾ Pharaoh and his people will follow you.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَاتْرُكِ الْبَحْرَ﴾ when you and your companions have crossed it ﴿رَهْوًا﴾ still, parted, until the Copts enter it ﴿إِنَّهُمْ جُنْدٌ مُغْرَقُونَ﴾ So he was reassured by that, and they were drowned.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَزُرُوعٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ a fine place of assembly.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَنَعْمَةٍ﴾ enjoyment ﴿كَانُوا فِيهَا فَاكِهِينَ﴾ living in comfort.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter [is thus]" ﴿وَأَوْرَثْنَاهَا﴾ i.e. their wealth ﴿قَوْمًا آخَرِينَ﴾ i.e. the Children of Israel.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّمَاءُ وَالْأَرْضُ﴾ unlike the believers, for whom, at their death, their place of prayer on the earth and the place where their deeds ascend in the heaven weep ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا مُنْظَرِينَ﴾ granted respite to repent.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَجَّيْنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ الْمُهِينِ﴾ the killing of the sons and the putting of the women to service.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ It is said: a badal (substitute) for الْعَذَابِ, with an implied muḍāf, i.e. "the punishment of"; and it is said: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْعَذَابِ ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَالِيًا مِنَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَلَقَدِ اخْتَرْنَاهُمْ﴾ i.e. the Children of Israel ﴿عَلَى عِلْمٍ﴾ on Our part, of their state ﴿عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ i.e. the beings of their time, i.e. the rational ones.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُمْ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ مَا فِيهِ بَلَاءٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ a manifest blessing: the splitting of the sea, the manna and the quails, and others.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿لَيَقُولُونَ﴾

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿إِنْ هِيَ﴾ i.e. the death after which there is life is not ﴿إِلَّا مَوْتَتُنَا الْأُولَى﴾ i.e. while they were sperm-drops ﴿وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُنْشَرِينَ﴾ raised alive after the second.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿فَأْتُوا بِآبَائِنَا﴾ alive ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ that we will be raised after our death, i.e. live. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ﴾ he was a prophet or a righteous man ﴿وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ of the nations ﴿أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ﴾ for their disbelief. The meaning: these are not stronger than those, and those were destroyed ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا مُجْرِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَاعِبِينَ﴾ in creating that; a ḥāl (circumstantial).

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿مَا خَلَقْنَاهُمَا﴾ and what is between them ﴿إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ i.e. being in the right in that, so that it may be taken as evidence of Our power, Our Oneness and other things ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ﴾ the Day of Resurrection, on which Allah will judge between His servants ﴿مِيقَاتُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ for the everlasting punishment.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَنْ مَوْلًى﴾ by kinship or friendship, i.e. he will not ward off from him ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ of the punishment ﴿وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ protected from it. And يَوْمَ is a badal (substitute) for يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ اللَّهُ﴾ and they are the believers, for they will intercede for one another by Allah's permission ﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ prevailing in His vengeance on the disbelievers ﴿الرَّحِيمُ﴾ to the believers.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿إِنَّ شَجَرَتَ الزَّقُّومِ﴾ it is among the vilest of the bitter trees in Tihāma; Allah the Exalted makes it grow in Hellfire.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿طَعَامُ الْأَثِيمِ﴾ Abū Jahl and his companions, people of great sin.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿كَالْمُهْلِ﴾ i.e. like the black dregs of oil; a second khabar (predicate) ﴿تَغْلِي فِي الْبُطُونِ﴾ with the upper-dotted letter [tāʾ] it is a third khabar, and with the lower-dotted letter [يَغْلِي] it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْمُهْلِ.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿خُذُوهُ﴾ it will be said to the guards of Hell (al-zabāniya): take the sinner ﴿فَاعْتِلُوهُ﴾ with kasra on the tāʾ and with ḍamma on it: drag him roughly and violently ﴿إِلَى سَوَاءِ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ the middle of the Fire.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿ثُمَّ صُبُّوا فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ مِنْ عَذَابِ الْحَمِيمِ﴾ i.e. of the scalding water from which the punishment never parts, so it is more emphatic than what is in the verse {يُصَبُّ مِنْ فَوْقِ رُؤُوسِهِمُ الْحَمِيمُ}; and it will be said to him:

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿ذُقْ﴾ i.e. the punishment ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْكَرِيمُ﴾ according to your claim and your saying: "There is no one between its two mountains mightier and nobler than I." And it will be said to them:

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا﴾ which you see of the punishment ﴿مَا كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَمْتَرُونَ﴾ you used to doubt it.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقَامٍ﴾ a place of assembly ﴿أَمِينٍ﴾ in which one is secure from fear.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿يَلْبَسُونَ مِنْ سُنْدُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ﴾ i.e. fine silk brocade and thick silk brocade ﴿مُتَقَابِلِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. none of them looks at the back of another's head, because the couches revolve with them.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ "the matter" is implied before it ﴿وَزَوَّجْنَاهُمْ﴾ from marrying, or: We paired them ﴿بِحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾ with fair women with wide, beautiful eyes.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ they ask the servants ﴿فِيهَا﴾ i.e. in the Garden, to bring ﴿بِكُلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ﴾ of it ﴿آمِنِينَ﴾ from its running out and from its harm and from everything feared; a ḥāl (circumstantial).

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الْمَوْتَ إِلَّا الْمَوْتَةَ الْأُولَى﴾ i.e. the one in this world after their life in it. Some of them said: إِلَّا means بَعْدَ (after) ﴿وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ﴾

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿فَضْلًا﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning tafaḍḍulan (as a bounty); accusative by an implied (muqaddar) تَفَضَّلَ ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ﴾ i.e. We made the Quran easy ﴿بِلِسَانِكَ﴾ in your language, so that the Arabs may understand it from you ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ take heed and believe; but they do not believe.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿فَارْتَقِبْ﴾ await their destruction ﴿إِنَّهُمْ مُرْتَقِبُونَ﴾ your destruction; and this was before the command to wage jihad against them came down.

daas-irab:1-10.t: ﴿حم وَالْكِتابِ الْمُبِينِ﴾ the i'rab of its like has already been given; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿أَنْزَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿فِي لَيْلَةٍ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿مُبارَكَةٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿مُنْذِرِينَ﴾ its khabar, and the verbal clause is the khabar of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿يُفْرَقُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb; ﴿كُلُّ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿أَمْرٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿حَكِيمٍ﴾ an adjective of أمر, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿أَمْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb; ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِنا﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of أمرا; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ﴾ kāna, its noun and its khabar, and the verbal clause is the khabar of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb); ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ both attached to رحمة; ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ two khabars of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿رَبِّ﴾ a badal (substitute) for ربك; ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات; ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted verb forming the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional that makes the verb jussive; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿مُوقِنِينَ﴾ its khabar, and the clause كنتم is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); ﴿لا﴾ negative, operating like inna; ﴿إِلهَ﴾ its noun, and its khabar is omitted; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿هُوَ﴾ a badal for the noun of لا; ﴿يُحْيِي﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَيُمِيتُ﴾ conjoined to يحيي; ﴿رَبُّكُمْ﴾ badal; ﴿وَرَبُّ﴾ conjoined; ﴿آبائِكُمُ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ an adjective; ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb); ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿فِي شَكٍّ﴾ both attached to an omitted khabar; ﴿يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is a ḥāl, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿فَارْتَقِبْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; ﴿تَأْتِي﴾ an imperfect verb; ﴿السَّماءُ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿بِدُخانٍ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ an adjective, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:11-18.t: ﴿يَغْشَى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿النَّاسَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of دخان; ﴿هذا عَذابٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ an adjective of عذاب, and the nominal clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf); ﴿رَبَّنَا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), in annexation; ﴿اكْشِفْ﴾ a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿عَنَّا﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause ربنا is the object of an omitted saying; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ its khabar, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); ﴿أَنَّى﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as a fronted khabar; ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ both attached to an omitted second khabar; ﴿الذِّكْرى﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the object of an omitted saying; ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿رَسُولٌ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective of رسول, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿تَوَلَّوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and قالوا is conjoined to تولوا; ﴿مُعَلَّمٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; ﴿مَجْنُونٌ﴾ a second khabar, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كاشِفُوا﴾ its khabar; ﴿الْعَذابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation), and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿إِنَّكُمْ عائِدُونَ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb; ﴿نَبْطِشُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿الْبَطْشَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْكُبْرى﴾ an adjective of البطشة, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾ its khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive, and what is sworn by is omitted, and the lām occurs in the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and قد is a particle of affirmation; ﴿فَتَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position; ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿قَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿وَجاءَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿رَسُولٌ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; ﴿كَرِيمٌ﴾ an adjective of رسول, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿أَنْ﴾ explicative (tafsīriyya); ﴿أَدُّوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is explicative, with no grammatical position; ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿عِبادَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿رَسُولٌ﴾ the khabar of inna; ﴿أَمِينٌ﴾ an adjective, and the nominal clause is causal.

daas-irab:19-25.t: ﴿وَأَنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and أن is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿لا تَعْلُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil (agent); ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿آتِيكُمْ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿بِسُلْطانٍ﴾ both attached to آتيكم; ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿وَإِنِّي﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and inna and its noun; ﴿عُذْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is circumstantial; ﴿بِرَبِّي﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَرَبِّكُمْ﴾ conjoined to بربي; ﴿أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the dropped first-person yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb عذت; ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إن is a conditional that makes the verb jussive; ﴿لَمْ﴾ a particle making the verb jussive; ﴿تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); ﴿لِي﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿فَاعْتَزِلُونِ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the nūn is the nūn of protection, and the dropped first-person yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; ﴿فَدَعا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿رَبَّهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to an implied clause; ﴿أَنَّ هؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ﴾ anna, its noun and its khabar; ﴿مُجْرِمُونَ﴾ an adjective of قوم, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and what follows it is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb دعا; ﴿فَأَسْرِ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition; ﴿بِعِبادِي﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿لَيْلًا﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿إِنَّكُمْ مُتَّبَعُونَ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation; ﴿وَاتْرُكِ الْبَحْرَ﴾ a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; ﴿رَهْواً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ جُنْدٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar; ﴿مُغْرَقُونَ﴾ an adjective of جند, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation; ﴿كَمْ﴾ predicative (khabariyya), in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi; ﴿تَرَكُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿مِنْ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿وَعُيُونٍ﴾ conjoined to جنات.

daas-irab:26-35.t: ﴿وَزُرُوعٍ وَمَقامٍ﴾ both conjoined to جنات; ﴿كَرِيمٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of مقام; ﴿وَنَعْمَةٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to فاكهين; ﴿فاكِهِينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of كانوا, and the verbal clause is an adjective of نعمة; ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿وَأَوْرَثْناها﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿قَوْماً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿آخَرِينَ﴾ an adjective; ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and ما is negative; ﴿بَكَتْ﴾ a past verb; ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿السَّماءُ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿وَالْأَرْضُ﴾ conjoined to السماء, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negative; ﴿كانُوا مُنْظَرِينَ﴾ kāna, its noun and its khabar, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the lām occurs in the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); ﴿نَجَّيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿بَنِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ; ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation), and the clause نجينا is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position, and the discourse is resumptive; ﴿مِنَ الْعَذابِ﴾ both attached to نجينا; ﴿الْمُهِينِ﴾ an adjective; ﴿مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ a badal (substitute) for His words من العذاب; ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كانَ عالِياً﴾ kāna and its khabar, and its noun is latent (mustatir), and the verbal clause is the khabar of inna; ﴿مِنَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾ both attached to an omitted second khabar, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿وَلَقَدِ اخْتَرْناهُمْ﴾ see verse no. 30 of the sura; ﴿عَلى عِلْمٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَآتَيْناهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مِنَ الْآياتِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿ما﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ﴿بَلؤُا﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective of بلاء; ﴿إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿لَيَقُولُونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative; ﴿هِيَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿مَوْتَتُنَا﴾ khabar; ﴿الْأُولى﴾ an adjective, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, ما is negative, operating like ليس; ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ its noun; ﴿بِمُنْشَرِينَ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, as the khabar of ما, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:36-43.t: ﴿فَأْتُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; ﴿بِآبائِنا﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional that makes the verb jussive; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate), and the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿أَهُمْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation expressing disapproval, and ﴿هُمْ﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿قَوْمُ﴾ conjoined to the pronoun; ﴿تُبَّعٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to قوم; ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted verb forming the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; ﴿أَهْلَكْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ its khabar, and the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and ما is negative; ﴿خَلَقْنَا السَّماواتِ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to السموات, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to السموات; ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿لاعِبِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ; ﴿ما﴾ negative; ﴿خَلَقْناهُما﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and lākinna and its noun; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar of lākinna, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl; ﴿إِنَّ يَوْمَ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿الْفَصْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿مِيقاتُهُمْ﴾ its khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis); ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) for يوم الفصل; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يُغْنِي﴾ an imperfect verb; ﴿مَوْلًى﴾ its fāʿil; ﴿عَنْ مَوْلًى﴾ both attached to the verb, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negative; ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception; ﴿مَنْ﴾ excepted by إلا; ﴿رَحِمَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila of من; ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ two khabars, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation; ﴿إِنَّ شَجَرَةَ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿الزَّقُّومِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:44-53.t: ﴿طَعامُ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿الْأَثِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿كَالْمُهْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted second khabar; ﴿يَغْلِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿فِي الْبُطُونِ﴾ both attached to the verb, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿كَغَلْيِ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿الْحَمِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿خُذُوهُ﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf); ﴿فَاعْتِلُوهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِلى سَواءِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿صُبُّوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; ﴿فَوْقَ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿رَأْسِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿مِنْ عَذابِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿الْحَمِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿ذُقْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the object of an omitted saying; ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْعَزِيزُ الْكَرِيمُ﴾ two khabars, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); ﴿إِنَّ هذا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿ما﴾ its khabar; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to تمترون; ﴿تَمْتَرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause إن هذا is the object of an implied saying; ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿فِي مَقامٍ﴾ both attached to the omitted khabar of inna; ﴿أَمِينٍ﴾ an adjective; ﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ﴾ a badal (substitute) for في مقام; ﴿وَعُيُونٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it «[Translator's note: the source text is garbled at this point (the brackets around في جنات and وعيون are corrupted); the reading given here follows the evident intent.]»; ﴿يَلْبَسُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is a second khabar of inna; ﴿مِنْ سُندُسٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of the omitted object; ﴿وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مُتَقابِلِينَ﴾ ḥāl.

daas-irab:54-59.t: ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "الأمر كذلك" (the matter is thus); ﴿وَزَوَّجْناهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is conjoined to the clause يلبسون; ﴿بِحُورٍ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿عِينٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ both attached to the verb as well; ﴿فاكِهَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿آمِنِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿لا يَذُوقُونَ﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿فِيهَا﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿الْمَوْتَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception; ﴿الْمَوْتَةَ﴾ excepted; ﴿الْأُولى﴾ an adjective of الموتة; ﴿وَوَقاهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿عَذابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿فَضْلًا﴾ an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably meaning a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb.]»; ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ both attached to فضلا; ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْفَوْزُ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ an adjective, and the nominal clause ذلك is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿فَإِنَّما﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa); ﴿يَسَّرْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿بِلِسانِكَ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ لعل and its noun; ﴿يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of لعل, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿فَارْتَقِبْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿مُرْتَقِبُونَ﴾ its khabar, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position, and the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:17-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَتَنَّا): "We tried and tested", that is, We dealt with them as one who tests does, wishing to know the reality of a thing. That test consisted in increasing their provision and giving them power in the land, whereupon they became corrupt, persisted in error, and rode the back of misguidance.
(رَهْواً): al-Zamakhsharī said in al-Kashshāf: "There are two views on rahw. The first is that it means 'calm'. al-Aʿshā said:
يمشين رهوا فلا الأعجاز خاذلة ... ولا الصدور على الأعجاز تتكل
(They walk calmly: neither do the hindquarters lag behind, nor do the forequarters lean upon the hindquarters.)
that is, a calm walk, at ease. When Moses crossed the sea he wanted to strike it with his staff so that it would close up, just as he had struck it and it had parted; so he was commanded to leave it calm, at ease, fixed in its state, with the water standing upright and the road dry, neither striking it with his staff nor changing anything of it, so that the Copts might enter it, and when they were inside, Allah would close it over them. The second view is that rahw is a wide gap. It is related of one of the Arabs that he saw a camel with a wide gap between its humps and said: 'Glory be to Allah, a rahw between two humps!', that is, leave it as it is, parted." So in origin it is a verbal noun of rahā yarhū rahwan, like ʿadā yaʿdū ʿadwan, either in the sense of "became calm" or in the sense of "parted and opened up". In al-Mukhtār: "rahā between his legs means he opened them wide, and its class is that of ʿadā; and rahā al-baḥr means the sea became calm, also of the class of ʿadā."
(فاكِهِينَ): "of good cheer", or "possessors of fruit", like "possessor of milk" (labin) and "possessor of dates" (tāmir). This form has already occurred. The wording of al-Qāmūs is: "al-fākiha is all fruit; al-fākihānī is its seller; and in the form fakhiḍ it means one who eats it; al-fākih is its owner; fakkahahum tafkīhan means he gave them a delicacy of it; the noun is al-fukayha, and al-fukāha with ḍamma; and fakiha, like fariḥa, fakahan, so he is fakih or fākih: good of spirit, laughing, or one who talks with his companions and makes them laugh."

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَجاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ): a resumptive sentence, introduced to begin setting forth examples for them from the peoples who came before them. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of certainty; فتنا is a past verb and agent; قبلهم is an adverbial attached to فتنا; قوم فرعون is the direct object. وجاءهم: the wāw is a conjunction; جاءهم is a past verb with a fronted direct object; رسول is the agent; كريم is an adjective.
(أَنْ أَدُّوا إِلَيَّ عِبادَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ): أن may be explicative, because the coming of messengers contains the sense of speech; it may be a maṣdar particle, in which case it with what follows is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to جاءهم; and it may be the lightened form of the heavy أنّ, its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), with the clause أدّوا إليّ as its predicate. عباد الله is a vocative, a genitive construct from which the vocative particle has been omitted, so that "servants of Allah" would mean the Copts. al-Zamakhsharī preferred that عباد الله be a direct object, and that they are the Children of Israel, the meaning being "hand them over to me and send them with me". This is supported by what occurs in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ: «فأتيا فرعون فقولا إنّا رسول رب العالمين أن أرسل معنا بني إسرائيل». إن and its noun; ولكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl; رسول is the predicate of إنّي; أمين is an adjective.
(وَأَنْ لا تَعْلُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ إِنِّي آتِيكُمْ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; وأن is conjoined to the first أن, and the same possibilities apply to it as to the first; لا is prohibitive; تعلو is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, its sign of jussive being the omission of the nūn; على الله is attached to تعلوا; إن and its noun, with the clause آتيكم as its predicate; بسلطان is attached to آتيكم; مبين is an adjective. The clause gives the reason for the prohibition and has no grammatical position.
(وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ): the wāw is a conjunction on بربي; إن and its noun, with the clause عذت as its predicate; بربي is attached to عذت; وربكم is conjoined to بربي; أن and what follows is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to عذت, that is, "from your stoning me"; the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is the direct object of ترجمون.
(وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا لِي فَاعْتَزِلُونِ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; تؤمنوا is the protasis; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; the clause اعتزلون is in the position of jussive as apodosis. The clause is joined with the fāʾ necessarily because it is a request (ṭalab). The yāʾ is likewise not written, because this is one of the "added" verses (āyāt al-zawāʾid).
(فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أَنَّ هؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ مُجْرِمُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to an implied element which al-Jalāl implied by his words "so they did not leave him alone"; دعا ربه is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; أنّ and what follows is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "that these..."; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to دعا; أن with its noun and predicate; مجرمون is an adjective of قوم.
(فَأَسْرِ بِعِبادِي لَيْلًا إِنَّكُمْ مُتَّبَعُونَ): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ faṣīḥa), which occurs as the answer to an implied condition, as if He had said: "If the matter is as you say, then travel by night"; بعبادي is attached to أسر; ليلا is an adverb of time, also attached to أسر; إن with its noun and predicate; the clause gives the reason for the command to travel by night (al-isrāʾ), which is travelling at night.
(وَاتْرُكِ الْبَحْرَ رَهْواً إِنَّهُمْ جُنْدٌ مُغْرَقُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; اترك is an imperative whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; رهوا is a ḥāl or a second direct object of اترك; إن with its noun and predicate; the clause gives the reason for the command to leave it.
(كَمْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ): the speech is linked to an implied element which is indispensable for the coherence of the discourse; the implied form is "so Moses was reassured by that, and their drowning was completed". كم is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, in the position of accusative as a fronted direct object of تركوا; من جنات وعيون is in the position of accusative as ḥāl.
(وَزُرُوعٍ وَمَقامٍ كَرِيمٍ): conjoined to جنات وعيون. By "noble station" (al-maqām al-karīm) are meant their crowded assemblies which they used to hold, and their pleasant gatherings in which they used to congregate.
(وَنَعْمَةٍ كانُوا فِيها فاكِهِينَ): also conjoined; it is an instance of conjoining the general to the particular, because "bounty" (niʿma) does not include everything mentioned before, nor other things not mentioned. The clause كانوا is an adjective of نعمة; فيها is attached to فاكهين; فاكهين is the predicate of كانوا.
(كَذلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْناها قَوْماً آخَرِينَ): كذلك is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, "the matter is thus". al-Zamakhsharī said: "The kāf is accusative, meaning 'in the manner of that expulsion We expelled them from it'", so in his view it is in the position of absolute object. Abu al-Baqāʾ said (it means) "an abandoning like that", making it an adjective of the omitted "abandoning". The wāw is a conjunction; أورثناها is a verb, agent and direct object, the clause being conjoined to كم تركوا; قوما is a second direct object; آخرين is an adjective of قوما.
(فَما بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّماءُ وَالْأَرْضُ وَما كانُوا مُنْظَرِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to the implied clause "they were drowned"; بكت عليهم السماء والأرض is a verb and agent; ما is negative; وكانوا منظرين is kāna with its noun and predicate.

* Rhetoric:
The meaning of "the heaven and the earth wept for them": in His words «فما بكت عليهم السماء والأرض» there is an implicit imaginative metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya takhyīliyya). The heaven and the earth are likened to one of whom concern can properly be expected; then the thing likened to (al-mushabbah bihi), namely the one of whom concern can properly be expected, is omitted, and one of its attributes, weeping, is borrowed for it. The meaning is that they did no righteous deed that would be cut off by their destruction so that the earth would weep for its cessation, nor did any such righteous deed ascend to the heaven so that it would weep after their destruction. Some made it a free metaphor (majāz mursal) for concern at the perishing of the one who perishes, the relation being causal: the effect is mentioned and the cause intended, since that concern is a cause which ordinarily leads to remaining.
Abū Ḥayyān said: «فما بكت عليهم السماء والأرض» is a metaphor expressing contempt for their affair, and that nothing changed at their destruction. In magnification it is said: "the heaven and the earth wept for him", "the wind wept for him", "the sun was darkened for him". Zayd ibn Mufarrigh said:
الريح تبكي شجوها ... والبرق يلمع في غمامه
(The wind weeps for its sorrow, while the lightning flashes in its cloud.)
And Jarir said:
فالشمس طالعة ليست بكاسفة ... تبكي عليك نجوم الليل والقمرا
(The sun is rising, yet it is not eclipsed; the stars of the night and the moon weep for you.)
We cannot avoid taking up Jarir's verse for explanation and parsing, for it has occupied the critics greatly. It belongs to a poem in which he laments ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and before it come:
نعى النعاة أمير المؤمنين لنا ... يا خير من حج بيت الله واعتمرا
(The announcers of death announced to us the Commander of the Faithful: O best of those who made pilgrimage and ʿumra to the House of Allah!)
حملت أمرا عظيما فاضطلعت به ... وقمت فيه بأمر الله يا عمرا
(You bore a great charge and were equal to it, and you carried it out by the command of Allah, O ʿUmar!)
Then: فالشمس طالعة (the verse). His words يا خير are a quotation of the announcers' speech, that is, "saying: O best..."; it is also possible that it is the poet's own speech, in which case it contains an iltifāt (shift of address). al-Naʿy is the proclamation of a death. The "great charge" is the caliphate with its hardships and burdens, which he likens to a tangible load that is carried, by way of the implicit metaphor, the "bearing" being the imaginative element of the metaphor. "The command of Allah" is His law. On this verse there are several opinions. Among them: that it contains a transposition (taqdīm and taʾkhīr), and that نجوم الليل and القمر are accusative by كاسفة and not by تبكي, its arrangement being "the sun is not eclipsing the stars of the night nor the moon; it weeps for you". If it is not eclipsing the other heavenly bodies, it is not shining, so it is black and dark, and all the time is night; and this is the utmost that exaggeration in elegies can reach, and among the finest that has been said in lamentation. طالعة is the predicate of الشمس; وليست بكاسفة is a second predicate; تبكي عليك is a ḥāl or a third predicate; نجوم الليل is the object of كاسفة, that is, the sun does not eclipse the stars of the night, because it has been obliterated and its light is feeble from the abundance of its weeping, so it cannot prevent the stars from appearing. It is also possible that نجوم الليل is the object of تبكي, that is, "she surpasses the stars of the night in weeping for you". It is said that its narration is thus a mistake, and that the narration is "the sun is eclipsed, not rising", that is, it will never rise from then on; the most likely view is that نجوم الليل is the object of تبكي. It is also said to be an adverbial of it, i.e. "for the duration of the stars of the night", etc. And it is said that نجوم is nominative as agent and القمر an object of accompaniment. The accusative of عمر is problematic, because it is a single proper noun and should have been indeclinable on ḍamma. There are several explanations. Among them: that he meant "O ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb" or "O ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz", the addressed genitive construct being accusative, and then he cut off the annexation because the metre ended. Among them: that he meant "yā ʿUmarā" as a lament (nudba) and dropped the final hāʾ, as was said of His words, Exalted: «يا أسفا على يوسف». Other things have been said, on which discussion would be long and unprofitable.

dervis-irab:30-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُبَّعٍ): he is Tubbaʿ al-Ḥimyarī, who marched with armies, built al-Ḥīra and built Samarqand (or, it is said, destroyed it). He was a believer while his people were disbelievers, and for that reason Allah censured them and not him. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: "The apparent sense is that Tubbaʿ is a well-known person, and that a comparison of merit was made between his people and the people of the Messenger, upon him be blessings and peace, although the word tubbaʿ is applied to every one who ruled the Arabs, just as kisrā is applied to whoever ruled the Persians and qayṣar to whoever ruled the Romans. It is said that his name was Asʿad al-Ḥimyarī and that his kunya was Abū Karib. Abu Ḥātim al-Riyāshī mentioned that he believed in the Prophet ﷺ nine hundred years before he was sent. It is related that when he believed, in Medina, he wrote a letter and composed verse. As for the verse, it is:
شهدت على أحمد أنه ... رسول من الله باري النسم
(I bear witness concerning Aḥmad that he is a messenger from Allah, the Creator of souls;)
فلو مدّ عمري إلى عمره ... لكنت وزيرا له وابن عمّ
(and if my life were extended to his lifetime, I would be a minister to him and a cousin.)
As for the letter, Ibn Isḥāq and others related that in it was: 'To proceed: I have believed in you and in your Book which has been sent down to you, and I am upon your religion and your sunna. I have believed in your Lord and the Lord of everything, and in all that has come from your Lord of the laws of Islam. If I reach you, then excellent and blessed; and if I do not reach you, intercede for me and do not forget me on the Day of Resurrection, for I am of your earliest community and I followed you before your coming; I am upon your creed and the creed of your father Abraham, peace be upon him.' Then he sealed the letter and engraved on it 'To Allah belongs the command before and after', and wrote its address: 'To Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah, the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger, the Seal of the Prophets and the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, ﷺ, from Tubbaʿ the First.' It is said that the letter and the verse were with Abū Ayyūb Khālid ibn Zayd and remained with him until the Prophet ﷺ was sent. They used to inherit it, elder from elder, until they handed it to the Prophet ﷺ. A group said that by Tubbaʿ is not meant a single man; what is meant are the kings of Yemen, who were called the Tabābiʿa. al-Jawharī said: 'The Tabābiʿa are the kings of Yemen; and al-tubbaʿ is the shade; and al-tubbaʿ is a kind of bird.' And the wording of al-Zamakhsharī: 'The kings of Yemen were called the Tabābiʿa because they follow (yatbaʿūn), just as they were called the Aqyāl because they take the midday rest (yataqayyalūn).'" And in Mukhtār al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-taqyīl is drinking at midday. The shade is called tubbaʿ because it follows the sun.
Now there were seventy Tubbaʿs among them. al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr al-Anṣārī said: لنا من بني قحطان سبعون تبعا ... أطاعت لنا بالخرج منّا الأعاجم
(Of the sons of Qaḥṭān we have seventy Tubbaʿs; the non-Arabs obeyed us, paying us tribute.)
ومنّا سراة الناس هود وصالح ... وذو الكفل منّا والملوك الأعاظم
(And of us are the noblest of men, Hūd and Ṣāliḥ; and Dhū al-Kifl is of us, and the mighty kings.)
It is also said they were eighty, which the verse did not allow him to say. The details of their reports are scattered through the bellies of the long history books, so let whoever is tempted to read enjoyable legends and their wondrous stories turn to them.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ نَجَّيْنا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ مِنَ الْعَذابِ الْمُهِينِ): a resumptive sentence, introduced to console the Prophet ﷺ for what he was enduring from Quraysh and to cool his heart with the assurance that Allah is able to rescue him and his followers from their harm, as He rescued the Children of Israel from the Copts, a matter which, outwardly, seemed remote from happening.
The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of certainty; نجينا is a verb and agent; بني إسرائيل is the direct object; من العذاب is attached to نجينا; المهين is an adjective of العذاب.
(مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ كانَ عالِياً مِنَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ): من فرعون is a substitute for «من العذاب» with repetition of the preposition, as though he himself were a humiliating torment, because of the torment and humiliation they suffered from him. It is also said that it is attached to an omitted ḥāl of العذاب, that is, "being from, or issuing from, Pharaoh". إن and its noun; the clause كان is its predicate; the noun of كان is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; عاليا is its predicate; من المسرفين is a second predicate of كان. The clause of إن and what follows has no position, because it is explanatory of the reason.
(وَلَقَدِ اخْتَرْناهُمْ عَلى عِلْمٍ عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of certainty; اخترناهم is a verb, agent and direct object; على علم is attached to an omitted ḥāl; على here means "with", that is, "with Our knowledge that they would deviate and commit lapses"; على العالمين is attached to اخترناهم, or (it is so) because of the many prophets among them.
(وَآتَيْناهُمْ مِنَ الْآياتِ ما فِيهِ بَلؤُا مُبِينٌ): conjoined to what precedes; آتيناهم is a verb, agent and object; من الآيات is a fronted ḥāl; ما is a second direct object of آتيناهم; فيه is a fronted predicate; بلاء is a postponed subject; مبين is an adjective of بلاء; and the sentence is the ṣila of the relative.
(إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ لَيَقُولُونَ): إن and its noun; the shifted lām; يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the clause is the predicate of إن. The clause «إن هؤلاء» is resumptive, introduced to speak of Quraysh after the digression about the Children of Israel.
(إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا مَوْتَتُنَا الْأُولى وَما نَحْنُ بِمُنْشَرِينَ): إن is negative; هي is the subject; إلا is a particle of restriction; موتتنا is the predicate of هي; الأولى is an adjective. The meaning of "the first death" will come in the section of Benefits. The wāw is a conjunction; ما is the Hijazi negative; نحن is its noun; بمنشرين: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and منشرين is its predicate, accusative in position and genitive in form.
(فَأْتُوا بِآبائِنا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, that is, "if you are truthful in what you say, then hasten for us the revival of those of our fathers who have died, so that it stands as proof for what you promise of the rising of the Hour and the resurrection of the dead".
(أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ أَهْلَكْناهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا مُجْرِمِينَ): the hamza is of rebuking interrogation; هم is the subject and خير the predicate; أم is a conjunction; قوم تبع is conjoined to هم; الذين is conjoined to قوم تبع; من قبلهم is attached to an omitted ṣila of الذين; the clause أهلكناهم is a ḥāl of the conjoined and the one conjoined to, or resumptive with no position; إن and its noun, with the clause كانوا مجرمين as its predicate. By superiority (khayriyya) is meant excellence in strength and power in this world. The clause «إنهم كانوا مجرمين» is explanatory and has no position, since it gives the reason for their destruction.

* Benefits:
The meaning of "the first death" (al-mawta al-ūlā) is this. When they were promised, after the life of this world, two further states, the first of them death and the other the life of resurrection, they affirmed the first state, which is death, and denied what comes after it. They called it "first" although they believed that nothing comes after it, because they set their denial on the footing of the affirmation, and so made it "first" in accordance with what had been said to them. This is preferable to taking "the first death" as the one preceding the life of this world, for two reasons. The first: they would not believe in restricting themselves to that death, since they affirm the death that follows the life of this world; and to take the direct restriction to death in their speech as referring to an attribute that is mentioned, and not to the death they actually witness, is a departure from the apparent sense without need. The second: the death that precedes the life of this world is not expressed by mawta, for mawta is of the form fiʿla, which suggests renewal and occurrence, whereas the death preceding the life of this world is a continuing state not preceded by a life that it came upon; besides, in the remainder of the sūra is His word, Exalted: «لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى», and what is meant by "the first death" here is only the death that follows the life of this world.

dervis-irab:38-50.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَوْلًى): in al-Mukhtār: "al-mawlā is the freed slave, the cousin, the helper, the neighbour and the ally."
(شَجَرَةَ الزَّقُّومِ): discussion of it has already preceded in Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt; return to it there.
(المهل): a noun that comprises the mineral substances such as silver and iron, and "al-ṣufr" is what of them is molten; also thin tar, thin oil, poison, pus, or specifically the pus of the dead, and the ash that falls from bread. It is with ḍamma on the mīm, and they permitted fatḥa on the mīm because they heard a rare dialect form of it; but al-mahl with fatḥa means deliberateness and gentleness.
(الْحَمِيمِ): water of intense heat.
(فَاعْتِلُوهُ): that is, "lead him with violence and harshness". al-ʿatl is to seize a man by the collar and drag him to prison or to killing; from it comes al-ʿutull, the rough, coarse one. In al-Mukhtār: "ʿatala al-rajul means he pulled him violently, of the class of ḍaraba and naṣara." So their saying al-ʿattāl for one who carries loads for a wage is correct beyond reproach, and the trade is al-ʿitāla.

* I'rab:
(وَما خَلَقْنَا السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما لاعِبِينَ): a resumptive sentence, introduced as proof of the soundness and occurrence of the gathering (al-ḥashr); you may also conjoin it to what precedes so that the discourse is coherent and its two ends meet. ما is negative; خلقنا is a verb and agent; السموات is the direct object; ما is conjoined to السموات والأرض; بينهما is an adverbial attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of ما; لاعبين is a ḥāl of the agent.
(ما خَلَقْناهُما إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the clause explains what precedes it. ما is negative; خلقناهما is a verb, agent and direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction; بالحق is a ḥāl, that is, "acting in truth in that, so that in it there be a proof for the intelligent"; the wāw is circumstantial; لكن is a particle resembling the verb, for rectification; أكثرهم is its noun and the clause لا يعلمون is its predicate.
(إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ مِيقاتُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ): إن and its noun; ميقاتهم is its predicate; أجمعين is emphasis of the pronoun, that is, for all people.
(يَوْمَ لا يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَنْ مَوْلًى شَيْئاً وَلا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ): يوم may be a substitute for «يوم الفصل», and may be an adverbial of what الفصل indicates, that is, "judgment is made between them on the day when ... will not avail"; it is not attached to الفصل itself, since الفصل has already been made a subject of predication. The clause لا يغني is in the position of genitive, the adverbial being annexed to it; مولى is the agent; عن مولى is attached to يغني; شيئا is a direct object or an absolute object, i.e. "a little of it"; the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; هم is the subject and the clause ينصرون is the predicate, the verb being passive and the wāw a deputy agent.
(إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ اللَّهُ): إلا is a particle of restriction; من is in the position of nominative as a substitute for the wāw in ينصرون, that is, "none is shielded from the punishment except him whom Allah has had mercy upon". It may also be accusative as an exception, being then a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ) in the opinion of al-Kisāʾī, that is, "but those upon whom Allah has had mercy will not reach a state in which they need someone among the creatures to benefit them"; or it may be connected (muttaṣil), its implied form being "no relative will avail a relative, except the believers, for they will be permitted to intercede and will intercede for some of them". The clause رحم الله is the ṣila of the relative.
(إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ): إن and its noun; هو is a subject or a detached pronoun of separation; العزيز الرحيم are two predicates of إن or of هو, and the sentence is the predicate of إن.
(إِنَّ شَجَرَةَ الزَّقُّومِ طَعامُ الْأَثِيمِ): إن and its noun; الزقوم is a genitive noun; طعام الأثيم is its predicate.
(كَالْمُهْلِ يَغْلِي فِي الْبُطُونِ كَغَلْيِ الْحَمِيمِ): كالمهل is a second predicate of إن; the clause يغلي is a ḥāl of الزقوم or of طعام الأثيم, and the discussion of a ḥāl coming from the muḍāf ilayhi has already preceded, because it is like a part of the muḍāf; في البطون is attached to يغلي; the kāf and its genitive noun are an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "it boils with a boiling like the boiling of scalding water".
(خُذُوهُ فَاعْتِلُوهُ إِلى سَواءِ الْجَحِيمِ): خذوه is an imperative, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, the wāw its agent and the hāʾ its object; the command is to the guardians of Hell (al-zabāniya), so the sentence is the quotation of an omitted saying; فاعتلوه is conjoined to خذوه; وإلى سواء الجحيم is attached to اعتلوه, that is, "to the middle of Hell".
(ثُمَّ صُبُّوا فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ مِنْ عَذابِ الْحَمِيمِ): ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; صبوا is an imperative and agent; فوق رأسه is an adverbial attached to صبوا; عذاب الجحيم (sic) is the direct object. «[Translator's note: the source writes عذاب الجحيم here, whereas the verse reads «من عذاب الحميم»; the parsing in the source treats the whole phrase as the direct object of صبوا.]»
(ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْكَرِيمُ): the sentence is the quotation of an omitted saying, that is, "and it will be said to him: Taste"; ذق is an imperative whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; إن and its noun; أنت is a subject or a pronoun of separation; العزيز الكريم are two predicates of إن or of أنت; the clause «إنك...» etc. is explanatory, and the secret of this explanation will come in the section of Rhetoric.
(إِنَّ هذا ما كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَمْتَرُونَ): إن and its noun; ما is its predicate; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; به is attached to تمترون; the clause تمترون is the predicate of كنتم.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «ثم صبّوا فوق رأسه من عذاب الحميم» there is an implicit imaginative metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya takhyīliyya): the punishment is likened to a liquid, and then "pouring" is imagined for it.
2- In His words «ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم» there is the art of mockery (tahakkum). It was already stated that this is the bringing of a word of glad tidings in the place of a warning, and of a promise in the place of a threat, out of the speaker's contempt for the one addressed and his derision of him. Examples of it have preceded in their places, such as His word, Exalted, in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: «بشر المنافقين بأن لهم عذابا أليما». It is the most infuriating for the one derided and the most painful to him.

dervis-irab:1-9.t:
* I'rab:
(حم وَالْكِتابِ الْمُبِينِ) The like of this was discussed in Sūrat al-Zukhruf, so renew your acquaintance with it. (إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنْذِرِينَ) إن with its noun; the clause أنزلناه is its predicate (khabar); في ليلة are both attached to أنزلناه; مباركة is an adjective (naʿt) of ليلة; the clause إنّا أنزلناه is the answer to the oath; إنّا is inna with its noun; the clause كنّا is its predicate; كان with its noun; منذرين is its predicate; and the clause إنّا كنّا has no grammatical position, because it is also the answer to the oath without a conjunction, or it is resumptive, or explicative of the answer to the oath. (فِيها يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ)
The sentence is resumptive or an adjective of ليلة. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī on its i'rab is of the highest order. He said: «If you ask: إنّا كنّا منذرين and فيها يفرّق كل أمر حكيم, what is the position of these two sentences? I say: they are two resumptive, interwoven (malfūfatān) sentences by which the answer to the oath is explained, namely His saying the Exalted: إنّا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة, as if it were said: "We sent it down because it is Our way to warn and to caution against punishment, and Our sending it down in this night in particular was because the sending down of the Qur'an is among the wise matters, and this is the night in which every wise matter is distinguished."» فيها are both attached to يفرق; يفرق is a passive imperfect verb; كل أمر is a deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); and حكيم is an adjective of أمر, that is, every wise matter is separated out and written, of the provisions of the servants, their appointed terms and all their affairs. (أَمْراً مِنْ عِنْدِنا إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ) They permitted several aspects for أمرا, and no particular aspect has been found preferable by us for us to decide upon it, so we shall give the wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ, then give the remaining views in the section on benefits. He said: «In its being accusative there are aspects. The first: it is the object of منذرين, like «لينذر بأسا شديدا». The second: it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), the governor in it being أنزلناه or منذرين or يفرق. The third: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in حكيم, or from أمر because it has been described, or from كل, or from the hāʾ in أنزلناه. The fourth: that it is in the position of a maṣdar (verbal noun), that is, "a separation from Us". The fifth: that it is a maṣdar, that is, "We commanded a command", and what the Book comprises of commands indicates that. The sixth: that it is a substitute (badal) for the hāʾ in فأنزلناه.» من عندنا is an adjective of أمر or is attached to يفرق; إن with its noun; and the clause كنّا مرسلين is the predicate of إنّا. (رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ) They permitted five aspects for رحمة, equal in preferability. The first: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), its governor being either أنزلناه, or أمرا, or يفرق, or منذرين. The second: that it is a maṣdar in the accusative by an implied verb, that is, "We showed mercy". The third: that it is an object of مرسلين. The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun of مرسلين, that is, "possessing mercy". The fifth: that it is a substitute for أمرا, in which case what was said above applies. من ربك is an adjective of رحمة or is attached to the very word "mercy"; إن with its noun; هو is a subject or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); and السميع العليم are two predicates of هو or of إنه, and parallels to it have been given earlier. (رَبِّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ) رب السموات والأرض is a substitute for ربك; ما is conjoined to السموات والأرض; the adverbial is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; إن is conditional; كنتم is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); موقنين is the predicate of كنتم; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "so be certain that Muḥammad is His Messenger". (لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) The sentence is also a predicate of إن; ربكم is a fourth predicate or the predicate of an omitted subject; and رب آبائكم الأولين is conjoined to what precedes. (بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ يَلْعَبُونَ) A rectification of an omitted element, as if He had said "so they are not certain; rather they are in doubt, according to their inner selves"; هم is a subject; في شك is the predicate; and the clause يلعبون is a ḥāl.

* Benefits:
1- The Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr): What is meant by the blessed night is the Night of Power. There has been disagreement about it and about the determination of its time, and it was also said to be the night of the middle of Shaʿbān; one can refer to the longer works to learn about it. Muslims in the east and west of the earth look forward to the Night of Power, celebrate it, are eager for it and expose themselves to the abundant good and great reward that gathers in it. The Night of Power is among the religious matters for which the text is sound with a soundness that leaves no doubt or constraint in the believer's breast, even though that secret which called Muslims to honour it was not stated with it. What we think is that the Night of Power was not, and will not be, a door that opens in the sky or a light that fills the space of the house; it is rather the beginning of Allah's all-embracing mercy, which rescued all humanity from the yoke of tyranny and took the perplexed by the hand to paths of clear signposts and noble ends and aims, in which they feel the coolness of reassurance, the ease of tranquillity and the recovery of lost right guidance. Perhaps it is for the sake of these noble meanings in the Night of Power that standing in prayer in it was made a covering for faults and a forgiveness of sins; so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Power out of faith and seeking reward, his past sins are forgiven."
2- The sayings of the i'rab scholars about أمرا: Al-Zamakhsharī said: «أمرا من عندنا is accusative for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ): He made every matter weighty by describing it as wise, then added weightiness to it and gave it grandeur by saying: "I mean by this matter a matter arising from Us, coming from Our presence and as Our knowledge and Our ordering require." It may be meant as the command (al-amr) that is the opposite of prohibition; then it is either put in the place of furqānan, which is the maṣdar of يفرق, since the meaning of amr and furqān is one in that, when something is made firm and written, it has been commanded; or it is a ḥāl from one of the two pronouns in أنزلناه, either from the pronoun of the agent, that is, "We sent it down commanding a command", or from the pronoun of the object, that is, "We sent it down while it is a command from Us about what must be done."»
As for al-Shihāb al-Samīn, he said it has aspects: the first, that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of أنزلناه; the second, that it is a ḥāl from its object, that is, "commanding" or "commanded"; the third, that it is a mafʿūl lahu, its governor being either أنزلناه, or منذرين, or يفرق; the fourth, that it is a maṣdar from the meaning of يفرق, that is, "a separation". There are other sayings that do not go beyond this scope.

dervis-irab:10-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِدُخانٍ) Smoke (dukhān) is well known. Abū ʿUbayda said: dukhān is also drought. Al-Qutabī said: it is called dukhān because of the dryness of the earth from it, until something rises from it like smoke. The regular plural in the small number is adkhina, and in the large number dukhnān, like ghurāb, aghriba and ghirbān. They deviated in pluralising it on the pattern fawāʿil, saying dawākhin, as if it were the plural of dākhina, approximately, just as they deviated in ʿanān, saying ʿawānin. In al-Qāmūs: «And al-dukhān, like ghurāb, jabal and rummān, is dust, and the plural is adkhina, dawākhin and dawākhīn.»

* I'rab:
«[Translator's note: the source prints the heading as «الأعراب» (al-aʿrāb) here, evidently for «الإعراب» (al-iʿrāb, i'rab).]»
(فَارْتَقِبْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِي السَّماءُ بِدُخانٍ مُبِينٍ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent inference (al-faṣīḥa); ارتقب is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; يوم is a direct object of ارتقب; the clause تأتي السماء is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; بدخان are both attached to تأتي; and مبين is an adjective of دخان. Regarding the smoke mentioned there are various views, to be consulted in the longer books of exegesis, and their summary is: it is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection and afflict the believer. (يَغْشَى النَّاسَ هذا عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) The sentence is in the position of the genitive as an adjective (naʿt) of دخان also, that is, it covers them and clothes them; الناس is a direct object; هذا is a subject (mubtadaʾ); عذاب is the predicate (khabar); أليم is an adjective of عذاب; the sentence is the content of an omitted saying; and the clause of saying is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "saying to your Lord". (رَبَّنَا اكْشِفْ عَنَّا الْعَذابَ إِنَّا مُؤْمِنُونَ) The completion of what they say; ربنا is a vocative, a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct); اكشف is an imperative verb of supplication and the agent is latent, its implied form being "You"; عنّا are both attached to اكشف; العذاب is a direct object; إن with its noun; مؤمنون is its predicate; and the sentence is causal for the supplication. (أَنَّى لَهُمُ الذِّكْرى وَقَدْ جاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مُبِينٌ)
أنّى is an interrogative noun meaning كيف ("how"), in the position of the accusative as an adverbial, and it is in the position of the nominative as a fronted predicate; لهم is a ḥāl; and الذكرى is a postponed subject. The interrogative here is taken to be other than literal; rather what is meant is to deem it far-fetched that they could have the reminder, by the indication of His saying «وقد جاءهم رسول مبين ثم تولوا عنه», that is, how will they be reminded and take a lesson and fulfil what they promised of faith when the punishment is removed from them, when there has come to them what is greater and more compelling for the necessity of taking heed than the removal of the smoke, namely what appeared at the hands of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of clear signs and of the miraculous Book and other things? Yet they were not reminded and turned away from him. The wāw is circumstantial; qad is a particle of affirmation; جاءهم رسول is a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; and مبين is an adjective. (ثُمَّ تَوَلَّوْا عَنْهُ وَقالُوا مُعَلَّمٌ مَجْنُونٌ) ثم is a conjunction; تولوا is a verb and an agent; the conjunction is upon an omitted element, that is, "so they were not reminded, then they turned away"; عنه are both attached to تولوا; قالوا is conjoined to تولوا; معلم is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, "he is taught", with a fatḥa on the doubled lām, a passive participle from ʿallama, that is, a non-Arab youth of some of Thaqīf teaches him (the allusion to this was given earlier in Sūrat al-Naḥl); and مجنون is a second predicate. (إِنَّا كاشِفُوا الْعَذابِ قَلِيلًا إِنَّكُمْ عائِدُونَ) إن with its noun; كاشفوا العذاب is its predicate; قليلا is an adverb of time attached to كاشفوا; and إن with its noun, and عائدون is its predicate. (يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ الْبَطْشَةَ الْكُبْرى إِنَّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ) يوم is an adverbial attached to an omitted element indicated by إنّا منتقمون, that is, "We shall take vengeance", and al-Zamakhsharī confined himself to this i'rab. Others permitted that it be a substitute (badal) for يوم تأتي; and it was said that it is accusative by an implied "mention"; and it was said that it is governed by منتقمون, and al-Zamakhsharī rejected this aspect on the ground that inna blocks that. The clause نبطش is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; البطشة is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq); الكبرى is an adjective; and إن with its noun, and منتقمون is its predicate.

dervis-irab:51-59.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السندس): it is the fine kind of brocade (dībāj), and al-istabraq is the coarse kind of it; it is an Arabicized form of the Persian istabr. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is it permissible for a non-Arabic word to occur in the clear Arabic Qur'an? I say: when it is Arabicized it ceases to be non-Arabic, because Arabicization means making it Arabic by modifying it, changing it from its pattern and treating it according to the aspects of i'rab." There is another question raised by the heretic Ibn al-Rāwandī: how did Allah promise the people of Paradise the wearing of istabraq, which is coarse brocade, when with the rich of this world it is a defect and a deficiency? The answer is that the coarse brocade of Paradise is not equal to the coarse brocade of this world, so that it should be faulted, just as the sundus of Paradise, which is the fine brocade, is not equal to the sundus of this world. Abu al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī, in Risālat al-Ghufrān, dealt with Ibn al-Rāwandī at length, in mockery and ridicule.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقامٍ أَمِينٍ): إن and its noun; في مقام is its predicate; أمين is an adjective of مقام.
(فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are a substitute for «في مقام», with repetition of the preposition.
(يَلْبَسُونَ مِنْ سُندُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ مُتَقابِلِينَ): the sentence is either a second predicate of إن or a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun; من سندس is attached to يلبسون; متقابلين is a ḥāl from the pronoun in يلبسون. In this ḥāl is a beautiful description of the gatherings of the people of Paradise: none of them looks at the back of another's neck, since their couches turn round with them.
(كَذلِكَ وَزَوَّجْناهُمْ بِحُورٍ عِينٍ): كذلك is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, "the matter is thus"; this sentence is parenthetical between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined, brought for confirmation. وزوجناهم is conjoined to يلبسون; it is a past verb, agent and direct object; بحور is attached to زوجناهم; عين is an adjective of حور. An unusual description of the ḥūr ʿīn will come in the section of Benefits.
(يَدْعُونَ فِيها بِكُلِّ فاكِهَةٍ آمِنِينَ): the sentence is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in زوجناهم; يدعون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, the wāw its agent; فيها is a ḥāl; بكل is attached to يدعون, that is, "they ask for it to be brought to them"; آمنين is a ḥāl, that is, "not fearing the consequence of eating it".
(لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الْمَوْتَ إِلَّا الْمَوْتَةَ الْأُولى): the sentence is a ḥāl from the pronoun in آمنين; لا is negative; يذوقون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; فيها is a ḥāl; الموت is the direct object; إلا is a particle of exception; الموتة is excepted from الموت as a disconnected exception; الأولى is an adjective. More will be said on the parsing of this exception in the section of Benefits.
(وَوَقاهُمْ عَذابَ الْجَحِيمِ): the wāw is a conjunction; وقاهم is a past verb with a latent agent referring to Allah; عذاب الجحيم is a second direct object.
(فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكَ ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): فضلا is an absolute object of an omitted verb; it is also said to be an object of purpose, but the first is closer, because it is a maṣdar agreeing with its governing verb in meaning, that is, "We bestowed that as a favour"; من ربك is an adjective of فضلا; ذلك is the subject; هو is a pronoun of separation; الفوز is the predicate; العظيم is an adjective of الفوز. It is also possible that هو is a second subject and الفوز its predicate, the sentence being the predicate of the demonstrative.
(فَإِنَّما يَسَّرْناهُ بِلِسانِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; إنما is kāffa and makfūfa (a particle that prevents the governing action of إن). We have made it eloquent because the verse is the summation (fadhlaka, a concluding digest) of the sūra, for it has made explicit something implied. يسرناه is a verb, agent and direct object; بلسانك is attached to يسرناه; لعل and its noun, with the clause يتذكرون as its predicate.
(فَارْتَقِبْ إِنَّهُمْ مُرْتَقِبُونَ): the fāʾ is again the eloquent fāʾ, that is, "if they do not take heed and do not believe in it, then wait"; ارتقب is an imperative whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you", and its object is omitted, its implied form being "their destruction"; the clause «إنهم مرتقبون» is explanatory of the command to wait; إن with its noun and predicate; the object of مرتقبون is also omitted, its implied form being "your destruction".

* Benefits:
1- A problematic exception: al-Shihāb al-Samīn said: "His words «إلا الموتة الأولى» have several aspects. The first is that it is a disconnected exception, i.e. 'but they have already tasted the first death'. The second is that it is connected, and they interpreted it as meaning that the believer at his death in this world is in the position of being in Paradise, because of his seeing what is given him of it or because of his certainty of its bliss. The third is that illā means siwā ('other than'); al-Ṭabarī transmitted this and weakened it; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: its weakening is not sound, rather its being in the sense of siwā is straightforward and consistent. The fourth is that illā means baʿda ('after'); al-Ṭabarī chose it and the majority rejected it, because the coming of illā in the sense of baʿda is not established. al-Zamakhsharī said: If you say, how was the first death, tasted before entering Paradise, excepted from the negated death that is tasted in it? I say: it was intended to say 'they will never taste death in it', so his words «إلا الموتة الأولى» were put in the place of that, because a death that has passed is impossible to taste in the future; so this belongs to the category of suspension upon the impossible, as if it were said: 'If the first death could be tasted in the future, then they would taste it in Paradise.'" I say: what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned and al-Samīn transmitted is built on الموتة being a substitute, according to the method of the substitute in which a substitute from a different genus is permitted. As for the method of the Hijazis, الموتة is accusative as a disconnected exception. The secret of the Tamimi dialect is the construction of the intended negation in a manner that leaves the hearer no hope of affirmation, so they say "there is no one in it except a donkey" in the sense of "if the donkey is among the people, then there is someone in it", thus suspending the affirmation upon something necessarily impossible by means of the negation.
2- The ḥūr ʿīn: We promised you the transmission of an unusual description of the ḥūr ʿīn taken from the noble hadith. Before we cite what we chose of the hadiths on this subject, we say: al-ḥūr is the plural of ḥawrāʾ, which, as in al-Qāmūs and elsewhere, derives from al-ḥawar with fatḥa, which is that the whiteness of the eye is intensely white and its blackness intensely black, its pupil is round, its eyelids are fine, and what surrounds it is white. al-ʿīn is the plural of ʿaynāʾ, like ḥamrāʾ; so ʿīn was originally with ḍamma on the ʿayn, on the pattern of qufl, but it was given kasra so that the yāʾ would be sound; that is, wide-eyed. What follows is the text of the hadith we chose for this description:
"On the authority of ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this verse: «يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا» to its end. He said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, the delegation (wafd) is only riders. The Prophet ﷺ said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, when they come out of their graves they will be met with white she-camels which have wings, upon which are saddles of gold; the straps of their sandals are shining light, and each step of them is as far as the eye can see. They will reach the gate of Paradise, and there will be a ring of red ruby upon plates of gold, and a tree at the gate of Paradise from whose root two springs flow. When they drink from one of them, the freshness of bliss flows into their faces, and when they perform ablution from the other, their hair will never be dishevelled. They will strike the ring with the plate; if only you could hear the ringing of the ring, O ʿAlī! Then it reaches each ḥawrāʾ that her husband has arrived; she is lightened by haste and sends her steward, who opens the door for him, and he says (and if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had not made him know himself, he would fall prostrate before him, from the light and splendour he sees): I am your steward who has been entrusted with your affair.
