He follows him, treading in his footsteps, and comes to his wife; she is lightened by haste and comes out of the tent, embraces him and says: You are my beloved and I am your beloved; I am the contented, so I shall never be angry; I am the blissful, so I shall never be in want; I am the immortal, so I shall never depart. Then he enters a house from its foundation to its roof one hundred thousand cubits, built upon stones of pearl and ruby, in layers of red, layers of green and layers of yellow, no layer resembling its fellow. He comes to the couch, and upon it is a bed, and on the bed seventy mattresses, on each mattress seventy wives, each wife wearing seventy garments, the marrow of her shin visible from beneath the garments. He fulfils his union with them in the span of one night. Beneath them flow running rivers: rivers of water not stagnant, pure, with no turbidity; rivers of purified honey which did not come from the bellies of bees; rivers of wine, a delight to the drinkers, which men did not press with their feet; and rivers of milk whose taste has not changed, which did not come from the bellies of cattle. When they desire food, white birds come to them and raise their wings, and they eat from their sides of whatever colours they wish; then they fly off and go away. And in it are hanging fruits: when they desire them, the branch inclines toward them and they eat of whatever fruits they wish, standing if they wish or reclining if they wish. That is His saying «وجنى الجنتين دان», and before them are servants like pearls." Ibn Abi al-Dunyā related it in the Book of the Description of Paradise, from al-Ḥārith. We content ourselves with this hadith, sufficing with it in place of many hadiths in this sense, which will come in their places, if Allah wills.

farraa:4-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ﴾.
﴿أَمْراً﴾ is accusative by His saying يفرق, in the sense: every affair is distinguished, a distinguishing (farqan) and a command (amran); and likewise.
His saying: ﴿رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾: that is distinguished as a mercy from your Lord. And it is allowed to put الرحمة in the accusative by مرسلين falling upon it, making the mercy the Prophet himself, Allah bless him.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and his companions put it in the genitive, and the people of Medina put it in the nominative. Al-Ḥasan also put it in the genitive, so that it follows ربك: "your Lord, the Lord of the heavens".
Whoever puts it in the nominative makes it follow His saying: ﴿إنهُ هُوَ السَّميعُ العَلِيمُ﴾; and another also put it in the nominative by resumption (istiʾnāf), as He said: "وما بينهُما الرحمنُ".

farraa:10-11.t:
His saying: ﴿تَأْتِي ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُّبِينٍ يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ هَـٰذَا عَذَابٌ﴾.
The Prophet, Allah bless him, had prayed against them, saying: "O Allah, make Your tread heavy upon Muḍar; O Allah, [send on them years] like the years of Joseph." So hunger struck them until they ate bones and carrion, and they would see between themselves and the sky [something like] smoke.
His saying: ﴿يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ هَـٰذَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾.
By it is meant: that is a punishment. And it is said that the people were saying: "This smoke is a punishment."

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّا كَاشِفُو ٱلْعَذَابِ قَلِيلاً إِنَّكُمْ عَآئِدُونَ﴾.
It is said: returning to your shirk; and it is said: returning to the punishment of the Hereafter.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ﴾.
He means: the Day of Badr, and it is the greatest assault.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾.
I.e. honoured with his Lord; and it may be "noble among his people", because he said: no prophet was sent except that he was of the noblest of his people.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿أَنْ أَدُّوۤاْ إِلَيَّ عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
He says: hand them over to me, send them with me; and that is His saying: ﴿أَرْسِلْ مَعِىَ بَنىِ إِسْرَائيلَ﴾.
And it is said: "Render to me [your obedience], O servants of Allah"; in the first interpretation العباد is accusative by أدوا.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿أَن تَرْجُمُونِ﴾.
Al-rajm (stoning) here is killing.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُواْ لِي فَٱعْتَزِلُونِ﴾.
He says: then leave me, neither against me nor for me.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنَّ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ قَوْمٌ﴾.
You give (أنَّ) fatḥa; and had you implied a verb of saying and given it kasra, it would have been correct.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱتْرُكِ ٱلْبَحْرَ رَهْواً﴾.
He says: still. He said: and Abū Tharwān recited to me:
كأنما أهلُ حجر ينظرون مَتى * يَرَونَنى خارجاً طير تَنَادِيد طيرٌ رأَتْ بازياً نَضْخُ الدماءِ به * أو أمةٌ خرجَتْ رهواً إلى عيد
(It is as if the people of Ḥajr, watching for when they will see me coming out, are scattering birds: birds that have seen a falcon spattered with blood, or a slave-girl who went out leisurely (rahwan) to a festival.)

farraa:26-29.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾.
It is said: fine dwellings; and it is said: the pulpits.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū Shuʿayb narrated to me, from Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلأَرْضُ﴾: he said: for the believer, his place of prayer on earth weeps over him, and the place in heaven where his deeds ascend weeps over him.
Al-Farrāʾ said: and so Ḥibbān reported it, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ﴾; and in the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh: "مِنْ عَذَابِ المُهِين".
This is among what is annexed to itself because the two nouns differ, like His saying: ﴿ولَدَارُ الآخِرَةِ خيرٌ﴾, and like His saying: ﴿وذَلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ﴾, which in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh is: "وذلك الدينُ القَيِّمَةُ".

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُم مِّنَ ٱلآيَاتِ مَا فِيهِ بَلاَءٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
He means: clear favours, among them that He saved them from the people of Pharaoh, shaded them with clouds, and sent down to them manna and quails. It is as you say to a man: "My favour (balāʾ) towards you is surely good." And it has been said concerning them that al-balāʾ is punishment; and all is correct.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأْتُواْ بِآبَآئِنَا إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
They address the Prophet, Allah bless him, alone; and it is like His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبىُّ إذا طلَّقتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾. In much of the speech of the Arabs, the Arabs put the action of one in the plural; of that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ أرْجِعونِ﴾.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
He means: for the truth.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَصْلِ مِيقَاتُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.
He means: the first and the last. Had ﴿مِيقَاتُهم﴾ been put in the accusative, it would have been correct, making "the day" an adverb (ṣifa). He said: one of them recited to me:
لو كنت أعلم أنّ آخر عهدكم * يوم الرحيل فعلت ما لم أفعل
(Had I known that my last meeting with you was on the day of departure, I would have done what I did not do.)
So he put يوم الرحيل in the accusative, as an adverb (ṣifa).
«[Translator's note: ṣifa here is al-Farrāʾ's Kufan term for the adverbial (ẓarf), not "adjective".]»

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
For the believers intercede for one another. If you wish, make مَن in the position of the nominative, as though you said: "No one stands except so-and-so"; and if you wish, you make it accusative by exception (istithnāʾ), cut off from the beginning of the speech, meaning: "O Allah, except whom You have had mercy upon."

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿طَعَامُ ٱلأَثِيمِ﴾.
He means: the wicked.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿كَٱلْمُهْلِ تَغْلِي﴾.
Many of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it: "تغلى", and it has been reported from ʿAbd Allāh, and the people of Medina read it likewise; and al-Ḥasan read it "يغلى", making it refer to the food or to the muhl (molten brass). Whoever makes it feminine refers to the feminine of the tree.
Like it is His saying: ﴿أَمَنَةً نُعاساً﴾: تغشى and يغشى; the masculine is for the drowsiness (nuʿās), and the feminine for the security (amana). And like it: ﴿أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَّنِىٍّ تُمْنَى﴾: the feminine is for the nuṭfa (drop), and the masculine from the manī (semen).

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱعْتِلُوهُ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with kasra, and the people of Medina read it: "فاعتلُوه", with ḍamma on the tāʾ.

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْكَرِيمُ﴾.
The readers read it with kasra on the alif. Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: a shaykh narrated to me, from Ḥujr, from Abū Qatāda al-Anṣārī, from his father, who said: I heard al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib say on the pulpit: "ذُقْ أَنك", with fatḥa on the alif. The meaning with fatḥa is: taste, because of this saying which you said in the world. Whoever uses kasra relates his saying. That is because Abū Jahl met the Prophet, Allah bless him; he said: the Prophet, Allah bless him, took hold of him and shook him, then said [to him]: "Woe to you, O Abū Jahl, woe!" And Allah sent it down as the Prophet, Allah bless him, said it. Abū Jahl answered him and said: "[By] Allah, neither you nor your Lord has power over me; I am the most honoured of the people of the valley among his people, and the mightiest of them." So it was revealed as he had said it. He said: so its meaning, as we see it, and Allah knows best, is that it is a rebuke, i.e. [173/b] taste, for you are honoured as you claimed, while you are not so.

farraa:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿فِي مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read it: ﴿مَقامٍ﴾, and the people of Medina read it (فى مُقام), with ḍamma on the mīm.
Al-maqām with fatḥa on the mīm is better in Arabic, because it is the place; and al-muqām is the staying; and all is correct.

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿وَزَوَّجْنَاهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وَأَمْدَدْناهُمْ بِعِيسٍ عِين"; al-ʿaysāʾ is the white one, and al-ḥawrāʾ likewise.

farraa:56-57.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوْتَةَ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾.
Someone may say: how did He except a death in the world that has passed from the death of the Hereafter? This is like His saying: ﴿ولا تَنْكِحُوا ما نَكَحَ آباؤُكم من النِّساءِ إِلاَّ ما قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾: إلا in this place is in the position of سوى (other than), as though He said: do not marry, do not do other than what your fathers did. Likewise His saying: ﴿لا يذُوقون فيها الموتَ﴾: other than the first death. And like it: ﴿خالدِينَ فيها ما دَامتِ السّماوَاتُ والأرضُ إِلا مَا شَاءَ ربُّك﴾, i.e. besides what your Lord has willed for them of addition of immortality beyond the measure of the world. And you say in speech: "You have a thousand with me, except (إلا) what you have through so-and-so", and its meaning is: besides what you have with me through so-and-so. So إلا may be a subtraction from what precedes it or an addition to it. What we have mentioned to you of these verses is an addition to what precedes إلا; and subtraction from what precedes إلا is your saying: "These are a thousand except a hundred", the meaning being: they are a thousand less a hundred.
His saying: ﴿وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ فضلاً﴾.
I.e. He did it as a favour from Him; and it is among what, had it come in the nominative, would have been correct, i.e.: that is a favour from your Lord.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: His saying «والكتاب»: the wāw is a particle of oath and a preposition; «الكتاب» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied (muqaddar) «أقسم» (I swear).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «إنَّا أنزلناه» is the answer to the oath, and the clause «إنَّا كنا» is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «فيها يفرق» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ليلة».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «أمرًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of {أَنْزَلْنَاهُ} in verse (3); the preposition and its genitive noun «من عندنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «أمرًا»; and the clause «إنَّا كنَّا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «رحمة» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of {مُرْسِلِينَ}; the preposition and its genitive noun «من ربك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رحمة»; the clause «إنه هو السميع» is resumptive; «هو» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ in «إنه»; «العليم» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: His saying «رب»: a badal (substitute) from {رَبِّكَ}; «ما» is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الأرض»; «بينهما» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause); the clause «إن كنتم موقنين» is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause of transcendence [«لا إله إلا هو»] is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن» in verse (6); «هو» is a badal (substitute) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar; the clause «يحيي» is a third khabar of «إن»; His saying «ربكم»: a fourth khabar; «الأولين» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «في شك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «هم»; the clause «يلعبون» is a second khabar of «هم»; and the clause «هم في شك» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «يغشى» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «دخان», and the clause «هذا عذاب» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied (muqaddar) saying that is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: saying.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The vocative clause is resumptive within the scope of the implied (muqaddar) saying; the clause «اكشف» is the answer to the vocative, resumptive; and the clause «إنَّا مؤمنون» is resumptive within the scope of the answer to the vocative.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «أنى» is an interrogative noun, an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «الذكرى»; the preposition and its genitive noun «لهم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الذكرى»; the clause «وقد جاءهم رسول» is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «لهم».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «ثم تولَّوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {جَاءَهُمْ}; the verb is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was omitted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; «معلم» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "he"; and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «إنَّا كاشفو» is resumptive; «قليلا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: a little removing; and the clause «إنكم عائدون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «يوم» is a badal (substitute) from {يَوْمَ تَأْتِي} in verse (10), and the clause «إنَّا منتقمون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «ولقد فتنَّا قبلهم» is resumptive; the clause «وجاءهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «قوم فرعون».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «أن» is explicative (mufassira), preceded by something with the meaning of saying; the clause «أدُّوا» is explicative; «عباد» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «أدُّوا»; the clause «إني لكم رسول» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «رسول».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: «أن» is explicative (mufassira), and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the explicative one; the clause «إني آتيكم» is resumptive; His saying «آتيكم» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «وإني عذت» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {إِنِّي آتِيكُمْ}; «أن» makes [the verb] accusative; «ترجمون» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the omission of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the implied (muqaddar) yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition «مِنْ».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «وإن لم تؤمنوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إني عذت».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «فدعا» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar from «أنَّ» and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition (الباء).

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; the clause «أسر» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted saying, i.e.: Allah said to Moses; and the clause «إنكم متبعون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «رهوًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «البحر», and the clause «إنهم جند» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «كم» is the declarative (khabariyya) one, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first; the preposition and its genitive noun «من جنات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كم»; and the clause «تركوا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «كانوا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «نعمة»; the preposition and its genitive noun «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «فاكهين».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: (كذلك وأورثناها) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter is thus, and the clause is parenthetical; the clause «وأورثناها» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {تَرَكُوا}; «قوما» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «فما بكت» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَأَوْرَثْنَاهَا}, and the clause «وما كانوا» is conjoined to the clause «فما بكت».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من فرعون» is a badal (substitute) from the preposition and its genitive noun before it and is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what it is attached to; the clause «إنه كان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «فرعون»; the preposition and its genitive noun «من المسرفين» is attached to a second khabar of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: (ولقد اخترناهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَلَقَدْ نَجَّيْنَا}; the preposition and its genitive noun «على علم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun «نا»; the preposition and its genitive noun «على العالمين» is attached to «اخترناهم».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من الآيات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما»; «ما» is the second object of «آتيناهم»; and the clause «فيه بلاء» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the nominal relative.

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: (إن هؤلاء ليقولون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: (إن هي إلا موتتنا الأولى وما نحن بمنشرين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); «إن» is negative, «إلا» is for restriction, and [then come] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); «ما» is negative, operating like laysa, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in its khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «فَأْتوا» is resumptive within the scope of the preceding saying; the clause «إن كنتم» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The clause «أهم خير» is resumptive; «أم» is the connected (muttaṣila) conjunctive one; «قوم» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «هم»; «والذين» is a noun conjoined to «قوم»; the clause «أهلكناهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of the ṣila (relative clause), the implied form being: and those who were settled before them, destroyed. The clause «إنهم كانوا» is a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «أهلكناهم».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The clause «وما خلقنا» is resumptive; «لاعبين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun «نا».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The clause «ما خلقناهما» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «خلقناهما»; and the clause «ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ما خلقناهما».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: «أجمعين» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the genitive pronoun «هم».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: «يوم» is a badal (substitute) from {يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ}; the clause «لا يغني» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «شيئا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and the clause «ولا هم ينصرون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا يغني».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: «من» is a relative noun, excepted; the clause «إنه هو العزيز» is resumptive; «هو» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ; and «العزيز» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: «كالمهل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second khabar (predicate), and the clause «يغلي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «المهل».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: (كغلي الحميم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf is a noun in the sense of «مثل» (like), a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: a boiling like the boiling [of scalding water].

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The clause «خذوه» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the preposition and its genitive noun «إلى سواء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اعتلوه».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من عذاب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «صبوا».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The clause «ذق» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied (muqaddar) saying; the clause «إنك أنت العزيز» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; «أنت» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «إن هذا ما» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تمترون».

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «في جنات» is a badal (substitute) from the preceding preposition and its genitive noun and is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what it is attached to.

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The clause «يلبسون» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «متقابلين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يلبسون».

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: (كذلك وزوجناهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter is thus, and the clause is parenthetical; the clause «وزوَّجناهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {يَلْبَسُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The clause «يَدْعون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of «زوَّجناهم»; «آمنين» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «يَدْعُون».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The clause «لا يذوقون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) in {يَدْعُونَ}; «الموتة» is excepted; the clause «ووقاهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا يذوقون»; «عذاب» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: «فضلا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: He bestowed a bestowal, and it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); the preposition and its genitive noun «من ربك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «فضلا»; «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: The clause «فإنما يسَّرناه» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «لعلهم يتذكرون».

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: The clause «فارتقب» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «إنهم مرتقبون».

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted, {أمرا من عندنَا}: أمرا is accusative, according to al-Akhfash, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of آمرين ("commanding"). Al-Mubarrad said it is in the position of a maṣdar (verbal noun), as though He said "We sent it down with a sending down". Al-Jarmī said it is a ḥāl from an indefinite noun, namely أمر حكيم; that is good since the indefinite noun has been described, and he allowed هذا رجل مقبلا. Al-Zajjāj said it is a maṣdar, as though He said يُفرق فرقا, so it is in the sense of فرق. It has also been said that يفرق is in the sense of يؤمر ("is commanded"), so it is again a maṣdar governed by what precedes it.

[Translator's note: the source has «امرين», evidently for «آمرين».]

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying {رَحْمَة من رَبك}: al-Akhfash said رحمة is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Farrāʾ said it is the object of مرسلين, making the mercy the Prophet, upon him be peace. Al-Zajjāj said رحمة is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of mercy", with the object of مرسلين omitted. It has also been said that it is a badal (substitute) for أمر; and it has been said that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying {أَنى لَهُم الذكرى}: الذكرى is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أنّى the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:15-15.t:
His saying {قَلِيلا}: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted ẓarf (adverbial), its implied form being "a little removal" or "a little time".

His saying {رب السَّمَاوَات}: whoever put it in the nominative made it a naʿt of السميع, or (nominative) by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); whoever put it in the genitive made it a badal (substitute) for ربك.

[Translator's note: رب السماوات is in āya 7, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {يَوْم نبطش}: يوم is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "remember, O Muhammad, the day We strike".

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {أَن أَدّوا إِلَيّ}: أن is in the accusative position by omission of the preposition, i.e. "with (the message) that: deliver to me"; and عباد الله is accusative, governed by أدّوا. It has also been said that it is a vocative with a muḍāf; if you put عباد in the accusative as a vocative, the object of أدّوا is omitted, i.e. "deliver to me your affair, O servants of Allah".

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying {وَأَن لَا تعلوا}: أن is conjoined to the first أن, in the accusative position.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {أَن ترجمون}: أن is in the accusative position by omission of the preposition, i.e. "from (من) that you stone me", meaning "revile me".

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying {فَدَعَا ربه أَن هَؤُلَاءِ}: أنّ is in the accusative position, governed by دعا. Whoever gave it kasra did so by an implied saying, i.e. "and he said: these…".

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying {واترك الْبَحْر رهوا}: رهوا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of "still", so that they would get into it and not shy away from it; one says عيش راهٍ, i.e. a life that is still and at ease. It has also been said that الرهو is "parted", i.e. leave it as it is, parted, path upon path, so that they get into it.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying {كم تركُوا}: كم is in the accusative position, governed by تركوا.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t:
His saying {كَذَلِك وأورثناها}: the kāf is in the nominative position as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the matter is thus". It has also been said that it is in the accusative position, on the implied form "We do a doing like that to whomever We wish to destroy".

[Translator's note: the source has «تفعل», evidently for «نفعل».]

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying {إِلَّا موتتنا}: موتتنا is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of مَا, because إن is in the sense of مَا; so the implied form is "it is nothing but our first death".

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying {وَالَّذين من قبلهم}: الذين is in the nominative position, conjoined to قوم تبّع, or as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with what follows it as the khabar (predicate); or it is in the accusative position by an implied verb indicated by أهلكناهم.

mekki-muskil:40-40.t: His saying إن يوم الفصل: يوم is the ism (noun) of إنّ, and its khabar (predicate) is ميقاتهم. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ allowed ميقاتَهم to be accusative by إنّ, making يوم الفصل an adverb (ẓarf) for the appointed time, in the position of the khabar of إنّ, i.e. "their appointed time is on the Day of Decision".

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {يَوْم لَا يُغني}: it is a badal (substitute) for the first يوم.

mekki-muskil:42-42.t: His saying {إِلَّا من رحم الله}: من is in the nominative position as a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in ينصرون, its implied form being "none will be helped except whom Allah has shown mercy". It has also been said that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being "except whom Allah has shown mercy: he will be pardoned". It has also been said that it is a badal for the first مولى, the implied form being "the day when none avails except whom Allah has shown mercy", i.e. none will intercede except whom Allah has shown mercy. This is a proof of the permissibility of intercession by believers for sinful believers, by the permission of Allah the Exalted. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said it is in the accusative position as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).

mekki-muskil:49-49.t: His saying {ذُقْ إِنَّك}: whoever read it with kasra on إنّ made it the beginning of a new sentence, meaning: "you used to say this of yourself in the world, and it used to be said to you" — and he is Abū Jahl, may Allah curse him. It has also been said that its meaning with kasra is an ironic allusion to him, meaning: "you are the humiliated and disgraced one now, contrary to what you used to say and what used to be said to you in the world." Whoever gave it fatḥa did so on the implied omission of the prepositional lām, i.e. "because you…" or "for (بأنك) you are the one to whom that used to be said in the world and who used to say it of himself". It is related that he used to say: "I am the mightiest and best-defended of the people of the valley." The kasra indicates that.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {مُتَقَابلين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in يلبسون.

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His saying {كَذَلِك}: the kāf is in the nominative position, i.e. "the matter is thus". It has also been said that it is in the accusative position as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "(He) does to the God-fearing a doing like that".

mekki-muskil:55-55.t: His saying {يدعونَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in زوجناهم; likewise آمنين, and likewise لا يذوقون.

mekki-muskil:56-56.t: His saying {إِلَّا الموتة}: a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It has also been said that إلا is in the sense of بعد ("after"), and it has been said in the sense of سوى ("other than"). The first is better.

mekki-muskil:57-57.t: His saying {فضلا من رَبك}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) governed by يدعون فيها. It has also been said that what governs it is ووقاهم, and it has been said that what governs it is آمنين.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿وآتيناهم من الآيات﴾: conjoined to what precedes. «آتيناهم» is a past verb, «نا» is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the object; «من الآيات» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ما فيه بلاء مبين﴾: «ما» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «آتيناهم»; «فيه» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); «بلاء» is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); «مبين» is an adjective of «بلاء»; and the clause «فيه بلاء» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t: ﴿إن هؤلاء ليقولون﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and «هؤلاء» is its noun; [the lām is] the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «يقولون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the clause «إن هؤلاء...» is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿إن هي إلا موتتنا الأولى﴾: «إن» is negative; «هي» is the mubtadaʾ (subject); «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «موتتنا» is the khabar (predicate) of «هي»; and «الأولى» is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿وما نحن بمنشرين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is the Ḥijāzī negative «ما», which operates like «ليس»; «نحن» is the noun of «ما»; «بمنشرين»: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and «منشرين» is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī «ما», accusative (manṣūb) in position, genitive (majrūr) in form by the bāʾ.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿فأتوا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; «ائتوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿بآبائنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ائتوا».
﴿إن﴾: conditional.
﴿كنتم﴾: a deficient (nāqiṣ) past verb, in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its noun.
﴿صادقين﴾: its khabar (predicate); the apodosis is omitted, i.e.: "then do that."

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿أهم خير﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī); «هم» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and «خير» is the khabar (predicate).
﴿أم قوم تبع والذين من قبلهم أهلكناهم﴾: «أم» is a conjunction; «قوم تبع» is conjoined to «هم»; «الذين» is conjoined to «قوم تبع»; «من قبلهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين», and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. «أهلكناهم» is a past verb, «نا» is the fāʿil (agent), and «هم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «أهلكناهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the conjoined and what it is conjoined to, or it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿إنهم كانوا مجرمين﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «هم» is its noun, and the clause «كانوا مجرمين» is its khabar; «كانوا» is a deficient, abrogating past verb, the wāw is its noun, and «مجرمين» is its khabar; the clause «إنهم كانوا مجرمين» is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position, because it gives the reason for their destruction.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض﴾: the wāw is resumptive. «ما» is negative, and «خلقنا السماوات» is a verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وما بينهما لاعبين﴾: «ما» is conjoined to «السماوات والأرض»; «بينهما» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of «ما», and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. «لاعبين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil. The clause «وما خلقنا السماوات...» is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿ما خلقناهما إلا بالحق﴾: the clause is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from the clause «وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين», with no grammatical position. «ما» is negative; «خلقناهما» is a verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «بالحق» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «لكن» is an abrogating particle of rectification (istidrāk); «أكثرهم» is its noun; «لا» is negative; «يعلمون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause «لا يعلمون» is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:40-40.t: ﴿إن يوم الفصل ميقاتهم أجمعين﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «يوم» is its noun; «الفصل» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «ميقاتهم» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; and «أجمعين» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun, i.e.: for all people.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿يوم لا يغني مولى عن مولى شيئا﴾: «يوم» is a badal (substitute) from «يوم الفصل», or an adverb (ẓarf) for what «الفصل» indicates, i.e.: He will judge between them on a day on which [no patron] will avail. «لا» is negative; «يغني» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); «مولى» is the fāʿil (agent); «عن مولى» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يغني»; «شيئًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: [availing] a little or a lot; and the clause «لا يغني» is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of the adverb to it.
﴿ولا هم ينصرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «لا» is negative; «هم» is the mubtadaʾ (subject); «ينصرون» is an imperfect verb, constructed for one whose agent is not named (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause «ينصرون» is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿إلا من رحم الله﴾: «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «مَن» is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a badal (substitute) from the wāw in «ينصرون», or accusative (manṣūb) as an excepted [noun], i.e.: but those on whom Allah has mercy will not be afflicted by anything for which they would need a created being to benefit them; or the exception is connected (muttaṣil), its implied form being: no relative will avail a relative, except the believers. The clause «رحم الله», a verb and its fāʿil (agent), is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
﴿إنه هو العزيز الرحيم﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun; «هو» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and «العزيز الرحيم» are two khabars (predicates) of «هو», and the clause is the khabar of «إن»; or «هو» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), and «العزيز الرحيم» are two khabars of «إن».

muyesser-irab:43-43.t: ﴿إن شجرة الزقوم﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «شجرة» is its noun; and «الزقوم» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿طعام الأثيم﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) in the previous ayah.
[Translator's note: strictly, «طعام» is the khabar of «إن» in the previous ayah, whose noun is «شجرة»; translated as written.]

muyesser-irab:45-45.t: ﴿كالمهل يغلي في البطون﴾: «كالمهل»: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), a second khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «المهل» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «يغلي» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هو); the clause «يغلي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الزقوم», or from «طعام الأثيم»; and «في البطون» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يغلي».

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿كغلي الحميم﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: it boils with a boiling like the boiling of scalding water; «غلي» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and «الحميم» is muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:47-47.t:
﴿خذوه﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is the speech reported by an omitted verb of saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf).
﴿فاعتلوه﴾: an imperative verb, conjoined to «خذوه».
﴿إلى سواء الجحيم﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اعتلوه».

muyesser-irab:48-48.t:
﴿ثم صبوا﴾: «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «صبوا» is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿فوق رأسه من عذاب الحميم﴾: «فوق رأسه» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «صبوا»; «من» is a connective (ṣila) particle; «عذاب الحميم» is genitive (majrūr) in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:49-49.t: ﴿ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم﴾: the clause is the speech reported by an omitted verb of saying, i.e.: and it will be said to him: "Taste!". «ذق» is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the kāf is its noun; «أنت» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and «العزيز الكريم» are two khabars (predicates) of «أنت», and the nominal clause is the khabar of «إن»; or «أنت» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), and «العزيز الكريم» are two khabars of «إن». The clause «إنك أنت العزيز الكريم» is causal (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:50-50.t: ﴿إن هذا ما كنتم به تمترون﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «هذا» is its noun; «ما» is its khabar (predicate); «كنتم» is a deficient, abrogating past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; «به» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تمترون»; «تمترون» is an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause «تمترون» is the khabar of «كنتم», and the clause «كنتم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:51-51.t: ﴿إن المتقين في مقام أمين﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «المتقين» is its noun; «في مقام» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate); and «أمين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مقام».

muyesser-irab:52-52.t: ﴿في جنات وعيون﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are a badal (substitute) from «في مقام», with the preposition repeated.

muyesser-irab:53-53.t: ﴿يلبسون من سندس وإستبرق متقابلين﴾: the clause is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن». «يلبسون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «من سندس» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يلبسون»; and «متقابلين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يلبسون».

muyesser-irab:54-54.t: ﴿كذلك وزوجناهم بحور عين﴾: «كذلك» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter is thus; this clause is parenthetical between the conjoined and what it is conjoined to, with no grammatical position, brought for affirmation. «زوجناهم» is a past verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object), conjoined to «يلبسون»; «بحور» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «زوجناهم»; and «عين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «حور».

muyesser-irab:55-55.t: ﴿يدعون فيها بكل فاكهة آمنين﴾: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «زوجناهم». «يدعون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «فيها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl; «بكل» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «يدعون»; and «آمنين» is a ḥāl, i.e.: they do not fear any ill consequence of eating it.

muyesser-irab:56-56.t:
﴿لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى﴾: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «آمنين». «لا» is negative; «يذوقون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «فيها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl; «الموت» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «إلا» is a particle of exception; «الموتة» is excepted from «الموت», the exception being disconnected (munqaṭiʿ); and «الأولى» is an adjective.
﴿ووقاهم عذاب الجحيم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «وقاهم» is a past verb, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah; «هم» is the mafʿūl bihi, and «عذاب الجحيم» is a second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:57-57.t:
﴿فضلا﴾: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: He bestowed a bounty — and it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar); or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
﴿من ربك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of «فضلًا».
﴿ذلك﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿هو﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).
﴿الفوز﴾: khabar (predicate).
﴿العظيم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of «الفوز»; or «هو» is a second mubtadaʾ, and «الفوز» is its khabar, and the nominal clause is the khabar of «ذلك».

muyesser-irab:58-58.t:
﴿فإنما يسرناه بلسانك﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; «إنما» is a restraining [particle] and a restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa); «يسرناه» is a past verb, «نا» is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «بلسانك» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يسرناه».
﴿لعلهم يتذكرون﴾: «لعل» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «هم» is its noun; «يتذكرون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause «يتذكرون» is the khabar (predicate) of «لعل».

muyesser-irab:59-59.t: ﴿فارتقب إنهم مرتقبون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; «ارتقب» is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); its object is omitted, its implied form being "their destruction" (هلاكهم). «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «هم» is its noun, and «مرتقبون» is its khabar (predicate); the object of «مرتقبون» is also omitted, its implied form being "your destruction" (هلاكك). The clause «إنهم مرتقبون» is causal (taʿlīliyya), giving the reason for the command to wait.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿حم﴾: the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿والكتاب المبين﴾: the wāw is the wāw of oath; ﴿الكتاب﴾ is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being «أقسم» (I swear); ﴿المبين﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of «الكتاب».

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; ﴿أنزلناه﴾ is a past verb, ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; ﴿في ليلة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزلناه﴾; ﴿مباركة﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ليلة﴾; the clause ﴿إنا أنزلناه﴾ is the answer of the oath (jawāb al-qasam).
﴿إنا كنا منذرين﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; ﴿كنا﴾ is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, ﴿نا﴾ is its noun, and ﴿منذرين﴾ is its khabar; the clause ﴿كنا﴾ is the khabar of «إن». The clause ﴿إنا كنا﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is also an answer of the oath, or because it is resumptive, or because it is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) between the qualifier — namely His words ﴿فيها يفرق كل أمر﴾ — and the qualified ﴿ليلة﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿فيها يفرق كل أمر حكيم﴾: the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position, or a ṣifa (adjective) of ﴿ليلة﴾. ﴿فيها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يفرق﴾; ﴿يفرق﴾ is an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); ﴿كل أمر﴾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿حكيم﴾ is a ṣifa of ﴿أمر﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿أمرا﴾: ﴿أمرا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿أنزلناه﴾ or of its object, i.e. We sent it down commanding, or [it being] commanded; or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), whose governor is either «أنزلناه», or «منذرين», or «يُفْرَق»; or ﴿أمرا﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, the implied form being «أمرنا أمرًا من عندنا» (We commanded a command from Us); or a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq, because it is in the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «يُفْرَق», i.e. a separating; or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿منذرين﴾, the first object being omitted, i.e. warning people of a command.
﴿من عندنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of ﴿أمرا﴾.
﴿إنا كنا مرسلين﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; ﴿كنا﴾ is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; ﴿مرسلين﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿كنا﴾; the clause ﴿كنا مرسلين﴾ is the khabar of «إن».

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿رحمة من ربك﴾: ﴿رحمة﴾ is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the governor of which is either ﴿أنزلناه﴾, or ﴿أمرًا﴾, or ﴿يفرق﴾, or ﴿منذرين﴾; or a maṣdar (verbal noun) made accusative by an implied verb, i.e. «رحمنا رحمة» (We showed mercy); or an object of ﴿مرسلين﴾; or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of ﴿مرسلين﴾, i.e. possessors of mercy; or a badal (substitute) of ﴿أمرًا﴾. ﴿من ربك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of ﴿رحمة﴾, or attached to the word «رحمة» itself.
﴿إنه هو السميع العليم﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun; ﴿هو﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿السميع العليم﴾ are two khabars (predicates) of ﴿هو﴾, and the nominal clause is the khabar of ﴿إن﴾; or ﴿هو﴾ is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and ﴿السميع العليم﴾ are two khabars of ﴿إنه﴾.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t: ﴿رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إن كنتم موقنين﴾: ﴿رب السماوات والأرض﴾ is a badal (substitute) of ﴿ربك﴾; ﴿ما﴾ is conjoined to ﴿السماوات والأرض﴾; ﴿بينهما﴾ is an adverb [attached to] the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ﴿إن﴾ is conditional; ﴿كنتم﴾ is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent) [Translator's note: so in the text; the tāʾ is the noun of «كان», as «كان» takes a noun, not a fāʿil]; ﴿موقنين﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿كنتم﴾; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being «فأيقنوا بأن محمدًا رسوله» (then be certain that Muḥammad is His Messenger).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation.
﴿إله﴾: its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿هو﴾: a badal (substitute) of the position of «لا» and its noun, because their position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); or a badal of the pronoun latent in the omitted khabar (predicate). The clause ﴿لا إله إلا هو﴾ is also a khabar of ﴿إن﴾ in the sixth ayah.
﴿يحيي ويميت ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين﴾: «يحيي»: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ because of heaviness, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). «يميت»: conjoined to «يحيي». ﴿ربكم﴾ is a fourth khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿رب آبائكم الأولين﴾ is conjoined to what preceded.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿بل هم في شك يلعبون﴾: «بل» is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) from an omitted [statement], as though He said: so they are not certain; rather, they are in doubt according to their inner thoughts. ﴿هم﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿في شك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); ﴿يلعبون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿يلعبون﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t: ﴿فارتقب يوم تأتي السماء بدخان مبين﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ); ﴿ارتقب﴾ is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); ﴿يوم﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿ارتقب﴾; ﴿تأتي﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿السماء﴾ is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿تأتي السماء﴾ is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; ﴿بدخان﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تأتي﴾; ﴿مبين﴾ is a ṣifa (adjective) of ﴿دخان﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿يغشى الناس هذا عذاب أليم﴾: the clause is in the position of a genitive, also a ṣifa (adjective) of ﴿دخان﴾; «يغشى» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هو); ﴿الناس﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿هذا﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject), ﴿عذاب﴾ is khabar (predicate), and ﴿أليم﴾ is a ṣifa of ﴿عذاب﴾; the clause is the maqūl (object of speech) of an omitted saying, and the clause of saying is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. saying to your Lord.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿ربنا اكشف عنا العذاب﴾: ﴿ربنا﴾ is an annexed (muḍāf) vocative; ﴿اكشف﴾ is a verb of supplication, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "You" (أنت); ﴿عنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اكشف﴾; ﴿العذاب﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إنا مؤمنون﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿نا﴾ is its noun, and ﴿مؤمنون﴾ is its khabar (predicate); the clause gives the reason for the supplication.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿أنى لهم الذكرى﴾: ﴿أنى﴾ is an interrogative noun in the sense of «كيف» (how), in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿الذكرى﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿وقد جاءهم رسول مبين﴾: ﴿قد﴾ is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿جاءهم﴾ is a past verb, and ﴿هم﴾ is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿رسول﴾ is a postponed fāʿil (agent); ﴿مبين﴾ is a ṣifa (adjective).

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿ثم تولوا عنه وقالوا معلم مجنون﴾: ﴿ثم﴾ is a conjunction; ﴿تولوا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the conjoining is to an omitted [clause], i.e. «فلم يذكروا ثم تولوا» (so they did not take heed, then they turned away); ﴿عنه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تولوا﴾; ﴿قالوا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿تولوا﴾; ﴿معلم﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿مجنون﴾ is a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿إنا كاشفو العذاب قليلا﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿نا﴾ is its noun, and ﴿كاشفو العذاب﴾ is its khabar (predicate); ﴿قليلًا﴾ is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كاشفو﴾.
﴿إنكم عائدون﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle, the kāf is its noun, and ﴿عائدون﴾ is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿يوم نبطش البطشة الكبرى﴾: ﴿يوم﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [verb] indicated by ﴿إنا منتقمون﴾, i.e. We will take vengeance; and it has been said: it is a badal (substitute) of ﴿يوم تأتي﴾; and it has been said: it is accusative by an implied «اذكر» (remember); and it has been said: by ﴿منتقمون﴾. The clause ﴿نبطش﴾ is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿البطشة﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿الكبرى﴾ is a ṣifa (adjective).
﴿إنا منتقمون﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿نا﴾ is its noun, and ﴿منتقمون﴾ is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿ولقد فتنا قبلهم قوم فرعون وجاءهم رسول كريم﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; the lām is [in] the answer of the omitted oath; ﴿قد﴾ is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿فتنا﴾ is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿قبلهم﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فتنا﴾; ﴿قوم فرعون﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وجاءهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿جاءهم﴾ is a past verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi; ﴿رسول﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿كريم﴾ is a ṣifa (adjective).

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿أن أدوا إلي عباد الله﴾: ﴿أن﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), because the coming of the messengers is only with a call, and that includes the sense of saying; ﴿أدوا﴾ is an imperative verb, and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿أدوا﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. «بأن أدوا» (with [the message]: deliver); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جاءهم﴾, and the clause ﴿أدوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdariyya ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿أن﴾ is lightened from the heavy [«أنّ»], its noun being an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause ﴿أدوا﴾ is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of the lightened «أن». ﴿عباد الله﴾ is an annexed (muḍāf) vocative from which the vocative particle has been omitted; and it has been said: ﴿عباد الله﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إني لكم رسول أمين﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its noun; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿رسول﴾ is the khabar of ﴿إني﴾; ﴿أمين﴾ is a ṣifa (adjective).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿وأن لا تعلوا على الله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿أن﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause after it is explicative with no grammatical position. ﴿لا﴾ is prohibitive, and ﴿تعلوا﴾ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn. Or ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. «بأن لا تعلوا» (with [the message]: do not exalt yourselves), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جاءهم﴾. The clause ﴿أدوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdariyya ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position [Translator's note: so in the text, copied from the previous ayah; here the clause meant is «لا تعلوا»]. Or ﴿أن﴾ is lightened from the heavy [«أنّ»], its noun being an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause ﴿لا تعلوا﴾ is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of the lightened ﴿أن﴾. ﴿على الله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تعلوا﴾.
﴿إني آتيكم بسلطان مبين﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its noun; ﴿آتيكم﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative, the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿آتيكم﴾ is the khabar of «إن»; ﴿بسلطان﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿آتيكم﴾; ﴿مبين﴾ is a ṣifa (adjective); the clause gives the reason for the prohibition, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿وإني عذت بربي وربكم أن ترجمون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its noun; ﴿عذت﴾ is a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿عذت﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; ﴿بربي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عذت﴾; ﴿ربكم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿بربي﴾; ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdariyya; ﴿ترجمون﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «أن» and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿عُذت﴾, i.e. «من أن ترجمون» (from your stoning me); the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is the object of «ترجمون».

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿وإن لم تؤمنوا لي فاعتزلون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إن﴾ is conditional; ﴿لم﴾ is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive; ﴿تؤمنوا﴾ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is connective; ﴿اعتزلون﴾ is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿اعتزلون﴾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿فدعا ربه أن هؤلاء قوم مجرمون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the statement is conjoined to an implied [clause], its implied form being «فلم يتركوه» (but they did not leave him alone); ﴿دعا﴾ is a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿ربه﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «هؤلاء» is its noun; ﴿قوم﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; «مجرمون» is a ṣifa (adjective) of ﴿قوم﴾; ﴿أن﴾ together with what it governs is in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. «بأن هؤلاء» (that these…), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿دعا﴾.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿فأسر بعبادي ليلا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ); ﴿بعبادي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أسر﴾; ﴿ليلًا﴾ is an adverb of time, also attached to ﴿أسر﴾.
﴿إنكم متبعون﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the kāf is its noun, and ﴿متبعون﴾ is its khabar (predicate); the clause gives the reason for the command to travel by night.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿واترك البحر رهوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿اترك﴾ is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); «البحر» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿رهوًا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿اترك﴾.
﴿إنهم جند مغرقون﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿هم﴾ is its noun, and ﴿جند﴾ is its khabar (predicate); ﴿مغرقون﴾ is a ṣifa (adjective) of ﴿جند﴾; the clause gives the reason for the command to leave [the sea].

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿كم تركوا من جنات وعيون﴾: the statement is linked to an implied [one], the implied form being «فاطمأن موسى بذلك فتم إغراقهم» (so Mūsā was reassured by that, and their drowning was accomplished); ﴿كم﴾ is predicative (khabariyya), in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿تركوا﴾; ﴿تركوا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿من﴾ is a redundant (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿جنات﴾ is the tamyīz (specification) of ﴿كم﴾, genitive (majrūr) by ﴿من﴾, accusative in position; ﴿عيون﴾ is conjoined to the form of ﴿جنات﴾, genitive.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t: ﴿وزروع ومقام كريم﴾: conjoined to ﴿جنات وعيون﴾; ﴿كريم﴾ is a ṣifa (adjective), genitive (majrūr).

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿ونعمة كانوا فيها فاكهين﴾: also conjoined; ﴿كانوا﴾ is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, and the wāw is its noun; ﴿فيها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فاكهين﴾; ﴿فاكهين﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿كانوا﴾; the clause ﴿كانوا﴾ is a ṣifa (adjective) of ﴿نعمة﴾.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t: ﴿كذلك وأورثناها قوما آخرين﴾: ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun in the sense of «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being «الأمر مثل ذلك» (the matter is like that); ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿أورثناها﴾ is a past verb, ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to ﴿كم تركوا﴾; ﴿قومًا﴾ is a second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿آخرين﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قومًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿فما بكت عليهم السماء والأرض﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the statement is conjoined to the implied clause «أغرقوا» (they were drowned); ﴿بكت﴾ is a past verb; ﴿عليهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بكت﴾; ﴿السماء﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿الأرض﴾ is conjoined to ﴿السماء﴾.
﴿وما كانوا منظرين﴾: ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿كانوا﴾ is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, the wāw is its noun, and ﴿منظرين﴾ is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿ولقد نجينا بني إسرائيل﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; the lām is [in] the answer of the omitted oath; ﴿قد﴾ is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿نجينا﴾ is a past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿بني إسرائيل﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿من العذاب﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نجينا﴾; ﴿المهين﴾ is a ṣifa (adjective) of «العذاب».

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿من فرعون﴾: ﴿من فرعون﴾ is a badal (substitute) of His words ﴿من العذاب﴾, with repetition of the preposition; and it has been said: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of «العذاب», i.e. being, or issuing, from Firʿawn.
﴿إنه كان عاليا من المسرفين﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the hāʾ is its noun, and the clause «كان» is its khabar (predicate); ﴿كان﴾ is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); ﴿عاليًا﴾ is its khabar; ﴿من المسرفين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second khabar of ﴿كان﴾; the clause of ﴿إن﴾ and what follows it has no grammatical position, because it is causal (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿ولقد اخترناهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is [in] the answer of the omitted oath; ﴿قد﴾ is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿اخترناهم﴾ is a past verb, ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿على علم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿على العالمين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿اخترناهم﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-2.t: (حم) (1) (وَالْكِتابِ): genitive (makhfūḍ) by the oath. (الْمُبِينِ) is [part] of its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: (إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ): Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned from the scholars that it is the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr). As for the blessing that is in it, it is the sending down of the Qur'an. Abū al-ʿĀliya said: it is all mercy; no believing servant who does good happens upon it but his past sins are forgiven him. ʿIkrima said: in it are written the pilgrims, the pilgrims to the House of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, so not one of them is left out and not one is added to them. It was called «مباركة» (blessed) because of the permanence of good in it and its continuance; البركة in the language is permanence and continuance.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: That is, in it is the wisdom from the doing of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: (أَمْراً مِنْ عِنْدِنا): there are five views on its accusative. Saʿīd al-Akhfash said: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the sense of "commanding" [Translator's note: the source has «أمرين», apparently for «آمرين»]. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: its accusative is the accusative of maṣdars (verbal nouns), that is: "We sent it down a sending down", and the command comprises the reports. Abū ʿUmar al-Jarmī said: it is a ḥāl from an indefinite [noun], and on this basis he permitted «هذا رجل مقبلا» ("this is a man, coming forward"). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «أمرا» is a maṣdar, the meaning being "in it is distinguished a distinguishing", with «أمرا» in the sense of فرق (distinguishing). The fifth view is that the meaning of «يفرق» is "is commanded and carried out", so it becomes like «هو يدعه تركا» ("he leaves it a leaving").

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: (رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ): there are five views on its accusative. Al-Akhfash said: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Farrāʾ construed it as an object, being accusative by «مرسلين», and made the mercy [refer] to the Prophet ﷺ. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «رحمة» may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); this is the best that has been said about its accusative. It was also said: it is a badal (substitute) of «أمر». The fifth view is that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). (إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): «هو» may be redundant (zāʾid), a separating [pronoun] (fāṣil); it may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with «السميع» its khabar (predicate), and (الْعَلِيمُ) is [part] of its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:7-9.t: (رَبِّ السَّماواتِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of «السميع»; it may also be nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). This is the reading of the Medinans and the Basrans except al-Ḥasan; he and the Kufans read «ربِّ السماوات» [in the genitive; Translator's note: the source's vowelling does not distinguish the two readings] as a badal (substitute), in the sense of "a mercy from your Lord, the Lord of the heavens"; and likewise «ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين» in the nominative and the genitive.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: [The plural] دواخن has been heard from the Arabs as the plural of دخان (smoke). Al-Qutabī [Ibn Qutayba] claimed that nothing came on this [pattern] except دخان and عثان. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is worth nothing according to the skilled grammarians; دواخن is only the plural of داخنة. This is the explicit statement of al-Farrāʾ and of everyone whose knowledge is relied on. Al-Farrāʾ reported: دخنت النار فهي داخنة ("the fire smoked, so it is smoking") when it produces smoke.

nahhas-irab:11-12.t: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: that is, the people who were struck by the drought say: «هذا عذاب أليم» ("This is a painful punishment").

nahhas-irab:13-14.t: (أَنَّى لَهُمُ الذِّكْرى): [الذكرى] is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh's view, and according to the view of others by an implied verb. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: «أنّى» draws in the meaning of «أين» (where) and «كيف» (how), that is: from which direction and in what state; from it is قالَ يا مَرْيَمُ أَنَّى لَكِ هذا [Āl ʿImrān: 37], that is, from which direction and in what state.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: (إِنَّا): its original is إنّنا, and the nūn was dropped for lightness. (كاشِفُوا الْعَذابِ): the original is كاشفون; the nūn was dropped for lightness. Whoever drops the nūn because of the meeting of two quiescent letters puts العذاب in the accusative. (قَلِيلًا) is accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of an adverb (ẓarf) or of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said: [إنكم عائدون means] "you will return to shirk". It was also said: to the punishment of the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t: (يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ) is accusative in the sense of "remember"; it may not be accusative by «منتقمين», because «إنّ» does not allow the like of this. Abū Jaʿfar and Ṭalḥa read (يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ) [i.e. «نَبْطُشُ», with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ], which is a well-known dialectal form; and the reading of Abū Rajāʾ is (يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ) [i.e. «نُبْطِشُ»] with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the ṭāʾ, with the object omitted [Translator's note: the source prints all three forms with the same vowelling]. One says بطش and أبطشه. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said: (وَجاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ): that is, [noble] with his Lord, Majestic and Mighty is He; and he said: he said «كريم», [noble] among his people.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: (أَنْ أَدُّوا إِلَيَّ عِبادَ اللَّهِ): «أن» is in the position of the accusative, the meaning being "with [the message] that" (بأن). You put «عباد الله» in the accusative by the action of the verb falling on them, that is: hand over the servants of Allah [to me], that is, release them from the torment. You may also put عباد الله in the accusative as a vocative in construct, the meaning then being: "that you render to me what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has commanded you, O servants of Allah."

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: (وَأَنْ لا تَعْلُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ) is conjoined to the first «أن». (إِنِّي آتِيكُمْ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ): Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: that is, with a clear, manifest proof that I am a prophet.

nahhas-irab:20-21.t: (وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ): assimilation (idghām) of the dhāl into the tāʾ is permissible because of its closeness to it and because the tāʾ is unvoiced (mahmūsa). (أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, that you revile me. The yāʾ was dropped because it is the head of a verse; and likewise (فَاعْتَزِلُونِ).

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: Whoever says «إنّ هؤلاء» [with kasra], the meaning according to him is: he said, «إنّ هؤلاء».

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: (فَأَسْرِ بِعِبادِي) is from سرى; whoever says أسرى says «فأسْرِ» [Translator's note: the source does not distinguish the two forms here, i.e. «فَاسْرِ» with hamzat al-waṣl versus «فَأَسْرِ»]. (لَيْلًا) is an adverb (ẓarf).

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: (وَاتْرُكِ الْبَحْرَ رَهْواً): [رهوا is accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: one says عيش راه, meaning easy and tranquil; so the meaning of «رهوا» is "still", so that they enter it while it is still and do not flee from it. It was also said: الرهو is that which is parted.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
«كم» in the speech of the Arabs is for multiplicity, and «ربّ» for paucity. Al-Kisāʾī claimed that the origin of «كم» is «كما»: when you say «كم مالك؟» the meaning is "like what thing of number is your wealth?", and the alif was dropped from «ما» just as it is dropped with the genitive particles, as in لِمَ أَذِنْتَ لَهُمْ [al-Tawba: 43]. It was said to him: "Then why did you make the mīm quiescent?" He said: because of frequency of use, as it is made quiescent in poetry; and he recited [metre: al-basīṭ], verse 414:
فلم دفنتم عبيد الله في جدث ... ولم تعجّلتم ولم تروحونا
(So why did you bury ʿUbayd Allāh in a grave, and why did you hasten, and why did you not come to us in the evening?)
Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān mentioned that this view is unsound, and he argued for that from what the Arabs use in answering «كم», because in answer to «كم مالك؟» they say "thirty" and the like. Had it been as he said, the answer would have been with the kāf, because if someone said «كمن أخوك؟» ("Like whom is your brother?"), you would say «كمحمد» ("like Muḥammad"); and if he said «مثل ما مالك؟» ("Like what is your wealth?"), you would say «مثل الثياب» ("like clothes"); and if he said «كأيّ شيء مالك؟» ("Like what thing is your wealth?"), you would say «كمال زيد» ("like Zayd's wealth"). This is not said with «كم», so it is established that it is not «ما» with the kāf of comparison prefixed to it, and that it is like «من» and «ما», used to ask about number; for if you said «أمالك ثلاثون أم أربعون؟» ("Is your wealth thirty or forty?"), it would not cover the meaning of «كم», because [كم] comprises all of that. It is an indeclinable noun, because it contains the meaning of particles. Sībawayh said: so they are as far from resemblance [to the verb] as «كم» and «إذ» are from the fully declinable [nouns].

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: In [the narration of] Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās: the noble station (al-maqām al-karīm) is the fine dwellings. Abū Jaʿfar said: It is well known in the language that the place where one stays is called «مقام كريم». In [the narration of] al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās: the station is the pulpits; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said the same, and it is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar. We have mentioned it with its chain of transmission in Sūrat «al-Shuʿarāʾ».

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: Yaʿqūb ibn al-Sikkīt said: النَّعمة is enjoyment of ease. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: «فكهين» means "delighted"; and from him: «فاكهين» means "rejoicing". Abū ʿUbayd reported from Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī that one says رجل فكه when he is good-humoured and much given to laughter. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that فكه and فاكه have one meaning, as one says حذر and حاذر. As for Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad], he made a subtle distinction between فَعِل and فاعل in the like of this, saying: الحذر is the one in whose nature is caution, and الحاذر is the one who is on guard (prepared). Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a sound, clear view, and what indicates it is that حذر is intransitive according to the grammarians.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: The kāf [in كذلك] is in the position of the nominative, that is: the matter is that; it may also be in the position of the accusative, in the sense: thus He does with those He destroys and takes vengeance upon.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: (فَما بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّماءُ وَالْأَرْضُ): most exegetes hold that it is literal, and that over the believer weep the place of his prayer on earth and the place of his ascent in heaven. It was also said: it is figurative, the meaning being: neither the people of heaven nor the people of earth wept over them. A third view: it is analogous to the Arabs' saying «ما بكاه شيء» ("nothing wept over him"). «بكت» came [feminine] according to the femininity of السماء; al-Farrāʾ claimed that some Arabs make it masculine.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: [المهين is] a naʿt (adjective) of العذاب. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is (مِنَ الْعَذابِ الْمُهِينِ) [Translator's note: so in the source; from what follows, the reading meant is the genitive construct «من عذاب المهين»], and he took it as the annexation of a thing to itself, like وَذلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ [al-Bayyina: 5]. Abū Jaʿfar said: The annexation of a thing to itself is impossible according to the Basrans, and the reading contradicts the main body [of the codices]. Were it sound, its implied form would be "from the punishment of the humiliating Pharaoh", then the adjective was put in the place of what it qualifies, and there would be a proof of the omission.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: he said: [i.e. «من المسرفين»] "of the idolaters"; and from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: he said: "of the murderous".

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: (وَلَقَدِ اخْتَرْناهُمْ): the pronoun refers back to the Children of Israel, that is, We chose them for messengership and honour. (عَلى عِلْمٍ): because whomever We chose among them for messengership would carry out its delivery. (عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ): because of the multitude of messengers among them. It was also said: the world of the people of their time.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: The soundest thing said about it is that البلاء here is blessing, as in «وجميل بلائه لديك» ("and His fine favour towards you"). Al-Farrāʾ said: البلاء here may also be punishment.

nahhas-irab:34-39.t:
(ما خَلَقْناهُما إِلاَّ بِالْحَقِّ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) (39)
(إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ لَيَقُولُونَ إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا مَوْتَتُنَا الْأُولى): that is, they say this out of habit, without proof, when the evidences had been made clear to them and the proofs had appeared to them. For this reason no argument was made against them here; rather they were made to fear and were threatened, and it was said: (أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ), that is, they knew that those were mightier than them. (وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ) is conjoined to «قوم»; it may also be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with what follows it as its khabar (predicate); and it may be in the position of the accusative by an implied verb indicated by «أهلكناهم». (إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا مُجْرِمِينَ).

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted (إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ مِيقاتُهُمْ) with the accusative [i.e. «ميقاتَهم»]. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: then يوم would be accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), the implied form being "that their appointed time is on the Day of Decision". Abū Jaʿfar said: inna and its noun may be separated by an adverb, so you say «إنّ حذاءك زيدا» ("Facing you is Zayd") and «إنّ اليوم القتال» ("Today is the fighting"), because the adverb carries its meaning in the speech even if you do not pronounce it; there is no disagreement among the grammarians about this. They disagreed about the ḥāl (circumstantial): al-Akhfash permitted putting it first, and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] forbade it. Al-Akhfash permitted «إنّ قائمين فيها إخوتك», putting قائمين in the accusative as a ḥāl. «أجمعين» is in the position of the genitive as tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ and mīm.

nahhas-irab:41-42.t: (يَوْمَ لا يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَنْ مَوْلًى شَيْئاً): you put يوم in the accusative as a badal (substitute) of the first يوم. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: (مَوْلًى عَنْ مَوْلًى): that is, [a protector] for a friend. (إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ اللَّهُ): there are four ways of parsing «من». Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: «من» is in the position of the nominative as a badal, its implied sense being "and none will be helped except whom Allah has mercy on". It may also be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: "except whom Allah has mercy on, for he will be pardoned". Others said: «من» is in the position of the nominative in the sense "none will avail except whom Allah has mercy on", that is, none will intercede except whom Allah has mercy on. This is a good view, because it is authentically established from the Prophet ﷺ that he will intercede for his community until whoever has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith is brought out of the Fire, and it is authentically established from him that the believers will intercede. The fourth view about «من» is that it is in the position of the accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); this is the view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ.

nahhas-irab:43-44.t: From Abū al-Dardāʾ: he said: «طعام الفاجر» ("the food of the wicked"). This is an exegesis, not a reading, because it contradicts the codex.
