nahhas-irab:45-46.t: «كالمهل تغلي في البطون» is the reading of the people of Medina, the people of Kufa and the people of Basra; the reading of Ibn Kathīr is (كَالْمُهْلِ يَغْلِي), and it is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. It contradicts the proof of the community of the people of the cities. The meaning in it is also far-fetched according to Abū ʿUbayd's interpretation, because he made «يغلي» [refer] to المهل, since it is nearer to it; but it is not المهل that boils in the bellies; المهل only boils in cauldrons, as is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he took silver from the treasury, melted it, then sent for the people of the mosque and said: "This is المهل." And from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: المهل is the dregs of oil. Abū Jaʿfar said: except that dregs of oil can only be said to boil with that [interpretation], according to the apparent sense of the verse [Translator's note: the sentence is obscure in the source and is translated as literally as possible].

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: (خُذُوهُ فَاعْتُلُوهُ) is the reading of the people of Medina, and the people of Kufa read (فَاعْتِلُوهُ) [with kasra on the tāʾ]. They are two dialectal forms, except that analogy requires the kasra, because it is like ضربه يضربه. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh permitted «خذوهو فاعتلوهو», keeping the wāw in continuous speech, except that the preferred choice is to drop it. The grammarians disagreed about that: the position of Sībawayh is that the original is «خذوهو» with the wāw retained, but it was dropped because two letters of prolongation and softness came together; the position of others is that it was dropped because of the two quiescent letters. Juwaybir said, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: it was revealed about Abū Jahl: «خذوه فاعتلوه», when he is ordered [to the Fire] on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: (فَاعْتِلُوهُ) means "push him", (إِلى سَواءِ الْجَحِيمِ), that is, to the middle of Hellfire.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: الحميم is the hot [water] whose heat has reached its extreme.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: «إن» has a kasra because it begins [a new sentence]; whoever reads (ذُقْ إِنَّكَ) [i.e. «أَنَّكَ» with fatḥa] takes it in the sense of "because you" or "for that you". The reading with kasra has the proof of the community behind it; moreover, [their] disbelief is greater than his saying "I am the mighty, the noble", because the interpretation of whoever reads it with fatḥa is: "Taste, because you used to say: I am the mighty, the noble."

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: It was said: by this He indicated that they are punished for doubt. It was also said: rather, along with their doubt they denied what they doubted. And whoever doubts something and denies it is disobedient to Allah the Exalted.

nahhas-irab:51-53.t:
[«في مَقام» with fatḥa is] the reading of the Kufans and Abū ʿAmr; the Medinans read (فِي مَقامٍ) [i.e. «مُقام»] with ḍamma on the mīm. Al-Farrāʾ said: مَقام is better in Arabic because it is for the place. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is something for which al-Farrāʾ is reproached: that it be said of readings that the community has transmitted from the community, "this is better than this"; because when the community transmits them from the community, it is said: thus it was revealed, since they do not agree upon error; so how can one of them be better than the other? مُقام with ḍamma has a sound meaning: it may mean "staying" (al-iqāma), as [the poet] said [metre: al-kāmil], verse 415:
عفت الدّيار محلّها فمقامها
(The abodes are effaced, their place of halting and their place of staying.)
مُقام is also the place, if you take it from أقام; and مَقام with fatḥa is also the place, if you take it from قام. (أَمِينٍ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: they are secure in it from hunger, sickness, old age and death, and secure from being expelled from it. Mujāhid said: عَلى سُرُرٍ مُتَقابِلِينَ [al-Ṣāffāt: 44]: none of them sees the back of another's head.

nahhas-irab:54-55.t: (كَذلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the nominative, that is: the matter is thus; it may also be in the position of the accusative, that is: thus [Allah] does with the God-fearing. (وَزَوَّجْناهُمْ بِحُورٍ عِينٍ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الحور are the white ones, and العين those with large eyes. Al-Akhfash said: some Arabs say «بحير عين». Abū Jaʿfar said: this is by making the first follow the second (itbāʿ); its counterpart is [the wording of] whoever narrated «ارجعن مأزورات غير مأجورات» ("Go back burdened with sin, unrewarded"), whereas the clear, eloquent [form] is «ارجعن موزورات» and «بحور». As for «عين», it is the plural of عيناء; it is [on the pattern] فُعْل, whose first radical was given a kasra because a yāʾ follows it.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: (لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الْمَوْتَ إِلَّا الْمَوْتَةَ الْأُولى): [الموتة] is accusative because it is an exception not of the same kind as the first.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
(فَضْلًا) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and what governs it is the meaning; there is disagreement about that meaning. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said about it that it is (يَدْعُونَ فِيها بِكُلِّ فاكِهَةٍ آمِنِينَ); he said: what governs it may also be (إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقامٍ أَمِينٍ). Others said: what governs it is (وَوَقاهُمْ عَذابَ الْجَحِيمِ). A fourth answer: all of this governs it, because its meaning, all of it, is a favour from Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.
All of this needs explanation. That is, it may be said: He, Majestic and Mighty is He, has said بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ [al-Anʿām: 127, and Yūsuf: 12 — Translator's note: so cited in the source] and بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ [al-Anʿām: 129], so what is the meaning of favour here? There is more than one answer to this. Among them: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, did not impose deeds out of any need of His for them; He imposed that on them only so that they would act and so enter Paradise; so the imposition and their admission into Paradise are a favour from Him, Majestic and Mighty is He. The soundest of the answers in this is that the believers have sins from which they are not free, even if for many of them they are minor; had Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, taken them to account for them, He would have punished them without wronging them; so when He forgave them and admitted them into Paradise, that was a favour from Him, Majestic and Mighty is He. Moreover, Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has blessings upon all His servants in this world; were their deeds set against those blessings, [the blessings] would consume them; so their entry into Paradise has become a favour, as he ﷺ said: «No one enters Paradise by his deeds.» It was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: «Not even I, unless Allah covers me with mercy from Him.»

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: (فَإِنَّما يَسَّرْناهُ بِلِسانِكَ): it was said: the meaning of يسّرناه is "We taught it to you, made you memorise it, and revealed it to you, so that you may be reminded by it and take heed".

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: (فَارْتَقِبْ): that is, wait for Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, to judge between you and them. (إِنَّهُمْ مُرْتَقِبُونَ): there are two views on it. One of them is that it is figurative, the meaning being that they are in the position of those waiting, because the matter will inevitably befall them. It was also said: it is literal, that is, they are waiting for what they hope for.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا خَلَقْنَاهُمَآ إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
﴿إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾ means: except for the establishing of the truth.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ لاَ يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَن مَّوْلًى شَيْئاً وَلاَ هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ﴾.
al-Mawlā: the ally (al-walī) and the helper, as the poet said:
فَغَدَتْ كِلاَ الفَرْجَيْنِ تَحْسِبُ أنَّهُ * مَوْلَى المَخَافَةِ، خَلْفُهَا وَأَمَامُهَا
(So she set off at dawn, reckoning each of the two openings, behind her and before her, to be the "mawlā" — the place most worthy — of fear.)
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever I am his mawlā, then ʿAlī is his mawlā."
There are three views on its meaning:
The first: that the meaning is: whoever I take as an ally, ʿAlī takes him as an ally.
The second view: whoever takes me as an ally, he [ʿAlī] takes him as an ally.
The third view: it is related that Usāma ibn Zayd said to ʿAlī, peace be upon him: "You are not my mawlā; my mawlā is only the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." So he [the Prophet], peace be upon him, said: "Whoever I am his mawlā, then ʿAlī is his mawlā."

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ شَجَرَةَ ٱلزَّقُّومِ طَعَامُ ٱلأَثِيمِ﴾.
Shuʿba said: I heard Sulaymān [relate] from Mujāhid, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās was sitting with a crook-headed staff (miḥjan) in his hand while the people were circling the House, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O people, fear Allah, and do not die except as Muslims. For if a single drop of al-zaqqūm were to drip upon the people of this world, it would make their livelihood bitter for them — so how about one whose food is al-zaqqūm?"
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: ﴿طَعَامُ ٱلأَثِيمِ﴾: the food of the wicked.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَٱلْمُهْلِ يَغْلِي فِي ٱلْبُطُونِ كَغَلْيِ ٱلْحَمِيمِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Abū Ẓabyān related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-muhl is the dregs of oil.
Then He said ﴿تَغْلِي فِي البُطُونِ﴾, meaning the tree.
And whoever reads ﴿يَغْلِي﴾ makes it refer to the food and al-zaqqūm.
Al-Farrāʾ and Abū Ḥātim said: whoever reads ﴿يَغْلِي﴾ may make it refer to al-muhl.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is an error, because al-muhl is not what boils in the bellies; rather, what boils is only likened to it.
And al-ḥamīm: hot water, as [the poet] said:
* "فِيهَا كِبَاءٌ مُعَدٌّ وَحَمِيمٌ" *
(In it is prepared incense and hot water.)
al-Kibāʾ: incense; one says kabbabtu al-ʿūd, i.e. I burned the aloeswood as incense. And al-kibā, with the short final alif (maqṣūr), is sweepings.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خُذُوهُ فَٱعْتِلُوهُ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ﴾.
That is, He says to the angels: Seize him and drag him.
Mujāhid said: that is, push him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says ʿatalahu, yaʿtuluhu and yaʿtiluhu, when he drags him with violence and force.
Qatāda said: ﴿إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ﴾: to the middle of Hellfire.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْكَرِيمُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, peace be upon them both, read ﴿ذُقْ أنَّكَ﴾ with a fatḥa on the hamza, and it is the reading of al-Kisāʾī. The meaning according to it is: Taste, because you used to say this; and the meaning is: according to your own claim.
Qatāda said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed concerning "Abū Jahl" the verse ﴿أَوْلَى
لَكَ فَأَوْلَى. ثُمَّ أَوْلَى لَكَ فَأَوْلَى﴾, whereupon he said: Does Muḥammad threaten me, when there is none between its two mountains mightier or nobler than I? So Allah revealed ﴿ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْكَرِيمُ﴾, and He revealed concerning him ﴿كَلاَّ لاَ تُطِعْهُ واسْجُدْ وَاقْتَرِبْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ﴾.
Al-Kisāʾī said: al-maqām (with fatḥa) is the place, and al-muqām (with ḍamma) is the residing, as [the poet] said:
* "عَفَتِ الدِّيَارُ مَحَلُّهَا فَمُقَامُهَا" *
(The dwellings have been effaced — their place of halting and their place of staying.)
And the meaning of ﴿أَمِينٍ﴾ is: [secure] from ailments and sorrows.
Qatāda said: "Amīn": [secure] from Satan, from the idol-stones (al-anṣāb), and from sorrows.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَلْبَسُونَ مِن سُندُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ﴾.
ʿIkrima said: al-istabraq is thick brocade.
Abū Isḥāq said: al-istabraq is taken from al-barīq (lustre), and it is what is placed upon the Kaʿba; and al-sundus is the fine [kind] of it.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ وَزَوَّجْنَاهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, We married them [to them].
Qatāda said: and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: ﴿كَذَلِكَ وَزَوَّجْنَاهُمْ بِعِيسٍ
عِينٍ﴾, and its meaning is: the white ones; one says jamal aʿyas (a camel that is aʿyas) when it is white tending towards a reddish-blond tinge.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِكلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ آمِنِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: secure from death, from illness and from Satan.
And someone else said: secure from its being cut off, and from the hidden harm of its ill effects and its unpleasantness; it is not like the fruit of this world, which has hidden harm and runs out.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوْتَةَ ٱلأُولَىٰ وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ﴾.
The meaning is: they will not taste death in it at all. Then He said ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوْتَةَ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾ — an istithnāʾ (exception) that is not from [the genus of] the first [i.e. a disjoined exception]. And Sībawayh recited:
مَنْ كَانَ أَسْرَعَ فِي تَفَرُّقِ فَالجٍ * فَلَبُونُهُ جَرِبَتْ مَعاً وَأَغَدَّتِ
(Whoever was quickest in dispersing [the tribe of] Fālij, may his milch-camels all together become mangy and afflicted with swellings.)
Then he excepted what is not from the first, saying:
إلاَّ كَنَاشِرَةَ التي ضَيَّعْتُمُ * كَالغُصْنِ فِي غُلَوَائِهِ المُتَنَبِّتِ
(Except [one] like Nāshira, whom you neglected, like a branch in the vigour of its sprouting growth.)

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَضْلاً مِّن رَّبِّكَ ذَلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, He did that as a favour.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱرْتَقِبْ إِنَّهُمْ مُّرْتَقِبُونَ﴾.
That is, they are waiting.

nahhas-meani:1-3.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿حمۤ وَٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ﴾ [Verses 1 - 3].
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: ﴿فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ﴾: the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr).
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are three views on the meaning of this verse:
a- Among the soundest of them is what Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The Qurʾān was sent down on the Night of Decree to the lowest heaven
all at once; then Gabriel brought it down over twenty years." This is a chain of transmission that cannot be rejected.
b- And it was said: the meaning is: We sent down a Qurʾān concerning the excellence of the Night of Decree,
namely the saying of the Exalted ﴿لَيْلَةُ القَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ﴾. These are two views.
c- And it was said: the meaning is: We began sending it down on the Night of Decree, as you say: "I
am going out to Mecca tomorrow," i.e. I am beginning the departure.

nahhas-meani:4-5.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ أَمْراً مِّنْ عِنْدِنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ﴾ [Verses 4 and 5].
There are two closely related views on its meaning:
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, settles the affairs of the world until the following year on
the Night of Decree — whatever there is of life, death or provision.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Qatāda said something similar, except that Mujāhid said: except wretchedness and felicity, for these two do not change.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So this is one view.
And the meaning on it is that on the Night of Decree the angels are commanded concerning what there will be of
rain, provision, life and death until the following year.
And the meaning of "yufraqu" and "yuʾmaru" is the same, as though He said: every wise matter is commanded,
as a command from Us.
And the other view: that it is the night of the middle of Shaʿbān, in which the affairs of
the year are settled, the living are copied out from the dead, and the pilgrims are recorded, so that no one is added to them and none is taken away from them.
Someone else said: ﴿يُفْرَقُ﴾: is decreed and set out in detail on that night, until the like of it in the next year.
And ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ means made firm (muḥkam).
And it was said: the meaning of ﴿يُفْرَقُ﴾ is: is separated, i.e. a distinction is made between
the believer, the disbeliever and the hypocrite; this is told to the angels and they know it.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَٱرْتَقِبْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِي ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī ibn
Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, who said: "The sign of the smoke has not yet passed,
and it will come: a smoke will come that afflicts the believers with something like a cold, and the disbeliever will burst."
And al-Aʿmash narrated from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, who said: "A man sat
and said: The smoke has not occurred; it will only be on the Day of Resurrection: something like a cold
will take hold of the believers from it, and it will be severe upon the disbelievers and the hypocrites. So we went in to
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd while he was reclining, and told him what [the man] had said. He got up and sat
angry, and said: When one of you is asked about what he does not know, let him say: I have no knowledge of it; for Allah, Majestic and Mighty, says to His Prophet ﴿قُلْ لاَ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ، ومَا أَنَا مِنَ المُتَكَلِّفِينَ﴾. I will tell you about the smoke: Quraysh rebelled
against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and disbelieved, so he prayed to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, against them that He make them hungry. A severe hunger struck them, until a man would see between the sky and the earth
something like smoke, from hunger and heat. Then Quraysh said ﴿ربَّنَا اكْشِفْ عَنَّا العَذَابُ
إنَّا مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, so Allah removed it from them, and they relapsed; then He seized them with the greatest seizing
on the day of Badr. Had the smoke been on the Day of Resurrection, it would not have been removed from them."

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّا كَاشِفُو ٱلْعَذَابِ قَلِيلاً إِنَّكُمْ عَآئِدُونَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: you will return to sins.
And it is possible that it means: [you will be returning] as dead men.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ ٱلْبَطْشَةَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ إِنَّا مُنتَقِمُونَ﴾.
Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Ibn Masʿūd said about ﴿ٱلْبَطْشَةَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ﴾: it is the day of Badr.
And ʿAwf and Qatāda narrated from al-Ḥasan: ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ ٱلْبَطْشَةَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ﴾: he said: the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَجَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: We tested them.
He said: ﴿وَجَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾: meaning Moses ﷺ.
He said: ﴿وأَنْ لاَ تَعْلُوا عَلَيَّ﴾: that you not be insolent.
He said: And His saying ﴿إنِّي آتِيكُمْ بِسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, that is, with a clear excuse.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ أَن تَرْجُمُونِ﴾.
Qatāda said: with stones.
Al-Farrāʾ said: al-rajm here is killing.
And Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated from Abū Ṣāliḥ concerning ﴿وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ أَن تَرْجُمُونِ﴾: he said: that they should say: a sorcerer, or
a soothsayer, or a poet.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِن لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُواْ لِي فَٱعْتَزِلُونِ﴾.
That is, leave me alone, neither for me nor against me.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱتْرُكِ ٱلْبَحْرَ رَهْواً إِنَّهُمْ جُندٌ مُّغْرَقُونَ﴾.
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿رَهْواً﴾: a road.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: smooth.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿وَٱتْرُكِ ٱلْبَحْرَ رَهْواً﴾:
that is, still; do not command it to return to what it was until the last of them is in it.
And it is narrated from Mujāhid that he said: ﴿رَهْواً﴾: that is, dry.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another. What is still is called
rahw, as the poet said:
والخَيْلُ تَمْرغ رَهْواً فِي أَعِنَّتِهَا * كَالطَّيْرِ يَنْجُو مِنَ الشُّؤْبُوبِ ذِي البَرَدِ
(And the horses move gently (rahwan) in their reins, like birds escaping a hail-laden downpour.)
And it is said: the people came rahwan, in a single ordered line.

nahhas-meani:25-26.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿كَمْ تَرَكُواْ مِن جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ وَزُرُوعٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [Verses 25 and 26].
Al-Farrāʾ said: It is said: the fine dwellings; and it is said: the pulpits.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلأَرْضُ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُنظَرِينَ﴾.
Al-Musayyab ibn Rāfiʿ narrated from ʿAlī, peace be upon him, that he said: "There weep
for the believer the gate through which his deeds ascend, and his place of prayer on earth."
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The believer has a gate
through which his deeds ascend and his provision descends; when he dies, it weeps for him, and
the place where he used to pray weeps for him. But there was no good in the house of Pharaoh, nor did
they have any righteous deed that ascended. Allah the Exalted said ﴿فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلأَرْضُ﴾."
And it was said: the meaning is: the people of the heaven and the people of the earth did not weep for them, as the Exalted said ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: When the Arabs regard someone's death as momentous, they say:
the sky wept for him, and the sun grew dark for him — figuratively — as the poet said:
وَالشَّمْسُ طَالِعَةً لَيْسَتْ بِكَاسِفَةٍ * تَبْكِي عَلَيْكَ نُجُومَ اللَّيلِ وَالقَمَرَا
(The sun, risen yet not eclipsing [them], weeps for you — [alongside] the stars of the night and the moon.)
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا كَانُواْ مُنظَرِينَ﴾: that is, given respite.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَجَّيْنَا بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ مِن فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَالِياً مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: He used to slaughter their sons and spare their women.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَقَدِ ٱخْتَرْنَاهُمْ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عَلَى ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: over the peoples of their own time.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُم مِّنَ ٱلآيَاتِ مَا فِيهِ بَلاَءٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: He saved them from their enemy, brought them across the sea, and sent down
upon them the manna and the quails.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So al-balāʾ here is blessing on this view, as
the poet said:
 * "فَأَبْلاَهُمَا خَيْرَ البَلاَءِ الَّذِي يَبْلُو" *
(And He bestowed on them both the best of the favours with which He tests.)
And al-balāʾ here may be punishment, the opposite of blessing, i.e. affliction overtook them when
they disbelieved in the signs of Allah.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ لَيَقُولُونَ إِنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ مَوْتَتُنَا ٱلأُوْلَىٰ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُنشَرِينَ﴾.
"Inna hāʾulāʾi" means Quraysh; "in hiya" means "mā hiya" (it is not); and al-munsharūn are those resurrected: Allah resurrected (anshara) the dead and they were resurrected (nasharū), as the poet said:
يَا آلَ بَكْرٍ أَنْشِرُوا لِي كُلَيْباً * يَا آلَ بَكْرٍ أَيْنَ أَيْنَ الفِرَارُ؟
(O clan of Bakr, bring Kulayb back to life for me! O clan of Bakr, where, where is the escape?)

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَأْتُواْ بِآبَآئِنَا إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ holds that His saying ﴿فَأْتُواْ﴾ is addressed to the Prophet ﷺ alone,
according to the Arabs' usage in addressing an eminent person.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ﴾.
ʿĀʾisha said: Tubbaʿ was a righteous man; Allah censured his people and did not censure him.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: Ibn ʿAbbās asked Kaʿb: How is it that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, mentioned
the people of Tubbaʿ and did not mention Tubbaʿ? He said: Tubbaʿ was one of the kings, and his people were soothsayers, and with them were some of the People of the Book. His people
used to lie about the People of the Book in his presence, so he said to all of them: Offer a sacrifice. So they offered [sacrifices],
and the sacrifice of the People of the Book was accepted while the sacrifice of his people was not accepted, so he embraced Islam. For that reason
Allah mentioned his people and did not mention him.

safi-cedvel:1-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) the wāw of the oath; (الكتاب) genitive by the wāw, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم"; (في ليلة) attached to (أنزلناه) ...
The clause «(أقسم) بالكتاب ...» has no grammatical position: inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «إنّا أنزلناه ...» has no grammatical position: answer to the oath.
The clause «أنزلناه ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «كنّا منذرين ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the (second) إنّ.
4- 5- (فيها) attached to the passive (يفرق); (أمرا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it coincides with it in meaning, i.e. a distinguishing [Note: Or in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of أنزلناه, or of its object, or of the fāʿil of يفرق.. or it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) governed by أنزلنا or منذرين or يفرق.]; (من عندنا) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (أمرا).
The clause «يفرق كلّ أمر ...» is in the position of genitive as naʿt of ليلة.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
(رحمة) an accusative mafʿūl li-ajlihi [Note: Or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of مرسلين, or a badal (substitute) of (أمرا).]; (من ربّك) attached to a naʿt of (رحمة); (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar is السميع, and the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ.].
The clause «إنّه ... السميع ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
(ربّ) a badal of ربّك, genitive like it; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a relative noun in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السموات; (بينهما) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; (كنتم) a deficient (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «كنتم موقنين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or parenthetical.] ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: then be certain of the message of Muhammad, upon him be peace.
8- (ربّكم) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو".
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "(الله)", in the position of nominative.. or a second khabar of the particle resembling the verb, إنّ.].
The clause «يحيى ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or it is a khabar after a khabar, and likewise the clause (هو) ربّكم.].
The clause «يميت ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يحيى.
The clause «(هو) ربّكم ...» has no grammatical position: another explanatory resumption.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī); (في شكّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
The clause «هم في شكّ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يلعبون ...» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Benefits:
- بل ...
In this verse occur the words of Allah the Exalted بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ يَلْعَبُونَ. (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); the meaning of iḍrāb is that you negate the judgement of what precedes it and affirm it for what follows it, as in: جاء زيد بل عمرو. We shall clarify some matters related to it:
1- It is a particle of digression. If a clause follows it, the sense of the digression is either cancellation (ibṭāl), as in the words of Allah the Exalted: وَقالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمنُ وَلَداً سُبْحانَهُ، بَلْ عِبادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ, i.e. rather they are servants; (بل) has cancelled the judgement that the All-Merciful has taken a son. And as in the words of Allah the Exalted: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ؟ بَلْ جاءَهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ.
Or it conveys transition from one purpose to another, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى. وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى. بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا, and ولَدَيْنا كِتابٌ يَنْطِقُ بِالْحَقِّ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ بَلْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ. In all of this it is a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ), not a conjunction, according to the correct view.
2- If a single word follows it, it is a conjunction. Then, if a command or an affirmation precedes it — (اضرب زيدا بل عمرا) and (قام زيد بل عمرو) — nothing is judged about what precedes it, and the judgement is affirmed for what follows it.
3- If a negation or prohibition precedes it, it serves to confirm what precedes it as it is and to assign its opposite to what follows it, as in «ما قام زيد بل عمرو» and «لا يقم زيد بل عمرو».
4- «لا» is added before it to reinforce the digression after an affirmation, as in the saying of the poet:
وجهك البدر لا بل الشمس لو لم ... يقض للشمس كسفة أو أفول
(Your face is the full moon — no, rather the sun, had eclipse or setting not been decreed for the sun.)
When it occurs after a negation, it reinforces the confirmation of what precedes it.

safi-cedvel:10-12.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunctive, for linking; (يوم) an accusative mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بدخان) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تأتي), and (الباء) is for transitivity (taʿdiya).
The clause «ارتقب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to a resumption caused by what preceded, i.e.: take heed, and watch.
The clause «تأتي السماء ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يغشي ...» is in the position of genitive as naʿt (adjective) of دخان.
The clause «هذا عذاب ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied speech verb, i.e.: they said: this is a punishment.
The clause «ربّنا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «اكشف عنّا ...» has no grammatical position: answer to the vocative.
The clause «إنّا مؤمنون ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Benefits:
- Some of the signs of the Resurrection.
It is narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ saw the disbelievers of Mecca turning away, he said:
O Allah, [send] seven [years] like the seven of Yūsuf. Then a year [of drought] seized them which destroyed everything, until they ate hides and carrion from hunger, and one of them would look at the sky and see something like smoke. Then Abū Sufyān came to him and said: You have come commanding obedience to Allah and the maintaining of kinship ties, and your people have perished, so pray to Allah for them.
So he prayed, and Allah removed the punishment from them; then they reverted, so He took vengeance on them on the day of Badr, as shown by the words of Allah the Exalted: يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ الْبَطْشَةَ الْكُبْرى إِنَّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ.
It is also said that it is a smoke that will come before the Hour is established and has not yet come. It will enter the ears of the disbelievers and the hypocrites until a man's head becomes like a roasted (ḥanīdh, grilled) head, while the believer will be afflicted by something like a cold, and the whole earth will be like a house in which a fire has been kindled. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿAmr al-Ḥasan [Translator's note: so in the source; probably "Ibn ʿUmar and al-Ḥasan"]. It is supported by what al-Baghawī narrated with the chain of al-Thaʿlabī from Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The first of the signs (i.e. the signs of the Hour) are the descent of ʿĪsā son of Maryam, and a fire that will come out of the depths of ʿAdan driving people to the place of gathering, taking its midday rest (sleeping) with them when they take their midday rest. Ḥudhayfa said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is the smoke?
So he recited this verse يَوْمَ تَأْتِي السَّماءُ بِدُخانٍ مُبِينٍ: it will fill what is between the east and the west and remain for forty days and nights. As for the believer, something like a cold will afflict him from it; and as for the disbeliever, he will be like one drunk; it will come out of his nostrils, his ears and his backside.
And Allah knows best. The meaning of حصّت is: destroyed.

safi-cedvel:13-16.t:
* I'rab:
(أنّى) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) [Note: Or it is an adverb governed by the sense of "being established" (al-istiqrār), and the khabar is (لهم).]; (لهم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الذكرى; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq).
The clause «أنّى لهم الذكرى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جاءهم رسول ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the pronoun in (لهم).
14- (تولّوا) indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied on the alif, which was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; (عنه) attached to (تولّوا); (معلّم) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو"; (مجنون) a nominative second khabar.
The clause «تولّوا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause جاءهم رسول.
The clause «قالوا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause جاءهم رسول [Note: Or it is a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of تولّوا, with قد implied.].
The clause «(هو) معلّم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
15- (قليلا) an accusative noun standing in for an implied adverb (ẓarf), i.e. a little time [Translator's note: the source has طرف, evidently a misprint for ظرف.] [Note: It may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. a little removal.] ...
The clause «إنّا كاشفوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), an answer to their supplication ...
The clause «إنّكم عائدون ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the preceding resumption.
16- (يوم) an accusative adverb of time, attached to (عائدون) [Note: Or attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر".]; (البطشة) an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq.
The clause «نبطش ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «إنّا منتقمون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption — or causal —.

* Morphology:
(14) معلّم: passive participle of the four-letter علّم; its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(15) عائدون: plural of عائد, active participle of the triliteral عاد; its pattern is فاعل. It contains the substitution (ibdāl) of the weak letter by hamza: its original form is عاود; the wāw came after the alif of فاعل and was changed to hamza, as is regular in the active participle of hollow verbs.
(16) البطشة: a maṣdar of a single occurrence (al-marra) of the triliteral verb بطش; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:17-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (قبلهم) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فتنا); the wāw is a conjunction — or circumstantial —.
The clause «قد فتنا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.. the implied oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
The clause «جاءهم رسول ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause answering the oath [Note: Or in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), with قد implied.].
18- (أن) explicative (tafsīriyya), because something carrying the sense of speech precedes it [Note: It may be maṣdar-forming, the interpreted maṣdar being in the position of genitive by an omitted bāʾ, i.e. بأن أدّوا, the preposition being attached to (جاءهم).. It may also be lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause أدّوا the khabar of أنّ.]; (إليّ) attached to (أدّوا); (عباد) an accusative vocative (munādā) from which the vocative particle has been omitted, and the object of (أدّوا) is omitted; (لكم) attached to a ḥāl of رسول.
The clause «أدّوا ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.
The clause «the vocative and its implied answer» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «إنّي لكم رسول ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the preceding command — or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
19- (الواو) conjunction; (أن) like the first, in all its possibilities; (لا) prohibitive; (على الله) attached to (تعلوا); (آتيكم) a nominative khabar (predicate) of إنّ, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ [Note: It is an active participle — or it is a nominative imperfect verb, (كم) being the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the clause the khabar of إنّ.]; (بسلطان) attached to (آتيكم) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in آتيكم.].
The clause «لا تعلوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the explicative clause.
The clause «إنّي آتيكم ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the preceding prohibition — or an explanatory resumption.
20- (الواو) resumptive; (بربّي) attached to (عذت); (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-making particle; the nūn in (ترجمون) is the nūn of protection (wiqāya) before the first-person yāʾ, which is deleted to suit the verse-ending (fāṣila).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ترجمون) is in the position of genitive [Translator's note: the source reads "in the position of a preposition", evidently a slip for "genitive".] by an omitted preposition, attached to (عذت), i.e. from your stoning me.
The clause «إنّي عذت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عذت ...» is the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «ترجمون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
21- (الواو) conjunction; (لم) for negation only; (تؤمنوا) a jussive imperfect verb, protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn, and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (لي) attached to (تؤمنوا) by its being made to carry the meaning of تقرّوا "acknowledge" (taḍmīn); (الفاء) linking the apodosis; the (النون) in (اعتزلون) is for protection.
The clause «إن لم تؤمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّي عذت.
The clause «اعتزلون» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with fāʾ.
22- (الفاء) conjunction.
The clause «دعا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: they did not leave him alone, so he called upon his Lord.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ هؤلاء قوم..) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (دعا), i.e.: he called upon his Lord with [the words] that these are a people.. and (الباء) is for transitivity (taʿdiya).

* Morphology:
(18) أدّوا: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, starting from the imperfect. Its imperfect assigned to the plural wāw is هم يؤدّون, originally يؤديون; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made vowelless and the vowel was moved to the dāl — iʿlāl by making vowelless — then the yāʾ was deleted because, being vowelless, it met the plural wāw, so it became يؤدّون. When it passed to the imperative, the iʿlāl remained. The pattern of أدّوا is أفعوا.
(19) تعلوا: it contains iʿlāl by deletion; its original form is تعلووا — with two wāws — and when two vowelless letters met, the wāw of the verb, the weak letter, was deleted and it became تعلوا; its pattern is تفعوا.
(آتيكم): active participle of the triliteral أتى, on the pattern فاعل. When the hamza of أتى met the alif of فاعل, they were merged and a madda was placed over them.. It contains iʿlāl by making vowelless, the original being آتيكم with ḍamma on the yāʾ..
The word may also be an imperfect of the triliteral أتى: when the hamza of the imperfect entered, the second hamza being vowelless, they were merged and the madda was placed over them; the original is أأتى with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:23-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (بعبادي) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أسر); (ليلا) an accusative adverb of time, attached to (أسر); the adverb comes for emphasis.
The clause «أسر ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if you want deliverance, then travel by night.. and the conditional clause is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied speech verb, i.e.: Allah the Exalted said to Mūsā ...
The clause «إنّكم متّبعون» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
24- (الواو) conjunction; (رهوا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of البحر [Note: Or a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb (اترك), if it is one of the verbs of transformation; al-ʿUkbarī said this.].
The clause «اترك ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause أسر ...
The clause «إنّهم جند ...» has no grammatical position: causal.

* Morphology:
(رهوا): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral رها يرهو, meaning "to be still" or "to part"; in the verse it is used in place of an adjective meaning "still" or "parted".

* Benefits:
- The hamza of the imperative.
The hamza of the imperative is a connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl) in the three-letter, five-letter and six-letter verbs. The three-letter, such as اكتب - انزل - اذهب.
The five-letter, such as: انتظم - ارتقب - احترس.
The six-letter, such as: استخدم - استغفر. It is to be noted that its vowel is kasra in the imperative, except for the three-letter verb with ḍamma on the ʿayn, where it comes with ḍamma, such as: اكتب - أرسم. Likewise it takes ḍamma in the imperfect of the five- and six-letter verbs in the passive [Translator's note: so in the source; the examples that follow are past passive forms.], such as: انتصر على العدو. استخدم الكتاب استخداما نافعا. As for the imperative of the four-letter verb beginning with a hamza, it is a disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ), such as: أكرم - أحسن ... etc. It occurs in the verse under discussion: فأسر.

safi-cedvel:25-29.t:
* I'rab:
(كم) declarative (khabariyya), an allusive noun of number (kināya al-ʿadad), in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من جنّات) tamyīz (specification); (فيها) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فاكهين).
The clause «تركوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كانوا فيها فاكهين» is in the position of genitive as naʿt (adjective) of نعمة.
28- (كذلك) attached to the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter is thus [Note: Or attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), governed by the verb تركوا or by an omitted verb, its implied form being "أهلكناهم" or "أخرجناهم".. In that case the clause أورثناها is conjoined to the implied clause.]; (الواو) conjunction; (قوما) an accusative second mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «(الأمر) كذلك ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «أورثناها ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause.
29- (الفاء) conjunction, and likewise (الواو); (عليهم) attached to (بكت); (ما) "sufficing" (kāfiya) [Translator's note: so in the source; نافية "negative" is evidently meant.] in both places.
The clause «ما بكت عليهم السماء» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أورثناها.
The clause «ما كانوا منظرين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to أورثناها.

* Morphology:
(29) بكت: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, the lām of the word and the tāʾ of the feminine.. its pattern is فعت.

* Rhetoric:
Imaginative representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya al-takhyīliyya): in the words of Allah the Exalted «فَما بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّماءُ وَالْأَرْضُ».
For the state of their death, because of its severity and magnitude, is likened to the state of one over whom the sky and the great celestial bodies weep. It is also said: it is an implicit imaginative metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya takhyīliyya), in that the sky and the earth are likened to a human being and weeping is attributed to them.
When an eminent man died, the Arabs would say, in magnifying his death: the sky and the earth wept over him, the wind wept for him, and the like. The poet said, lamenting the Commander of the Believers ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz:
الشمس طالعة ليست بكاسفة ... تبكي عليك نجوم الليل والقمرا
(The sun is risen, not eclipsed, weeping over you — [outshining] the stars of the night and the moon.)

* Benefits:
- In this verse occurs (كم) al-khabariyya (the declarative كم). We have spoken in detail about the interrogative كم and the declarative كم in Sūrat al-Zukhruf, verse (6), so refer back to it.

safi-cedvel:30-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) for realisation (taḥqīq); (من العذاب) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نجّينا).
The clause «نجّينا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.. the implied oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
31- (من فرعون) a badal (substitute) of العذاب with the preposition repeated; (من المسرفين) attached to a second khabar of (كان).
The clause «إنّه كان عاليا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
32- (ولقد) like the first, and the wāw is a conjunction; (على علم) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent pronoun; (على العالمين) attached to (اخترناهم) by its being made to carry the meaning of ميّزناهم "We distinguished them" (taḍmīn).
The clause «اخترناهم ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.. the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first oath clause.
33- (الواو) conjunction; (من الآيات) attached to a ḥāl of (ما), which is the second object; (فيه) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of (بلاء).
The clause «آتيناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اخترناهم.
The clause «فيه بلاء ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

* Benefits:
- (ما) occurs in the noble verse in the words of Allah the Exalted: وَآتَيْناهُمْ مِنَ الْآياتِ ما فِيهِ بَلؤُا مُبِينٌ. (ما) here admits two readings: either it is a relative noun, or it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa) meaning "a thing". In both cases it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause after it is the ṣila in the first case and an adjective in the second. Ibn Hishām explained this aspect, saying: in our saying أعجبني ما صنعت, (ما) may mean الذي, or be an indefinite qualified noun — and on these two the resumptive pronoun is omitted, the implied form being أعجبني ما صنعته — or be maṣdar-forming, with no resumptive pronoun. Accordingly the implied sense is: "what you made pleased me", or "something you made", or "your making". These three readings occur in the words of Allah the Exalted: ثُمَّ لا يَجِدُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجاً مِمَّا قَضَيْتَ, i.e. of that which you decided, or of a thing you decided, or of your decision.
Ibn Hishām says: I do not know of them adding (ما) after the bāʾ except that its meaning is causal.
As in the words of Allah the Exalted: فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهُمْ لَعَنَّاهُمْ and فَبِما رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ.
As for (من), it sometimes admits being relative or qualified indefinite, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَبِالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَما هُمْ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ; the implied sense is: among the people is he who says, or someone who says.

safi-cedvel:34-36.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negative, governing like ليس; (منشرين) genitive in form, accusative in position, khabar (predicate) of ما ...
The clause «إنّ هؤلاء ليقولون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إن هي إلّا موتتنا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ما نحن بمنشرين ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause that is the object of speech.
36- (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (بآبائنا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ائتوا); (كنتم) a deficient (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «ائتوا ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if you speak the truth, then bring ...
The clause «إن كنتم صادقين» has no grammatical position: explicative.. and the apodosis is implied, indicated by what precedes it.

* Morphology:
(35) منشرين: plural of منشر, with ḍamma, then sukūn, then fatḥa; a passive participle of the four-letter أنشر; its pattern is مفعل.

safi-cedvel:37-39.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) interrogative, carrying the sense of rebuke; (أم) a conjunction; (قوم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the third-person pronoun هم; (الواو) resumptive — or conjunctive —; (الذين) a relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: It may be conjoined to (قوم) by the wāw, and the clause أهلكناهم is then a new sentence (mustaʾnafa).]; (من قبلهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
The clause «هم خير ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «الذين من قبلهم أهلكناهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أهلكناهم ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «إنّهم كانوا مجرمين ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كانوا مجرمين ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
38- (الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to السموات; (بينهما) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; (لاعبين) an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of خلقنا.
The clause «ما خلقنا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
39- (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of خلقناهما; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative.
The clause «ما خلقناهما ...» has no grammatical position: a badal (substitute) of the clause ما خلقنا السموات.
The clause «لكنّ أكثرهم لا يعلمون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما خلقناهما.
The clause «لا يعلمون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of لكنّ.

* Morphology:
(تبّع): a proper name; he is Tubbaʿ al-Ḥimyarī, said to have been a prophet or a righteous man. Its pattern is فعّل with ḍamma on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

* Benefits:
- Who is Tubbaʿ?
It is said: he is Tubbaʿ al-Ḥimyarī, one of the kings of Yemen, called Tubbaʿ because of the large number of his followers (atbāʿ). It is also said: it is a title of the kings of Yemen, just as [the ruler] is called caliph in Islam. Tubbaʿ used to worship fire; then he became Muslim and called his people Ḥimyar to Islam, but they denied him.
From Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: Do not revile Tubbaʿ, for he had become Muslim. Narrated by Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal.
From Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: I do not know whether Tubbaʿ was a prophet or not a prophet.
From ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: Do not revile Tubbaʿ, for he was a righteous man. Ibn Isḥāq and others mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbās — they said: The last Tubbaʿ was Abū Karib Asʿad ibn Malīk. He had marched with armies towards the east, until he settled al-Ḥīra [Translator's note: the source has حير الحيرة, literally "he made al-Ḥīra a ḥīra (encampment)"], built Samarqand, and returned from the direction of the east. He made his way through Medina and found that his son, whom he had left there, had been treacherously killed, so he resolved to destroy it. The Anṣār would fight him by day and give him hospitality by night, and this pleased him. While he was thus, two rabbis from Qurayẓa came to him and persuaded him to abandon the fighting, and he entered their religion. Then he set out heading for Yemen, and on the way a group from Hudhayl met him and tempted him [to plunder] the Kaʿba; when he learned of their lie he killed them, and he went to the Kaʿba, clothed it, sacrificed six thousand camels, circumambulated and shaved his head. Then he left for Yemen and called his people to Islam, but they denied him.

safi-cedvel:40-42.t:
* I'rab:
(أجمعين) a genitive tawkīd (emphasis) in meaning (maʿnawī) of the pronoun in (ميقاتهم) ...
The clause «إنّ يوم الفصل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
41- (يوم) an accusative badal (substitute) of the first يوم; (لا) negative; (عن مولى) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يغني); (شيئا) an accusative mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. anything of the punishment; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative; the wāw in (ينصرون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «لا يغني مولى ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا هم ينصرون ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause لا يغني.
The clause «ينصرون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
42- (إلّا) for exception; (من) in the position of nominative as badal of the nāʾib fāʿil [Note: Or of the first مولى.]; (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is العزيز, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ.. It may also be borrowed for the accusative position, as a tawkīd of the noun of إنّ.].
The clause «رحم الله ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «إنّه ... العزيز» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:43-50.t:
* I'rab:
(كالمهل) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second khabar of (إنّ) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of طعام الأثيم, the governing factor in it being the sense of emphasis in (إنّ).]; (في البطون) attached to (يغلي); (كغلي) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. a boiling like the boiling of scalding water.
The clause «إنّ شجرة الزقّوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يغلي ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of المهل.
47- 50- (الفاء) conjunction; (إلى سواء) attached to (اعتلوه); (ثمّ) a conjunction; (فوق) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to (صبّوا); (من عذاب) attached to (صبّوا); (أنت) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a pronoun borrowed for the accusative position, a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of إنّ.]; (ما) a relative noun, khabar of إنّ; (به) attached to (تمترون).
The clause «خذوه ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied speech verb [Note: I.e. Allah says to the keepers of Hell (al-zabāniya).].
The clause «اعتلوه ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause that is the object of speech.
The clause «صبّوا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause اعتلوه.
The clause «ذق ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied speech verb [Note: I.e. the keepers of Hell say to him.].
The clause «إنّك ... العزيز» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «إنّ هذا ما ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كنتم به تمترون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «تمترون ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(46) غلى: an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral غلى يغلي of the ḍaraba class; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(49) ذق: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion on account of being indeclinable on sukūn; its original is ذوق; the wāw was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.

* Rhetoric:
1- Simile (tashbīh): in the words of Allah the Exalted «إِنَّ شَجَرَةَ الزَّقُّومِ طَعامُ الْأَثِيمِ، كَالْمُهْلِ يَغْلِي فِي الْبُطُونِ كَغَلْيِ الْحَمِيمِ».
For the zaqqūm is likened to copper melted by the action of fire, which is مهل, because it is left gradually (yumhal) in the fire until it melts. They describe every blameworthy food as boiling in the bellies — not literally; it is only figurative, as you say: rancour boils in his heart, and enmity boils in his breast.
2- Implicit imaginative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-takhyīliyya): in the words of Allah the Exalted «ثُمَّ صُبُّوا فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ مِنْ عَذابِ الْحَمِيمِ».
For the punishment is likened to a liquid, and then pouring is imagined for it, as in his saying:
صبّت عليه صروف الدّهر من صبب
(The vicissitudes of time were poured upon him from a slope.)
and as in the words of Allah the Exalted «أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنا صَبْراً». So He mentioned the punishment with pouring attached to it, borrowed for it, so that it would be more terrible and more awe-inspiring.
3- The figure of sarcasm (al-tahakkum): in the words of Allah the Exalted «ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْكَرِيمُ». This figure consists of using the language of good tidings in the place of warning, and of promise in the place of threat, out of the speaker's contempt for the one addressed and mockery of him; it is more galling to the one mocked and more painful to him.
For this noble verse came by way of mockery and sarcasm towards one who used to vaunt his might and nobility over his people.

safi-cedvel:51-57.t:
* I'rab:
(في مقام) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of إنّ; (في جنّات) a badal (substitute) of مقام with the preposition repeated; (من سندس) attached to (يلبسون).
The clause «إنّ المتّقين في مقام ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يلبسون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of nominative as a second khabar of (إنّ).].
54- (كذلك) attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter is thus; (الواو) conjunction; (بحور) attached to (زوّجناهم).
The clause «الأمر كذلك ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «زوّجناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يلبسون.
55- (فيها) attached to (يدعون); (بكلّ) attached to (يدعون) by its being made to carry the meaning of يرغبون "they desire" (taḍmīn); (آمنين) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يدعون.
The clause «يدعون ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in (زوّجناهم).
56- 57- (لا) negative; (فيها) attached to (يذوقون); (إلّا) for exception; (الموتة) excepted, accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) [Note: Some said the exception is connected (muttaṣil), the interpretation being: the believer, at his death in this world, is as though in his place in Paradise, because of what he is given of it or because of what he becomes certain of regarding its bliss (Ḥāshiyat al-Jamal).]; (الواو) conjunction; (فضلا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it coincides with it in derivation, i.e. as a favour [Note: It may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) governed by وقاهم or يدعون.]; (من ربّك) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (فضلا); (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).
The clause «لا يذوقون ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the fāʿil in (يدعون) or of the pronoun in (آمنين).
The clause «وقاهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause زوّجناهم, taking account of the iltifāt (shift of person).
The clause «ذلك ... الفوز» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(54) حور: plural of حوراء, feminine of أحور, a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from حور يحور of the fariḥa class, i.e. the black of the eye became intense and its white became intense; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
Implicit imaginative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-takhyīliyya): in the words of Allah the Exalted «إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقامٍ أَمِينٍ».
أمين is from أمن (trustworthiness), which is the opposite of betrayal; the place is described by it by way of metaphor, as though a fearful place betrays its occupant because of the hardships he meets in it.

safi-cedvel:58-58.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (بلسانك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يسّرناه), and (الباء) is for accompaniment.
The clause «يسّرناه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لعلّهم يتذكرون» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يتذكّرون» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.

* Rhetoric:
- The five verbs (al-afʿāl al-khamsa).
In this verse occur the words of Allah the Exalted لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ. The verb يتذكرون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). We shall set out below the most important points concerning the five verbs:
1- They are called the five verbs because we form five forms from the verb. The five verbs are every imperfect to which the dual alif, the plural wāw or the yāʾ of the (feminine) addressee is attached.
So from the verb يكتب we form the five verbs as follows: يكتبون - تكتبون - يكتبان - تكتبان - تكتبين.
2- The five verbs are made nominative by the retention of the nūn.
3- They are made accusative and jussive by the deletion of the nūn.
So I say: لم يكتبوا - لم تحفظي - لن تذهبوا - لن تنصرفا.
Remark: the dual alif, the plural wāw and the yāʾ of the addressee attached to the verb are in the position of nominative as fāʿil, or in the nominative as its noun if the verb is deficient (nāqiṣ) (i.e. kāna and its sisters).

safi-cedvel:59-59.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition.
The clause «ارتقب» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if they disbelieve, then await their destruction.
The clause «إنّهم مرتقبون» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(مرتقبون): plural of مرتقب, active participle of the five-letter ارتقب; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {يَغْشَى الناس}: a second adjective (ṣifa), meaning "with a clear smoke that envelops."
His saying: «هذا عَذابٌ» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; and that saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "saying that." It is also possible that it is not governed by any saying at all, but is a mere statement of information.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {أنى لَهُمُ الذكرى}: it is possible that «أنَّى» is the khabar (predicate) of «ذِكْرى», with «لهم» serving as a clarification. It is also possible that «أنَّى» is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), attached to the settled-in-place meaning in «لهم», since «لهم» has occurred as the khabar of «ذِكْرى».
His saying: «وقد جاءَهم» is a ḥāl from «لهم». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «مُعَلِّم» with kasra on the lām.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {قَلِيلاً}: an adjective of an omitted time or verbal noun, i.e. "a little removal" or "a little time."

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ}: it is said that it is a badal (substitute) for «يَومَ تأتي». It is said that it is accusative through an implied "remember" (udhkur). It is said that it is governed by «مُنْتَقِمون». And it is said that it is governed by what «مُنْتَقِمون» points to, namely "he takes vengeance" (yantaqim). This last was rejected on the ground that what follows «إنَّ» does not operate on what precedes it, and that only what is able to operate may be the thing that is explained.
His saying: «نَبْطِش»: the majority read it with fatḥa on the nūn and kasra on the ṭāʾ, i.e. "we seize them." al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read it with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, which is a dialectal form of the imperfect of بَطَشَ. al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ and Ṭalḥa read it with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the ṭāʾ, which is transferred from بَطَشَ, i.e. "the angels seize them." On this reading «البَطْشَةَ» may be accusative through «نُبْطِشُ» with the extra element dropped, like {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17]; or it may be accusative through an implied verb, i.e. "the angels seize them, so they seize the seizure."

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا}: it was read «فَتَّنَّا» with shadda, for intensification or multiplication, because of the multiplicity of what it relates to. And «جاءهم رسولٌ» may be resumptive (istiʾnāf) or a ḥāl.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {أَنْ أدوا}: it may be the explicative (mufassira), because something with the sense of saying precedes it; it may be the lightened (mukhaffafa) one; and it may be the one that puts the imperfect in the subjunctive, which is connected to an imperative. There is a difficulty, mentioned earlier, in taking it as the lightened one: the khabar in this chapter does not occur as a request. And if it is taken as a maṣdar particle, it is with the preposition omitted, i.e. "he came to them with (the message) that you hand over." «عبادَ الله» may be a direct object (mafʿūl bihi). It is said in the exegesis that he asked them to hand over to him the Children of Israel, and {فَأَرْسِلْ مَعِيَ بني إِسْرَائِيلَ} indicates this. Or it may be a vocative (munādā), with the object omitted, i.e. "give me obedience, O servants of Allah."

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {وَأَن لاَّ تَعْلُواْ}: conjoined (ʿaṭf) to the first «أَنْ». The majority read «إنِّي آتِيْكم» with kasra on the hamza, as resumptive. It was also read with fatḥa, assuming a lām, i.e. "and that you do not exalt yourselves, because I am bringing you…"

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {أَن تَرْجُمُونِ}: i.e. "from your stoning me" (min an tarjumūn).
And his saying: «إنِّي عُذْتُ» is resumptive. Abū ʿAmr and the two companions (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) assimilated the dhāl into the tāʾ. Its justification has already been given in Ṭāhā at his saying {فَنَبَذْتُهَا} [Ṭāhā: 96].

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {أَنَّ هؤلاء}: the majority read it with fatḥa, with an implied preposition, i.e. "he called upon him with (the plea) that these…". Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā and al-Ḥasan read it with kasra, with an implied saying according to the Basrans, and by treating «دَعا» like "said" according to the Kufans.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {فَأَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي}: the two readings with connecting and cutting hamza have been given earlier. al-Zamakhsharī said: "There are two aspects to it: an implied saying after the fāʾ, i.e. 'so He said: travel by night with My servants'; or it is the apodosis of an implied condition, as if He had said: 'if the matter is as you say, then travel by night with My servants.'" The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "He often claims the omission of the condition, but that is not permitted except with clear evidence, such as an imperative or the like preceding it."

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {رَهْواً}: it may be a second object, on the basis that «تَرَكَ» means "made" (ṣayyara); or a ḥāl, on the basis that it does not have that meaning. As for الرَّهْو, it is said to mean stillness, so the meaning is "leave it still." One says: رَهَا يَرْهُوا رَهْواً. From this comes "the horses came رَهْواً." al-Nābigha said:
4014 - والخيلَ تَمْزَعُ رَهْواً في أَعِنَّتِها ... كالطيرِ تَنْجُوْ مِنَ الشُّؤْبوب ذي البَرَدِ
(The horses run smoothly in their bridles, like birds escaping a downpour with hail.)
And رَهَا يَرْهُو in his walking means he went gently. al-Qaṭāmī said:
4015 - يَمْشِيْنَ رَهْواً فلا الأَعْجازُ خاذِلَةٌ ... ولا الصدورُ على الأعجازِ تَتَّكِلُ
(They walk gently; the hindquarters do not fail, nor do the chests rely on the hindquarters.)
From Abū ʿUbayda: رَهْواً means "leave it open, in gaps, as you left it."
In the exegesis: when the sea split for Moses and he came up out of it, he feared that Pharaoh would follow him, so he wished to strike it so that it would return and they would not catch up with him. He was commanded to leave it in gaps. Its origin is from their saying: / رَها الرجلُ يَرْهُو رَهْواً, when the man parted what is between his legs. الرَّهْو and الرَّهْوَة mean a place that is both elevated and low, where (water) collects, so it is one of the contronyms (aḍdād). الرَّهْوَة is also the woman with a wide private part. And الرَّهْو is a bird, said to be the crane. The discussion of the parallel to {كَمْ تَرَكُواْ مِن جَنَّاتٍ} has already been given in al-Shuʿarāʾ.

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {وَمَقَامٍ}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the mīm, which is a noun of place, the place of standing. Ibn Hurmuz, Qatāda, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ, and Nāfiʿ in the transmission of Khārija read it with ḍamma, a noun of place from أقام.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
And النَّعْمَة with fatḥa means the freshness and delight of life. The majority read it as genitive. Abū Rajāʾ made it accusative, conjoined to «كم», i.e. "they left much of such-and-such, and they left a pleasant life."
His saying: «فاكِهين»: the majority read it with alif, meaning "of good spirit" or "possessors of fruit" like لابن (possessor of milk) and تامر (possessor of dates). It is also said: فاكهين means "heedless, amusing themselves." al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read «فَكِهين», meaning "treating lightly, mocking." al-Jawharī said: "One says: فَكِهَ الرجلُ, with kasra, and he is فَكِهٌ when he is a joker; and الفَكِهُ also means the insolent (al-ashir)."

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: the kāf may be nominative in position, as khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is thus"; al-Zajjāj inclined to this. It may also be accusative in position; al-Ḥūfī implied: "We destroyed (them) a destruction, and took vengeance a vengeance, like that." al-Kalbī said: "Thus I do to whoever disobeys Me." It is also said that the implied form is "He does a deed like that." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "a leaving like that," making it an adjective of the omitted "leaving." On all these aspects one stops at «كذلك» and begins «وأَوْرَثْناها». al-Zamakhsharī said: "The kāf is accusative in the sense of: 'in the likeness of that expulsion We expelled them from it, and We made another people, not of them, inherit it.'" On this view «وأَوْرَثْناها» is conjoined to that clause which governs the kāf, and so stopping at «كذلك» is not permitted.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السمآء}: it may be a metaphor (istiʿāra), like the saying of al-Farazdaq:
4016 - الشمسُ طالِعَةٌ ليسَتْ بكاسِفَةٍ ... تَبْكي عليك نجومَ الليلِ والقمرا
(The sun is rising, not eclipsed; the stars of the night and the moon weep for you.)
Jarīr said:
4017 - لَمَّا أتى خبرُ الزُّبَيْرِ تواضَعَتْ ... سُوْرُ المدينةِ والجبالُ الخُشَّعُ
(When the news of al-Zubayr came, the walls of the city humbled themselves, and the submissive mountains.)
al-Nābigha said:
4018 - بكى حارِثُ الجَوْلانِ مِنْ فَقْدِ رَبِّهِ ... وحَوْرَانُ منه خاشِعٌ مُتَضائِلُ
(Ḥārith of al-Jawlān wept for the loss of his lord, and Ḥawrān, humbled by it, shrank.)

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {مِن فِرْعَوْنَ}: there are two aspects to it. The first: it is a badal (substitute) for «العذاب», either with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from the torment of Pharaoh," or by way of exaggeration, making him the very torment itself and so substituting him for it. The second: it is a ḥāl from «العذاب», its implied form being "proceeding from Pharaoh."
ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) read {مِنَ عَذَابِ المهين}, which is the annexation of the qualified noun to its attribute, since the original is "the humiliating torment," as in the well-known reading.
Ibn ʿAbbās read «مَنْ فرعونُ» with fatḥa on the mīm of «مَنْ» and nominative «فرعونُ», as mubtadaʾ and khabar; it is a question of contempt, like your saying "Who are you and Zayd?" Then He explained his state by the clause that follows, in His saying {إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَالِياً مِّنَ المسرفين}.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {على عِلْمٍ عَلَى العالمين}: the first «على» is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl from the agent in «اخْتَرْناهم». The second is attached to «اخْتَرْناهم». In the Shaykh's (Abū Ḥayyān's) wording: since their meanings differ, it is permissible for both to be attached to «اخْتَرْنا». The Shaykh recited a parallel to that:
4019 - ويَوْماً على ظَهْر الكَثِيْبِ تَعَذَّرَتْ ... عليَّ وآلَتْ حَلْفَةً لم تَحَلَّلِ
(And one day, on the back of the sand dune, she was unyielding toward me and swore an oath she did not absolve.)
Then he said: "So «على عِلْم» is a ḥāl, either from the agent or from the object; and «على ظَهْر» is a ḥāl from the agent in «تَعَذَّرَتْ». The operator in the ḥāl is the operator in its owner." There is something to consider here: his first statement, "and therefore both are attached to one verb when the meanings differ," contradicts making the first a ḥāl, because then it is not attached to the verb. And his statement "the operator in the ḥāl is the operator in its owner" does not help in that.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {والذين مِن قَبْلِهِمْ}: three aspects are possible. The first: it is conjoined to «قومُ تُبَّع». The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is what follows, namely «أَهْلَكْناهم». As for the first aspect, «أَهْلَكْناهم» is either resumptive or a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in the ṣila. The third: it is accusative through an implied verb which «أَهْلَكْناهم» explains. In that case «أَهْلكنا» has no grammatical position.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {لاَعِبِينَ}: a ḥāl. ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «وما بينَهُنَّ» because the heavens and the earth are a plural. The majority read «بينَهما», considering the two kinds.

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ بالحق}: a ḥāl, either from the agent, which is the apparent view, or from the object, i.e. "except as ones acting rightly" or "ones joined/ with the truth."

semin-durr:40-40.t: His saying: {إِنَّ يَوْمَ الفصل مِيقَاتُهُمْ}: the majority read «ميقاتُهم» as nominative, the khabar of «إنَّ». It was also read as accusative, as the ism (subject) of «إنَّ», with «يومَ الفصلِ» as its khabar. And «أَجْمعين» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the genitive pronoun.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ لاَ يُغْنِي}: it may be a badal from «يومَ الفصل», or an explicative apposition (bayān) according to those who do not require agreement in definiteness and indefiniteness; it may be accusative through an implied "I mean" (aʿnī); or it may be an adjective of «مِيقاتُهم», though it is indeclinable (buniya). Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. But this is not possible according to the Basrans, because it is annexed to an inflected word. This was discussed earlier, at the end of al-Māʾida. It may also be accusative through a verb that «يومَ الفَصْلِ» points to, i.e. "He decides between them on a day when… no benefit." It is not permitted for it to be accusative through «الفصل» itself, because that would entail a separation between the two by an outsider, namely «ميقاتُهم», and «الفَصْل» is a maṣdar, in which that is not permitted. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "because it has already been predicated about," and there is looseness in this, since predicating about what is annexed to «الفَصْل» does not negate «الفَصْل».
His saying: «ولا هم»: the pronoun is plural, referring back to «مَوْلَى», although it is singular, because the meaning was intended and so it was pluralised; and it is indefinite in a context of negation, so it is general.

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ الله}: four aspects are possible. The first, which is the saying of al-Kisāʾī: it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ). The second: it is connected, its implied form being "no relative avails another relative, except the believers, for they will be permitted to intercede, and they will intercede for some of one another." The third: it is nominative as a badal for the first «مَوْلَى», with «يُغْني» meaning "benefits"; al-Ḥūfī said this. The fourth: it is also nominative in position, as a badal for the wāw of «يُنْصَرُون», i.e. "none will be protected from the torment except whom Allah has shown mercy."

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {كالمهل}: it may be a second khabar, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is like molten brass (al-muhl)." It is not permitted to be a ḥāl from «طعام الأثيم». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "because there is then no operator." There is something to consider here, because it is permissible for it to be a ḥāl, with the operator in it being the sense of comparison, as in your saying "Zayd is your brother, courageous."
الأَثيم is an intensive adjective. One also says الأَثُوم, like الصَّبور and الشَّكور. As for المُهْل: it is said to be the dregs of oil. It is said to be the sediment of tar. It is said to be what is melted of gold or silver. And it is said to be what is melted of them and of everything similar among the malleable metals, such as iron, copper and lead. المَهْل with fatḥa means calm and gentleness. From it comes {فَمَهِّلِ الكافرين} [al-Ṭāriq: 17]. al-Ḥasan read «كالمَهْل» with fatḥa on the mīm only, which is a dialectal form of المُهْل with ḍamma.
His saying: «يَغْلي»: Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read it with yāʾ (below). The agent is a pronoun referring back to the food (ṭaʿām). Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to refer to the zaqqūm. It is said it refers to the muhl itself, and «يَغْلي» is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition-phrase, i.e. "resembling the muhl, boiling." It may be a ḥāl from the muhl itself. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it boils," meaning the zaqqūm or the food. The rest read «تَغْلي» with tāʾ (above), the agent being a pronoun for the tree; the clause is then a second khabar, or a ḥāl according to one opinion, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it boils."

semin-durr:46-46.t: His saying: {كَغَلْيِ الحميم}: an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl from its pronoun, i.e. "it boils a boiling like the boiling of scalding water," or "it boils it, resembling the boiling of scalding water."

semin-durr:47-47.t: His saying: {فاعتلوه}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read «اعْتُلوه» with ḍamma on the ʿayn. The others read it with kasra. They are two dialectal forms in the imperfect of عَتَله, meaning to drag him with harshness and coarseness, like عَرَش يَعْرِش and يَعْرُش. And العُتُلّ means the harsh, coarse one.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {إِنَّكَ أَنتَ}: al-Kisāʾī read it with fatḥa in the sense of cause, i.e. "because you." It is also said that the implied form is: "Taste the torment of (the fact) that you are the mighty one." The others read it with kasra, as resumptive conveying the cause, so the two readings converge in meaning. This speech is by way of mockery, which is more infuriating to the one mocked. Similar is the saying of Jarīr to a poet who called himself "the flower of Yemen":
4020 - ألَمْ يَكُنْ في وُسُومٍ قد وَسَمْتُ بها ... مَنْ كان موعظةً يا زهرةَ اليَمَنِ
(Was there not, in the brands I have branded with, a warning for whoever needed one, O flower of Yemen?)
That poet had said:
4021 - أبْلِغْ كُلَيْباً وأَبْلِغْ عَنْك شاعرَها ... أنِّي الأَغَرُّ وأنِّي زهرةُ اليمنِ
(Convey to Kulayb, and convey on your behalf to its poet, that I am the radiant one and I am the flower of Yemen.)

semin-durr:52-52.t: His saying: {فِي جَنَّاتٍ}: / it may be a badal for His saying «في مَقام» with repetition of the operator, or it may be a second khabar.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
