His saying: {يَلْبَسُونَ}: it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in the preposition-phrase, or the khabar of «إنَّ» with the preposition-phrase attached to it, or resumptive.
His saying: «مُتقابلين»: a ḥāl from the agent of «يَلْبَسون». The explanation of these words, السُّنْدس, الإِستبرق and المقام, has already been given.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: there are two aspects to this kāf. The first: accusative, as an adjective of a maṣdar, i.e. "We do to the God-fearing a deed like that," i.e. like that deed. The second: nominative, as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is thus." Abū l-Baqāʾ implied before it a circumstantial clause, saying: "its implied form is: we did that, and the matter is thus"; there is no need for this. One stops at «كذلك» and begins with His saying «وزَوَّجْناهم».
His saying: «بِحُوْرٍ عِيْنٍ»: the majority read «حور» with tanwīn, described by «عِيْن». ʿIkrima did not give it tanwīn; he annexed them, because they divide into wide-eyed (ʿīn) and not wide-eyed. The explanation of الحُور العين has already been given.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying: {يَدْعُونَ}: a ḥāl from the object of «زَوَّجْناهم», and its object is omitted, i.e. "they call the servants for every fruit."
His saying: «آمِنين»: it may be a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the agent of «يَدْعُون», in which case it is a nested ḥāl.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {لاَ يَذُوقُونَ}: it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «آمِنين», or a third or second ḥāl from the object of «زَوَّجْناهم», with «آمنين» a ḥāl from the agent of «يَدْعُون» as stated earlier, or an adjective of «آمِنين», or resumptive. ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «لا يُذاقون» in the passive.
His saying: {إِلاَّ الموتة الأولى}: there are several aspects. The first: it is a disconnected exception, i.e. "but they have already tasted the first death." The second: it is connected, and they interpreted it thus: the believer at his death in this world is in the position of being in Paradise, because of seeing what he will be given of it, or because of his certainty of its bliss. The third: «إلاَّ» is in the sense of "other than" (siwā); al-Ṭabarī reported this and judged it weak. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "His judging it weak is not correct; rather its being in the sense of siwā is sound and coherent." The fourth: «إلاَّ» is in the sense of "after" (baʿd). al-Ṭabarī preferred it, and the majority rejected it, because «إلاَّ» in the sense of "after" is not established. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is the first death, which is tasted before entering Paradise, excepted from the death whose tasting is negated? I say: it was intended to say 'they will not taste death there at all,' so He put His saying {إِلاَّ الموتة الأولى} in the place of that; for tasting the past death in the future is impossible, so it is of the type of suspension upon the impossible: as if it were said, 'if the first death could be tasted in the future, then they will taste it in Paradise.'" I say: among the scholars of rhetoric this is called negating a thing by means of its proof. Similar is the saying of al-Nābigha:
4022 - لا عَيْبَ فيهم غيرَ أنَّ سيوفَهُمْ ... بهنَّ فُلولٌ مِنْ قِراعِ الكتائبِ
(There is no fault in them, except that their swords have nicks from striking the battalions.)
He means: if anyone counts the nicks of swords from striking battalions a fault, then this is their fault; but counting it among faults is impossible, so fault is negated from them by the proof of suspending the matter upon an impossibility. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, after what I earlier related from al-Ṭabarī: "So He made clear that He negated tasting death from them, and that nothing reaches them of it beyond what preceded in this world." He means that it is speech to be taken according to its meaning.
His saying: «ووَقاهم»: the majority read it lightened. Abū Ḥaywa read «ووقَّاهم» with shadda for intensification, and it is not for transitivity, since it already governs two objects before that.

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {فَضْلاً}: this is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and that is what Makkī meant when he said: "a maṣdar that «يَدْعُون» operates on." It is said that the operator in it is «ووَقاهم»; it is said, «آمِنين»; but this only appears sound if it is an object of purpose. It is also possible that it is a maṣdar, because «يَدْعُون» and what follows are of the type of bestowing favour, so it is a maṣdar concurring with its operator in meaning. Abū l-Baqāʾ made it accusative through an implied verb, i.e. "We bestowed that as a favour," i.e. as bestowal.

semin-durr:58-58.t: His saying: {يَسَّرْنَاهُ}: i.e. the Qur'an, in your tongue, i.e. in your language. The bāʾ is for accompaniment./

semin-durr:59-59.t: His saying: {فارتقب إِنَّهُمْ مُّرْتَقِبُونَ}: the two objects of "watching" (irtiqāb) are omitted, i.e. "so watch for victory from your Lord; they are watching, with regard to you, what they wish for of reversals and treacheries, but that will never harm you."

semin-durr:3-3.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: {إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَاهُ}: it may be the answer to the oath, or it may be parenthetical, the answer being His saying {إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ}, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya preferred it. It was also said: «إنَّا كُنَّا» is resumptive, or a second answer without a conjunction.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ}: it may be resumptive, or an adjective of «ليلة» with what is between them parenthetical. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: 'إنَّا كُنَّا مُنْذِرين' and 'فيها يُفْرَقُ', what is the position of these two sentences? I say: they are two resumptive sentences, folded together (malfūfatān), by which he explained the answer of the oath, which is «أَنْزَلْناه», as if it were said: 'We sent it down because it is in Our nature to warn and caution, and Our sending it down in this night in particular was because the sending down of the Qur'an is among the wise matters, and this night is the one in which every wise matter is distinguished.'" I say: this is among the fine points of this man.

Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj and al-Aʿmash read «يَفْرُقُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the rā', and «كلَّ» accusative, i.e. "Allah distinguishes every matter". Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «نَفْرِقُ» with the nūn of majesty, «كلَّ» accusative, so al-Zamakhsharī reported; and al-Ahwāzī reported from him «يَفْرِق» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the rā', «كلَّ» accusative, «حكيمٌ» nominative as the agent of «يَفْرِق». From al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash also: «يُفَرَّقُ» like the majority, except with doubling.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {أَمْراً}: it has twelve analyses. The first: it is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «أَنْزَلْناه». The second: it is a ḥāl from its object, i.e. "We sent it down commanding", or "commanded". The third: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and its accusative-assigner is either «أَنْزَلْناه», or «مُنْذرِين», or «يُفْرَقُ». The fourth: that it is a maṣdar from the meaning of «يُفْرَق», i.e. "distinguishing". The fifth: that it is a maṣdar of an omitted «أَمَرْنا». The sixth: that «يُفْرَقُ» has the sense of «يَأْمُر». The difference between this and what preceded: here you return the governing agent to the maṣdar, and in what preceded, the reverse. The seventh: that it is a ḥāl from «كُلُّ». The eighth: that it is a ḥāl from «أَمْرٍ», and that is permitted because it is described. Except that in it are two things: the coming of the ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi in cases other than those mentioned; and second, that it is confirmatory. The ninth: that it is a maṣdar of «أَنْزَل», i.e. "We sent it down a sending down". Al-Akhfash said this. The tenth: that it is a maṣdar, but with the governing agent interpreted in its meaning, i.e. "We commanded it a command by reason of the sending down", as they said that in the two analyses «فيها يُفْرَقُ فَرْقاً» or «يَنْزِل إنزالاً». The eleventh: that it is accusative as specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). Al-Zamakhsharī said this, and he does not mean by it the technical ikhtiṣāṣ, since that is not indefinite. The twelfth: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «حكيم». The thirteenth: that it is accusative as a direct object of «مُنْذِرين», like His saying {لِّيُنْذِرَ بَأْساً شَدِيداً} [al-Kahf: 2], with the first object omitted, i.e. "warning the people of a command". [Translator's note: the source says "twelve" but lists thirteen.] The sum is that its accusative returns to four things: the direct object, the object of purpose, the maṣdar, and the ḥāl; the multiplicity is only according to the positions, and you have known them from what I have set before you.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «أَمْرٌ» nominative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It strengthens the accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ."

His saying: «مِنْ عِنْدِنا»: it may be attached to «يُفْرَقُ», i.e. "from Our side", and it is for the beginning of the range figuratively. It may also be an adjective of «أَمْراً».

His saying: {إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ}: a third answer, or resumptive, or a badal from His saying {إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ}.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {رَحْمَةً}: it has five analyses. [The first:] a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. Its governing agent is either «أَنْزَلْناه», or «أَمْراً», or «يُفْرَقُ», or «مُنْذِرين». The second: a maṣdar of an implied verb, i.e. "We showed mercy, a mercy". The third: an object of «مُرْسِلين». The fourth: a ḥāl from the pronoun of «مُرْسِلين», i.e. "possessors of mercy". The fifth: that it is a badal from «أَمْراً», so what preceded applies to it, and the analyses of it become many.

«مِنْ رَبِّك» is attached to «رَحْمة», or to an omitted element as an adjective. In «مِنْ ربِّك» there is a shift (iltifāt) from the first person to the third; had it followed the pattern of what preceded, He would have said: "a mercy from Us".

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {رَبِّ السماوات}: the Kufans read «رَبّ» genitive, and the others nominative. The genitive is as a badal, or explication (bayān), or adjective. The nominative is on an implied mubtadaʾ, or on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَآئِكُمُ}: the majority read it nominative as a badal, explication or adjective of «ربُّ السماوات» for those who read it nominative, or on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}, or a khabar after a khabar of His saying {إِنَّهُ هُوَ السميع}, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ according to all, I mean the readers of the genitive and the nominative, or the agent of His saying «يُميت». In «يُحْيي» there is a pronoun that refers back to what precedes, i.e. "He gives life", that is, the Lord of the heavens, "and He causes death", so the overt noun is put where the pronoun belongs. It may be that «يُحيي ويُميت» is an instance of conflict (tanāzuʿ). The nominative may be attributed to the first or the second, like «يَقُوم ويَقْعد زيد», and this is what Abū l-Baqāʾ meant by his saying: "or on the condition of explanation".

Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Abū Ḥaywa and al-Ḥasan read it genitive / as a badal, explication or adjective of «رب السماوات», and this requires them to read «رَبِّ السماوات» genitive. Al-Anṭākī read it accusative as praise.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ تَأْتِي}: accusative by «ارْتَقِبْ» as an adverbial. The object is omitted, i.e. "await the promise of Allah on that day". It may also be that it is itself the object awaited.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَارْتَقِبْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِي السَّمَاءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُبِينٍ (١٠)).
His saying (يَوْمَ تَأْتِي): it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of فَارْتَقِبْ.

ukberi-tibyan:11-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَغْشَى النَّاسَ هَذَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (١١) رَبَّنَا اكْشِفْ عَنَّا الْعَذَابَ إِنَّا مُؤْمِنُونَ (١٢) أَنَّى لَهُمُ الذِّكْرَى وَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مُبِينٌ (١٣)).
His saying (هَذَا عَذَابٌ): i.e. it is said: "this…". And (الذِّكْرَى) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لَهُمْ» is the khabar (predicate). And (أَنَّى) is an adverb governed by [the notion of] settledness (al-istiqrār).
It is also possible that «أَنَّى» is the khabar and «لَهُمْ» is for clarification (tabyīn).
(وَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:15-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا كَاشِفُوا الْعَذَابِ قَلِيلًا إِنَّكُمْ عَائِدُونَ (١٥) يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ الْبَطْشَةَ الْكُبْرَى إِنَّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ (١٦)).
And (قَلِيلًا): i.e. "for a little time", or "a little removal". And (يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ): it is said: it is a badal (substitute) of [يَوْمَ] تَأْتِي. It is also said: it is an adverb of time for عَائِدُونَ. It is also said: the implied wording is "remember". It is also said: it is an adverb of time for what the speech indicates, i.e. "We shall take vengeance on the day We strike".
It is also read «نُبْطِشُ», with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the ṭāʾ; one says أَبْطَشْتُهُ when you enable him to strike; i.e. "We shall enable the angels to strike".

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَنْ أَدُّوا إِلَيَّ عِبَادَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ (١٨)).
His saying (عِبَادَ اللَّهِ): i.e. "O servants of Allah", i.e. render to me what is due from you.
It is also said: it is the object of أَدُّوا, i.e. "leave me free with those who have believed in me".

ukberi-tibyan:20-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ (٢٠) وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا لِي فَاعْتَزِلُونِ (٢١) فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ قَوْمٌ مُجْرِمُونَ (٢٢)).
(وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ): resumptive. And (أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ): i.e. "from your stoning me" (مِنْ أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ).
And (أَنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ) is accusative by «دَعَا».
It is also read with kasra (إِنَّ), because دَعَا has the sense of قَالَ ("said").

ukberi-tibyan:24-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاتْرُكِ الْبَحْرَ رَهْوًا إِنَّهُمْ جُنْدٌ مُغْرَقُونَ (٢٤) كَمْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ (٢٥) وَزُرُوعٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ (٢٦) وَنَعْمَةٍ كَانُوا فِيهَا فَاكِهِينَ (٢٧) كَذَلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْنَاهَا قَوْمًا آخَرِينَ (٢٨)).
And (رَهْوًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْبَحْرَ, i.e. "still".
It is also said: it is a second object, i.e. "make it [so]".
And (كَمْ) is accusative by «تَرَكُوا». And (كَذَلِكَ): i.e. "the matter is thus". It is also said: the implied wording is "a leaving like that".

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُبَارَكَةٍ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنْذِرِينَ (٣)).
His saying (إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ): it is the answer to the oath. And «إِنَّا كُنَّا» is resumptive.
It is also said: it is another answer, without a conjunction.

ukberi-tibyan:30-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ نَجَّيْنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ الْمُهِينِ (٣٠) مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَالِيًا مِنَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ (٣١) وَلَقَدِ اخْتَرْنَاهُمْ عَلَى عِلْمٍ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ (٣٢)).
His saying (مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ): it is a badal (substitute) of «الْعَذَابِ» with the preposition repeated, i.e. "from the punishment of Pharaoh"; it may also be that Pharaoh himself is made a punishment.
And (مِنَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ) is a further khabar (predicate), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «عَالِيًا».
And (عَلَى عِلْمٍ) is a ḥāl of the agent pronoun, i.e. "We chose them, knowing them"; and «عَلَى» [in عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ] is attached (mutaʿalliq) to اخْتَرْنَا.

ukberi-tibyan:37-38.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا مُجْرِمِينَ (٣٧) وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَاعِبِينَ (٣٨)).
His saying (وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): it may be conjoined to «قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ», so that «أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ» is resumptive, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in the ṣila (relative clause). It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ; or accusative by an omitted verb. And (لَاعِبِينَ) is a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ (٤)).
His saying (فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ): it is resumptive.
It is also said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of لَيْلَةٍ, and «إِنَّا...» is parenthetical between the two.

ukberi-tibyan:40-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ مِيقَاتُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ (٤٠) يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَنْ مَوْلًى شَيْئًا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ (٤١)).
And (أَجْمَعِينَ) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the genitive pronoun. (يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِي): it may be a badal (substitute) of (يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ); or a naʿt (adjective) of «مِيقَاتُهُمْ», but made indeclinable (mabnī); or an adverb of time for what الْفَصْلِ indicates, i.e. "He will judge between them on the day when … will not avail". It is not attached to الْفَصْلِ itself, because a predicate has been given about it.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ اللَّهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ (٤١)) [Translator's note: so in the text; this is verse ٤٢].
His saying (إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ): it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), i.e. "whomever Allah has mercy on by accepting intercession for him".
It may also be a badal (substitute) of the object of يَنْصُرُونَ, i.e. "they will not help anyone except whom Allah has mercy on".

ukberi-tibyan:45-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَالْمُهْلِ يَغْلِي فِي الْبُطُونِ (٤٥) كَغَلْيِ الْحَمِيمِ (٤٦) خُذُوهُ فَاعْتِلُوهُ إِلَى سَوَاءِ الْجَحِيمِ (٤٧)).
His saying (يَغْلِي): it is read with yāʾ. It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in the kāf, i.e. "it resembles molten metal, boiling". It is also said: it is a ḥāl of الْمُهْلِ. It is also said: the implied wording is "it boils", i.e. the Zaqqūm or the food.
As for the kāf, it may be a second khabar (predicate), or on the implied wording "it is like molten metal". It cannot be a ḥāl of «طَعَامُ», because there would then be nothing to govern it.
It is also read with tāʾ (تَغْلِي), i.e. the tree; and the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "a boiling like the boiling of scalding water".
(فَاعْتِلُوهُ): with kasra on the tāʾ and with ḍamma on it — two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:49-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْكَرِيمُ (٤٩) إِنَّ هَذَا مَا كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَمْتَرُونَ (٥٠) إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ (٥١) فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ (٥٢) يَلْبَسُونَ مِنْ سُنْدُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ مُتَقَابِلِينَ (٥٣) كَذَلِكَ وَزَوَّجْنَاهُمْ بِحُورٍ عِينٍ (٥٤) يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِكُلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ آمِنِينَ (٥٥) لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الْمَوْتَ إِلَّا الْمَوْتَةَ الْأُولَى وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ (٥٦) فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكَ ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ (٥٧)).
His saying (ذُقْ إِنَّكَ): «إِنَّكَ» is read with kasra, as resumptive, and it is mockery of him; it is also said [it means]: "you are the mighty, the noble, in the eyes of your people". It is also read with fatḥa (أَنَّكَ), i.e. "taste the punishment of your being…".
And (مَقَامٍ), with fatḥa and with ḍamma (مُقَامٍ), has been mentioned in al-Aḥzāb. And (فِي جَنَّاتٍ) is a badal (substitute) of «مَقَامٍ» with the preposition repeated.
As for «يَلْبَسُونَ», it may be the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ, so that «فِي» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it; or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in the preposition phrase; or resumptive. And (كَذَلِكَ): i.e. "Our doing is thus", or "the matter is thus".
And (يَدْعُونَ) is a ḥāl of the agent in زَوَّجْنَا [Translator's note: so in the text; the agent of زَوَّجْنَا is "We", and the intended reference is evidently the object pronoun هُمْ]. And (لَا يَذُوقُونَ) is another ḥāl, of the pronoun in يَدْعُونَ or of the pronoun in آمِنِينَ; or another ḥāl after آمِنِينَ; or a naʿt (adjective) of آمِنِينَ. His saying (إِلَّا الْمَوْتَةَ الْأُولَى): it is said that the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), i.e. "they died the death".
It is also said: it is connected (muttaṣil), because the believer at his death in this world is as if in his station in the Garden, since he sees what he is given of it, or what he becomes certain of of its bliss. It is also said: «إِلَّا» has the sense of "after". It is also said: it has the sense of "other than". And (فَضْلًا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "We bestowed that as a favour". And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْرًا مِنْ عِنْدِنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ (٥)).
His saying (أَمْرًا): there are several views on its accusative. The first: it is the object of مُنْذِرِينَ, like His saying (لِيُنْذِرَ بَأْسًا شَدِيدًا). The second: it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), governed by «أَنْزَلْنَاهُ» or «مُنْذِرِينَ» or «يُفْرَقُ». The third: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «حَكِيمٍ», or of «أَمْرٍ» because it has been qualified, or of كُلُّ, or of the hāʾ in أَنْزَلْنَاهُ. The fourth: that it is in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a separating from Us". The fifth: that it is a maṣdar, i.e. "We commanded a commanding", indicated by the commands the Book contains. The sixth: that it is a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ in «أَنْزَلْنَاهُ».
As for (مِنْ عِنْدِنَا), it may be a naʿt (adjective) of أَمْرًا, or attached (mutaʿalliq) to يُفْرَقُ.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ (٦)).
His saying (رَحْمَةً): there are several views on it. The first: that it is the object of «مُرْسِلِينَ», what is meant by it being the Prophet ﷺ.
The second: that it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). The third: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "We had mercy on you with a mercy".
The fourth: that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «مُرْسِلِينَ»; and it is best that the implied wording be "possessed of mercy".

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ (٧)).
His saying (رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ): in the nominative (رَبُّ) on the implied wording "He is the Lord"; or as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ»; or as a khabar after a khabar. And in the genitive as a badal (substitute) of «رَبِّكَ».

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (٨)).
His saying (رَبُّكُمْ): i.e. "He is your Lord". It may also be a further khabar (predicate), or the fāʿil (agent) of «يُمِيتُ», with a pronoun in «يُحْيِي» referring to what precedes it, or on the condition of explanation (ʿalā sharīṭat al-tafsīr) [i.e. the pronoun anticipating the noun that follows].

zajjaj:10-10.t:
And His saying: ﴿فارْتَقِبْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِي السَّماءُ بِدُخانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ ﴿يَغْشى النّاسَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 11]: "فارْتَقِبْ" means: so wait. In most of the exegesis, the smoke has already passed: that was when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against Muḍar, saying: «"O Allah, make Your tread heavy upon Muḍar, and make it years upon them like the years of Joseph,"» that is, make their years of drought like the years of Joseph. The Arabs also call drought "اَلسَّنَةَ" (the year), so the meaning would be: "Make it droughts upon them." So the rain was withheld, the land became barren, and between the sky and the earth there was something like smoke.
And His saying: ﴿هَذا عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 11]: the meaning is: the people upon whom the drought descends say: "This is a painful punishment"; and likewise His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا اكْشِفْ عَنّا العَذابَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 12].

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا كاشِفُو العَذابِ قَلِيلا إنَّكم عائِدُونَ﴾: "أنَّكم عائِدُونَ" is also permissible; whoever reads "أنَّكم عائِدُونَ", that is the [proper] way. The meaning is that He informs them that they will not take admonition, and that when the hateful thing is removed from them they will return to their transgression.
«[Translator's note: as printed, the source calls the fatḥa reading "أنَّكم" "the proper way" (al-wajh), though the canonical text has "إنَّكم" with kasra; the source may intend the kasra reading here.]»

zajjaj:16-16.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ البَطْشَةَ الكُبْرى إنّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾: "يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ" and "نَبْطُشُ" ﴿إنّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾: this is like "عَكَفَ، يَعْكُفُ، ويَعْكِفُ" and "عَرَشَ، يَعْرِشُ، ويَعْرُشُ", and this is frequent in the language. It has been said that the greatest seizure is the day of Badr. "يَوْمَ" cannot be accusative by His saying "مُنْتَقِمُونَ", because what comes after "إنّا" cannot govern what precedes it; rather, it is accusative by [an implied] "واذْكُرْ يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ البَطْشَةَ الكُبْرى" (and remember the day We seize with the greatest seizure).

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنّا قَبْلَهم قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾, up to His saying: ﴿أنْ أدُّوا إلَيَّ عِبادَ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 18]. The meaning of "أنْ أدُّوا إلَيَّ عِبادَ اللَّهِ" is: hand over to me the servants of Allah, meaning the Children of Israel, as He said: ﴿فَأرْسِلْ مَعَنا بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ ولا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 47], that is, release them from your torment. It is also permissible that "عِبادَ اللَّهِ" be accusative as a vocative (nidāʾ), so the meaning would be: "Render to me what Allah has commanded you, O servants of Allah."

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿وَأنْ لا تَعْلُوا عَلى اللَّهِ إنِّي آتِيكم بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾: that is, with a clear, evident proof, showing that I am a prophet.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
Sūrat al-Dukhān
Meccan
﷽
It has come in the exegesis: Whoever recites Sūrat "al-Dukhān" on the eve of Friday, affirming and believing, Allah will forgive him. We have explained the meaning of "حـم" earlier.
And His saying: ﴿والكِتابِ المُبِينِ﴾ is an oath.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَإنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي ورَبِّكم أنْ تَرْجُمُونِ﴾: that is, lest you kill me.
And His saying: ﴿وَإنْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا لِي فاعْتَزِلُونِ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 21]: that is, if you do not believe me, then be neither against me nor with me.

zajjaj:22-22.t: ﴿فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أنَّ هَؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ مُجْرِمُونَ﴾: Whoever reads "إنَّ" with kasra, the meaning is: "He said: These are…", and "إنَّ" after [a verb of] saying is with kasra. The fatḥa is permissible with the meaning "فَدَعا رَبَّهُ بِأنَّ هَؤُلاءِ" (so he called upon his Lord [saying] that these…).

zajjaj:24-24.t: And His saying: ﴿واتْرُكِ البَحْرَ رَهْوًا﴾: It has come in the exegesis: "dry," as He said: ﴿فاضْرِبْ لَهم طَرِيقًا في البَحْرِ يَبَسًا﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 77]. The lexicographers said: "رَهْوًا" means still.

zajjaj:25-25.t: And His saying: ﴿كَمْ تَرَكُوا مِن جَنّاتٍ وعُيُونٍ﴾ ﴿وَزُرُوعٍ ومَقامٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 26]: It has come in the exegesis that the noble place (al-maqām al-karīm) here means the pulpits; and it has come concerning "مَقامٍ كَرِيمٍ": that is, in fine dwellings.

zajjaj:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ وأوْرَثْناها قَوْمًا آخَرِينَ﴾: the meaning is "the matter is thus"; the position of "كَذَلِكَ" is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied (muḍmar) mubtadaʾ (subject).

zajjaj:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَما بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّماءُ والأرْضُ﴾: because they died as disbelievers. When the believers die, the heaven and the earth weep for them: of the earth, the believer's place of prayer weeps for him, that is, the place where he prayed; and of the heaven, the place where his deeds ascend and where his provision descends. It has come in the exegesis that the earth weeps for the believer for forty mornings.
And His saying: ﴿وَما كانُوا مُنْظَرِينَ﴾: that is, they were not granted a delay of the punishment. ﴿وَلَقَدِ اخْتَرْناهم عَلى عِلْمٍ عَلى العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 32]: that is, over the peoples of their age.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْناهُ في لَيْلَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ﴾: It has come in the exegesis that it is the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr). Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْناهُ في لَيْلَةِ القَدْرِ﴾ [al-Qadr: 1]. The exegetes said: "في لَيْلَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ" is the Night of Decree; it was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, then sent down to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ piece by piece.

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ هَؤُلاءِ لَيَقُولُونَ﴾ ﴿إنْ هي إلا مَوْتَتُنا الأُولى وما نَحْنُ بِمُنْشَرِينَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 35]: this was said by the disbelievers of Quraysh. The meaning of "إنْ هي" is "it is not (mā hiya)," and the meaning of "بِمُنْشَرِينَ" is "to be resurrected." One says "أنْشَرَ اللَّهُ المَوْتى" (Allah raised the dead) and "نُشِرُوا هم" (they were raised).

zajjaj:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أهم خَيْرٌ أمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ﴾: It has come in the exegesis that Tubbaʿ was a believer and that his people were disbelievers. And it has come that he looked at an inscription on two graves in the region of Ḥimyar: on the grave of one of them, "This is the grave of Raḍwā," and on the other, "This is the grave of Ḥubbā," the two daughters of Tubbaʿ, who associated nothing with Allah.
«[Translator's note: the subject of "نَظَرَ" (he looked) is not named in the source; it may be an unnamed narrator rather than Tubbaʿ.]»

zajjaj:39-39.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ما خَلَقْناهُما إلا بِالحَقِّ﴾: by it are meant the heavens and the earth; that is, only for the establishment of the truth.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيها يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, on the Night of Decree, apportions every matter in which there is wisdom, of the provisions of the servants, their terms of life, and all their affairs, which are appointed until the Night of Decree that falls in the following year.

zajjaj:40-40.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ مِيقاتُهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾: "مِيقاتَهم", with the tāʾ in the accusative, is also permissible, but I do not know that it has been read so, so do not ever read it so. Whoever reads "مِيقاتُهم" in the nominative makes "يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ" the noun (ism) of "إنَّ" and makes "مِيقاتُهم" the khabar (predicate). Whoever makes "مِيقاتَهم" accusative makes it the noun of "إنَّ" and makes "يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ" accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), the meaning being: "Their appointed time is on the Day of Decision."

zajjaj:41-41.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ لا يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَنْ مَوْلًى شَيْئًا﴾: no ally will avail his ally anything, nor a father his child, nor a child his father.

zajjaj:43-43.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ شَجَرَتَ الزَّقُّومِ﴾ ﴿طَعامُ الأثِيمِ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 44]: by it [the sinner] is meant here Abū Jahl ibn Hishām. And "اَلْمُهْلُ" is the dregs of oil; and it is also said: "اَلْمُهْلُ" is whatever is molten of silver, copper and the like.

zajjaj:47-47.t: And His saying: ﴿خُذُوهُ فاعْتِلُوهُ﴾: It is also read "فاعْتُلُوهُ" — with ḍamma on the tāʾ, and with kasra. The meaning is: "O angels, seize him and drag him." "اَلْعَتْلُ" is that one is seized and taken off with harshness and violence. ﴿إلى سَواءِ الجَحِيمِ﴾: to the middle of Hellfire.

zajjaj:49-49.t: And His saying: ﴿ذُقْ إنَّكَ أنْتَ العَزِيزُ الكَرِيمُ﴾: All the people [readers] have the kasra in "إنَّكَ" except al-Kisāʾī alone, who read "ذُقْ أنَّكَ أنْتَ", that is: because you said, "You are indeed the mighty, the noble." That is because he [Abū Jahl] used to say: "I am the mightiest and best-defended of the people of this valley." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: "Taste this punishment; you are the one who said: I am the mighty, the noble."

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْرًا مِن عِنْدِنا﴾.
And His saying: ﴿رَحْمَةً مِن رَبِّكَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 6]: both are accusative. Al-Akhfash said: as ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "We sent it down, commanding a command and being merciful with mercy." It is also possible that it is accusative by "يُفْرَقُ", in the position of "يَفْرُقُ فَرْقًا" (a mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object), because "أمْرًا" has the meaning of "فَرْقًا", since the meaning is "a command is enjoined in it." And it is possible that "رَحْمَةً مِن رَبِّكَ" is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), that is: "We sent it down as a mercy," that is, "for the sake of mercy."

zajjaj:51-51.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُتَّقِينَ في مَقامٍ أمِينٍ﴾: that is, in it they are safe from changes of fortune.

zajjaj:53-53.t: And His saying: ﴿يَلْبَسُونَ مِن سُنْدُسٍ وإسْتَبْرَقٍ مُتَقابِلِينَ﴾: It has been said: "اَلْإسْتَبْرَقُ" is thick brocade, and "اَلسُّنْدُسُ" is silk. It was called "إسْتَبْرَقٌ" — and Allah knows best — only because of the intensity of its sheen (barīq).

zajjaj:56-56.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها المَوْتَ إلا المَوْتَةَ الأُولى﴾: the meaning is: they will not taste death in it at all, apart from the first death which they tasted in this world. The two [verses] are as He said: ﴿وَلا تَنْكِحُوا ما نَكَحَ آباؤُكم مِنَ النِّساءِ إلا ما قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 22].

zajjaj:57-57.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَضْلا مِن رَبِّكَ﴾: "فَضْلٌ مِن رَبِّكَ" is also permissible, but it must not be read so, because it contradicts the codex. The accusative is on the meaning of His saying ﴿يَدْعُونَ فِيها بِكُلِّ فاكِهَةٍ آمِنِينَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 55], and on the meaning of ﴿إنَّ المُتَّقِينَ في مَقامٍ أمِينٍ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 51], and that is by a bounty from Allah; so the meaning is: "Allah did that for them as a bounty from Him and a favour from Him."

zajjaj:59-59.t: And His saying: ﴿فارْتَقِبْ إنَّهم مُرْتَقِبُونَ﴾: its meaning is: "So wait; they too are waiting."

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿رَبِّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ وما بَيْنَهُما﴾: with the genitive and the nominative. The nominative is as a description (ṣifa), and the genitive is on [the basis of] His saying "مِن رَبِّكَ رَبِّ السَّماواتِ" (from your Lord, the Lord of the heavens). Whoever reads the nominative, it is on [the basis of] His saying: "إنَّهُ هو السَّمِيعُ العَلِيمُ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ"; or, if you wish, as resumptive (istiʾnāf), with the meaning: "He is the Lord of the heavens."

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿لا إلَهَ إلا هو يُحْيِي ويُمِيتُ رَبُّكم ورَبُّ آبائِكُمُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾: It is also read "رَبِّكم ورَبِّ آبائِكُمُ الأوَّلِينَ". The genitive is with the meaning "رَحْمَةً مِن رَبِّكَ رَبِّكم ورَبِّ آبائِكُمُ الأوَّلِينَ" (a mercy from your Lord, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers).
